records.application_period: Online applications are received twice each year. The application link only becomes active one month prior to the submission deadline, i.e. from 1 March and 1 September. September applications result in a three-month visit during April-June of the following year; March applications result in a three-month visit during September-November of the same year.
records.description: The Visiting PhD Fellowship gives registered doctoral students a three-month placement at UNU-WIDER in Helsinki to use the institute's resources and facilities for their PhD dissertation or thesis research on developing economies. Fellows prepare one or more research papers and present a seminar on their findings, and may have the opportunity to publish in the WIDER Working Paper Series. UNU-WIDER provides a return travel grant, medical insurance for the stay, and a monthly stipend of EUR 2,100 to cover living expenses during the fellowship period in Helsinki.
records.best_fit: Doctoral students already enrolled in a PhD programme, ideally at a later stage of their doctorate, with a demonstrable ability to conduct research on developing economies and strong quantitative and/or qualitative analytical skills. Early-career, female and developing-country researchers are particularly encouraged to apply.
records.funding_period: Monthly, for the period of stay in Helsinki
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be enrolled in a PhD programme and have shown ability to conduct research on developing economies, be fluent in written and oral English and possess good quantitative and/or qualitative analytical skills.

official_details.description: The Visiting PhD Fellowship Programme gives registered doctoral students the opportunity to utilize the resources and facilities at UNU-WIDER for their PhD dissertation or thesis research on developing economies, and to work with the institute's researchers in areas of mutual interest. Visiting PhD fellows typically spend three consecutive months at UNU-WIDER before returning to their home institution. During their time in Helsinki, fellows prepare one or more research papers and present a seminar on their research findings. They may also have the opportunity to publish their research in the WIDER Working Paper Series. The programme was previously known as the PhD Internship Programme.

records.name: SA-TIED Request for Research Proposals: Public revenue mobilization; Poverty, inequality, and labour markets
records.official_source: United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER), with the National Treasury of South Africa
records.region: South Africa (South Africa-based and international researchers)
records.duration: Milestone-driven: first draft of papers due 8 June 2027 and final draft due 8 September 2027, with a work-in-progress workshop in June or July 2027
records.deadline: Closing date: 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2). Submit questions by 8 October 2026.
records.application_period: Launched 17 September 2026; proposals close 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC+2. Questions on the proposal process were due by 8 October 2026, with queries and responses published on the RfRP announcement page and updated on a rolling basis.
records.description: UNU-WIDER and the South African National Treasury invite proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme for research using South African tax administrative data. Accepted proposals are paid a research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 on delivery of a working paper of 10,000 words or fewer, and the resulting papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series. This is research funding rather than a degree scholarship: the deliverable is a policy paper, and the honorarium is expected to cover all expenses of the research.
records.best_fit: Qualified individual researchers, groups and non-profit organisations able to conduct high-quality economic research on public revenue mobilization, poverty, inequality and labour markets, using South African tax administrative data. Applications from women and South African researchers are particularly encouraged, and preference is given to early-career researchers and scholars from the Global South.
records.eligibility_summary: Proposals are welcome from individuals, groups of individuals and non-profit organisations, using South Africa-based and international researchers, with South African researchers, women, and early-career and Global South scholars particularly encouraged.
eligibility: Proposals from individuals, groups of individuals, and non-profit organizations are welcome
Calls for South Africa-based and international researchers to submit proposals
Research must be conducted primarily, but not exclusively, using South African tax administrative data
Papers must be written in English and limited to 10,000 words or fewer, inclusive of text, tables, figures, footnotes and references
Papers may use either theoretical or empirical approaches
Researchers requiring access to National Treasury tax administrative datasets will be subject to agreed restrictions to preserve confidentiality
coverage: Research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000, paid upon delivery of a working paper depending on the qualifications of the lead researcher and assessment of the proposal
A small travel stipend for researchers using the South African tax administrative data who live outside of Gauteng
benefits: Publication of the resulting paper under UNU-WIDER copyright as an SA-TIED research paper
Possible publication in the WIDER Working Paper Series
Opportunity to participate in at least one knowledge-sharing event
Engagement with the SA-TIED communications team to develop a knowledge mobilization output such as a video, social media product, infographic, brief or blog
Inclusion in a research team building capacity in South African institutions, with UNU-WIDER seeking participation from Historically Disadvantaged Institutions

Details such as address, gender, nationality and date of birth of all researchers involved must be entered on the form
The cover page, the proposal, and short CVs of five pages or less per researcher must be uploaded
The provided proposal template must be used for the proposal

Prepare the proposal using the provided template, observing the word limits
Select the correct online form: individual, group of individuals, or non-profit organization
Enter the contact details and the details of all researchers involved, including address, gender, nationality and date of birth

Submit the form before 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC+2
Send any questions on the proposal process to researchproposal3@wider.unu.edu by 8 October 2026
For successful proposals, sign a consultant contract or institutional contractual agreement with UNU-WIDER
records.selection_notes: Each proposal is reviewed for scientific merit and feasibility and selected on three criteria: relevance to the research project, strength of empirical and policy contributions, and qualifications and experience of the research team. Preference is given to applications from early-career and female scholars and researchers from South Africa. Only the final decision on whether the proposal is accepted is communicated; applicants must not expect feedback on their proposals. Funding decisions are targeted for 9 November 2026.
records.notes: Successful researchers or their institutions sign a consultant contract or institutional contractual agreement with UNU-WIDER under UNU conditions of service, and transfer copyright of the research produced to UNU-WIDER so that it can be licensed on full open access; if no further publication is expected, copyright can be transferred back to the authors. Any material published externally thereafter should carry due acknowledgement of UNU-WIDER as the original commissioning institute. Successful applicants may be asked to attend at least one knowledge-sharing event and a work-in-progress workshop of about 1-1.5 days.

official_details.description: The United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER), together with the National Treasury of South Africa, is requesting research proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme. The call invites South Africa-based and international researchers to submit proposals to conduct research primarily, but not exclusively, using the South African tax administrative data. Papers generated will be published as part of the workstreams on public revenue mobilisation for inclusive development and on poverty, inequality, and labour markets.
purpose: Investigate the determinants of revenue collection in South Africa and the effects of the tax structure on economic growth and inequality
Examine how people and firms respond to tax policy design and tax administration processes
Address inclusivity of South Africa's growth path and policy options to promote inclusive growth
Explore individual and structural constraints on self-employment and informal sector activity
Assess the Social Relief of Distress grant as a potential platform into productive livelihoods
Examine asset inequality, infrastructure as redistribution, and immigration in the South African labour market
Produce policy-relevant recommendations that can be taken forward in a further phase of work

records.name: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
records.official_source: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), National Security Education Program; administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE)
records.region: Overseas study outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand (preferred regions: Africa, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East). Applicants must be U.S. citizens enrolled at a U.S. institution.
records.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
records.deadline: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027 - both 5pm Eastern time.
records.application_period: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycle is open as of 2026-10-01. National deadlines are January 20, 2027 (Fellowships) and January 27, 2027 (Scholarships), 5pm Eastern time. Selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect.
records.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.
records.best_fit: U.S. citizens aged 18 or over who are matriculated at an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate degree programme, can commit 8-52 weeks to overseas study of a Boren-preferred language in a Boren-preferred region, and intend to pursue a federal national-security career.
records.eligibility_summary: U.S. citizens aged 18 or older, matriculated at an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate programme, proposing a continuous programme of at least 12 weeks (8 weeks for undergraduate STEM) of classroom language study in a country outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, and of which they are not a citizen.

records.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.
records.notes: Non-deferrable in practice: recipients must remain matriculated at their U.S. institution for the whole funded period and may not graduate until the award is complete, and overseas programmes must be approved by a Boren Program Advisor before travel. Not renewable as published - the award is a fixed one-time grant tier set by overseas duration, and requests to increase awards above the published maximums are contingent upon availability of funds. No return-home obligation is published; instead recipients must complete at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation, with preference given to a longer-term commitment. Internships conducted during a Boren-funded period may not be remunerated nor conducted with the U.S. or a foreign government, and Boren Fellows may not work as journalists while abroad, even freelance or unpaid. Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent upon availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.

official_details.description: The Boren Awards are a component of the National Security Education Program (NSEP) that funds the intensive study of language abroad by U.S. undergraduate and graduate students who commit to federal service. Boren Scholarships support undergraduates and Boren Fellowships support graduate students; both require a continuous period of overseas study with at least 15-20 weekly language contact hours. The award is a fixed grant tier determined by duration of overseas study ($8,000 / $12,500 / $25,000) and is explicitly not all-inclusive: the programme states that funding "is designed to cover the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses" and lists a closed set of eligible and ineligible costs.
purpose: The National Security Education Program (NSEP) awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service

The Boren Awards award scholarships and fellowships that have launched alumni careers into the federal workforce

selection_criteria: Boren Scholarships criterion 1: Does the applicant provide a clear and compelling explanation of the significance of their overseas destination, region, language, field of study, and overseas study to U.S. national security? Priority organizations (Tier One) are the Departments of War, State, and Homeland Security, as well as the Intelligence Community.

Boren Scholarships criterion 2: Does the applicant demonstrate an understanding of how they might fulfill the one-year federal service requirement and a longer-term commitment to the federal government? Consider the leadership potential the applicant would bring to the federal government.

Boren Scholarships criterion 3: Does the applicant demonstrate a serious commitment to language study, before, during, and after their overseas study? The Boren Awards require a minimum of 15-20 contact hours per week. Does the applicant have realistic expectations for the proficiency level obtainable abroad?

Boren Scholarships criterion 4: Has the applicant proposed a study plan in a preferred overseas destination, region, and language, with a preferred major or field of study, meeting the preferred duration of 25+ weeks? If not, have they made a compelling argument on the basis of U.S. national security?
Boren Scholarships criterion 5: Does the applicant possess the appropriate academic preparation, adaptability, flexibility, and maturity required to succeed abroad?

Boren Fellowships criterion 4 (additional): If proposing research in addition to language study, does the applicant have a comprehensive, clear and feasible overseas plan, with language study being the primary purpose of their overseas plan?
Veteran Preference: Veterans of the U.S. armed forces are encouraged to apply, and selection preference will be given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.

Preference factors: the Boren Awards give preference based on program duration, focus on intensive study of a preferred language in a preferred overseas destination, the applicant's field of study, and applicants with longer-term interest in a federal career.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated on these criteria by IIE-organized regional merit review panels consisting of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The regional panels make recommendations for each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know should be stated clearly in the essays and other application materials. Applicants are notified if they have been selected in mid-to-late April.
application_method: Start a new application on the Apply Now page by selecting the overseas location and language you want to study (you may change selections at any time)
Get support from your Boren Awards campus representative and watch the introductory webinar
Choose a programme: apply for a Regional Flagship Language Initiative or select/design your own study programme

Complete the application sections in order (eligibility determination, personal information, academic information, employment history, activities, programme information and budget, essays, language self-assessment, additional information, recommendations, submission agreement, review)
Notify your recommenders through the online system and track their submission status
Click 'Submit Application' on the Review section before the national deadline
application_steps: 1. Create a new application at https://apply.iie.org/borenscholarship (Boren Scholarships) or https://apply.iie.org/borenfellowship (Boren Fellowships)
2. Pass the Eligibility Determination section - you must answer all of these questions to unlock the rest of the application

3. Enter personal information (name, permanent and mailing address, email, telephone, sex as it appears on your birth certificate, birthdate, country of residence, veteran/reservist/active-service status)

4. Enter academic information (academic level, degree type, major, GPA, maximum possible GPA, institution location, dates attended/graduation date) and upload an UNOFFICIAL transcript of the current institution
5. List up to three relevant jobs and up to three relevant activities, 50-100 words each

6. Enter programme information: study abroad city, program sponsor, program name, proposed overseas institution, Study Plan Summary (max 250 words), upload the Study Abroad Program Description (max 5 pages), weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition, and any alternate study abroad program
7. Write and submit Essay 1 (National Security, max 800 words) and Essay 2 (Motivation and Public Service Careers, max 800 words for Scholarships / 1000 words for Fellowships)
8. Complete the Language Self-Assessment for the Boren language plus up to four additional languages

9. Complete Additional Information: up to three overseas countries, up to five honours and awards, optional other scholarships, ROTC participation, how you learned about Boren, prior NSEP participation
10. Add recommenders, select the type (Letter of Recommendation or Language Evaluation), and click 'Send to Recommender'
11. Read and agree to the Submission Agreement policies
12. Review the application, fix any errors flagged, and click 'Submit Application'

A national security argument in essay 1 that contradicts the career plan in essay 2
Jargon-heavy essay 1 written for specialists instead of an educated generalist audience
Transcripts containing an unredacted Social Security number or date of birth
Recommenders who are family members or friends, or letters submitted by a relative
Proposals focused on gender ideology, diversity/equity/inclusion or environmental justice, which the programme says it may not fund under the cited Executive Orders

records.name: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
records.official_source: U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Division of Graduate Education
records.region: United States (applicants must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents; study must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico)
records.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
records.deadline: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.
records.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. records.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.
records.notes: No post-graduate study service requirement. Fellowship funds are awarded to the institution of higher education at which the fellow is enrolled, and the institution is responsible for disbursing the stipend to the fellow; the fellowship is therefore only usable at an eligible accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. The fellowship period is five years with three years of financial support, so fellows must plan for two unfunded years. Fellows may transfer to another institution after completing the first fellowship year. Practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) are excluded at any time during the fellowship, as are joint science-professional degree programs. Applicants may submit only one application per annual competition, and only in the first year of their first graduate degree program (joint bachelor's-master's students are limited to one application). No clinical or medical-school pathway is eligible.

official_details.description: The purpose of the U.S. National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP) is to help ensure the quality, vitality, and strength of the scientific and engineering workforce of the United States. Since 1952, the program recognizes and supports outstanding graduate students pursuing full-time research-based master's and doctoral degrees in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM. Each Fellowship provides three years of support over a five-year Fellowship period. For each of the three years of support, NSF provides a $37,000 stipend and a $16,000 Cost of Education allowance provided to the institution of higher education (IHE) in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each Fellow using the support in a Fellowship year. While the Fellowship is offered to the individual, the Fellowship funds are awarded to the IHE at which a Fellow is enrolled, and the IHE is responsible for disbursement of the stipend to the Fellow.

document_format_rules: PDF format only for the statement documents.
Official transcripts should be uploaded in PDF format.

Page limits: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement three pages; Graduate Research Plan two pages. The page limits include all references, citations, charts, figures, images, and lists of publications and presentations.
Page size: standard 8.5" x 11" page size.

Margins: 1" margins on all sides, with no text inside the 1" margins (no header, footer, name, or page number). Remove page numbers; stray images or shapes can violate the margin rule even when the page margin is set to 1 inch.

Fonts: Arial (not Arial Narrow), Courier New, or Palatino Linotype in 10-point or larger; Times New Roman or Computer Modern family, 11-point or larger. Symbol or Cambria Math fonts are accepted for Greek letters or special characters. Smaller than 10-point fonts are accepted for mathematical formulas, equations, figures, tables or diagram captions.
Spacing: no less than single-spacing (approximately 6 lines per inch). Do not use line spacing options such as "exactly 11 point," that are less than single spaced.
Equations and symbols should be inserted as a non-editable image to bypass compliance checking and avoid font type and size errors.
Provide descriptive alternative text (alt text) for all images, graphs and charts, and use sufficient colour contrast for legibility.
Do not include links to supplemental materials (papers, videos); reviewers are instructed to evaluate only the evidence provided within the application.

Google Docs may not properly export bulleted text and should not be used; OpenOffice inserts an unallowable font for superscripts and subscripts; certain LaTeX-generated PDF elements are not yet supported and LaTeX fonts in formulas are not supported; Microsoft Word 2007 or earlier may produce font errors.
In Microsoft Office, "Select All" does not include inserted images, shapes, numbered lists or bullets, which carry their own fonts and must be updated to accepted fonts and sizes.
If text is inside an image, it must be part of the image and not editable, otherwise font errors can result.
Do not use 'Print as PDF'; use 'Export' / 'Create PDF'. On Mac, avoid 'Save as PDF' set to 'Best for Printing'; choose 'Best for electronic distribution and accessibility'.
To check fonts: open the PDF, right click the document content, select 'Document Properties', open the 'Fonts' tab and review the font types.
Blank pages within a PDF cause upload errors; export the PDF to Word, delete the blank page and re-save as PDF.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted.
selection_criteria: Intellectual Merit: the potential to advance knowledge.
Broader Impacts: the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers, and experts in STEM fields. Reviewers are selected by NSF Program Officers charged with oversight of the review process, and care is taken to ensure that reviewers have no conflicts of interest with the applicants. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study the applicant selected, using all available information in the completed application. Intellectual Merit factors may include the applicant's ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as a part of a team, interpret and communicate research (e.g. through publications or presentations), take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors may include the likelihood that the applicant's activities will increase participation in STEM, improve STEM education in schools through outreach and mentoring, increase public scientific literacy and public engagement with STEM through community outreach, increase collaboration among academia, industry and other types of organizations, improve education and educator development at any level in STEM, improve the well-being of individuals in society, develop a globally competitive STEM workforce, improve national security, increase the economic competitiveness of the U.S., and enhance infrastructure for research and education. NSF does not provide past applications or statements. GRFP funds people, not specific projects; the plan demonstrates potential, not a binding commitment. The program is highly competitive. NSF typically notifies applicants in the spring. Estimated number of awards under the 2027 solicitation: 1500, pending availability of funds.

Decide your Major Field of Study once and check the deadline calendar against it, rather than assuming a single closing date.
Do not waste time hunting for past successful applications — NSF does not provide them.
Do not submit by email or post; the module is the only accepted route.
Budget for the fact that the fellowship period is five years but only three years are funded; the $37,000 stipend must also absorb books, equipment and any uninsured health costs.
Attend the NSF GRFP applicant webinars and office hours if you can — several were held in September 2026 for this cycle.
Submit well before 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on your deadline day; the module will not accept late applications.
common_rejection_risks: Ineligible status: not a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident; on a student visa; awaiting a green card.
Ineligible academic level: more than one academic year completed in a graduate degree-granting programme, or a previous master's degree in any field.
Enrolment in, or plan to enter, a practice-oriented professional degree, or a joint science-professional degree such as MD/Ph.D. or JD/Ph.D.
A second application in the same annual competition, or a prior application made while enrolled in a degree-granting graduate programme.

Non-compliant statement PDFs: wrong font or size, text inside the 1-inch margins, page numbers in headers or footers, exceeding the three-page or two-page limits, wrong page size, line spacing below single, or an unsupported file format.
Blank pages in the uploaded PDF, which trigger upload errors.
Fewer than two reference letters received by the reference letter deadline — the application can be submitted but will not be reviewed.
Selecting a Major Field of Study whose subfield is not listed in the Notice of Funding Opportunity Appendix, which makes the research topic ineligible.
Including external links to supplemental material, which reviewers are instructed to ignore.
Missing the field-specific deadline or submitting after 8:00 p.m. Eastern time; the module does not accept late submissions.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Two of the five fellowship years carry no financial support.
Room and board, books, supplies, computers and equipment — not itemised as covered on the pages read; expected to come out of the $37,000 stipend.
Health insurance, where not provided by the institution.
Any travel, conference or relocation costs, for which no published coverage exists.
Fees the institution may charge that are not mandatory fees covered by the cost-of-education allowance — confirm with the institution.
Application costs are nil, but any costs of obtaining official transcripts.
document_audit: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement: PDF only, maximum three pages, 8.5" x 11", 1" margins with nothing in the margin including page numbers, Arial (not Arial Narrow)/Courier New/Palatino Linotype at 10 point or larger or Times New Roman/Computer Modern at 11 point or larger, no less than single spacing, separate headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.

Reference letters: two must be received by NSF; up to five may be requested and ranked; three names with affiliations and email addresses are required; family members may not serve as referees.

Letters are due 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on October 16, 2026, before the field-specific application deadline. If more than three letters are received, only the top three are considered.

submission_workflow: Create or sign in to your Research.gov account.
Open the GRFP Application Module when it opens (usually July or August).
Enter personal information, select your level, and record education, work and other experience.
Upload official undergraduate transcripts as PDF and graduate transcripts if applicable.
Select the Major Field of Study and subfield, and note the resulting deadline.
Add three reference writers with affiliations and email addresses, rank them, and submit the requests.
Write, format-check and upload both statement PDFs using the official templates.
Monitor for reference letter receipt; chase any referee who has not submitted before October 16, 2026.
Run the module's own compliance check, fix any page, margin or font errors, then submit before 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on your field's deadline.
Retain your submitted confirmation; if you need changes, withdraw and restore the package before the deadline, edit, and resubmit.

Enrol full-time in an eligible research-based graduate degree programme at the accredited nonprofit institution to which the award is made.
The fellowship funds go to the institution, which disburses the stipend to the fellow; coordinate stipend arrangements with your graduate school.
Follow the GRFP Administrative Guide for fellows and coordinating officials, plus NSF award terms and conditions.
Meet the programme's expectation of contributing to breakthrough discovery, technological innovation and national security, STEM outreach and mentorship, and U.S. economic competitiveness.
No post-graduate study service requirement and no return-home requirement apply.
Report outcomes and outcomes data under NSF Public Access and reporting requirements; supplemental funding exists to sustain research during medical leave.
Track the three years of financial support within the five-year fellowship period and plan self-funding for the other two years.

records.name: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
records.degree_levels: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
records.official_source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), administered with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE)
records.region: United States (federal agencies and U.S. Congressional offices in Washington, DC)
records.duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial programme Orientation
records.deadline: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
records.application_period: Online application opens August 3, 2026 and closes 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 for the 2027-2028 programme. Semi-finalist notifications with travel arrangements are made by February 24, 2027; interviews in Washington, DC February 27 - March 1, 2027; finalist notifications March 9, 2027; congressional fellows placement interviews mid-June 2027; fellows arrive in Washington, DC mid-August 2027.
records.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.
records.best_fit: Experienced, currently employed U.S. K-12 STEM teachers or district officials who have at least five complete years of full-time classroom STEM teaching, can secure an eleven-month leave of absence, and can relocate to the Washington, DC area.
records.funding_period: monthly living stipend over an eleven-month fellowship
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens who have completed five years of full-time STEM classroom teaching, have taught full-time in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school or school district for at least five of the last seven years, are currently so employed, can obtain an eleven-month leave of absence, and can obtain a recommendation letter from a school district official.
eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum full-time teaching requirement.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.
Be able to provide a letter of recommendation from a school district official as one of their three required letters of recommendation.
Be able to obtain a leave of absence from teaching in order to participate in the program for the full eleven months.
coverage: Monthly living stipend of $8,200.
Travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency; limitations on foreign travel vary by agency.
Education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved expenses aligned with the Fellow's individual professional development plan, including courses, conferences and professional books.
Relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for Fellows relocating from outside of the Washington, DC area (home-to-Washington distance more than 50 miles one way).
Stipend of up to $550 per month (individual plan) or $1,300 per month (family plan) to offset the cost of health insurance.
Designated office space and agency/office-specific orientation and training.
Official twice monthly professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
benefits: Develops a professional development plan to guide individual professional development objectives outside host office responsibilities, with ongoing mentoring provided by the AEF Programme.
Access to a national network of education leaders and programmes.
Placement in a federal agency or U.S. Congressional office, with the DOE sponsoring up to five placements in congressional offices.
Up to ten personal days off per year and up to ten sick days off without reduction in the Fellow's stipend.
Fellows are connected with outgoing Fellows to help identify available housing in the Washington, DC area.
requirements: All applications must be completed online through the online application system.
Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements.
All applications, including recommendations, are due by the specified application deadline; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for evaluation and placement.
Materials uploaded into the application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Completion of all required fields, including contact information; education background (formal education and continuing education); teaching and professional experience; professional awards and recognition; citizenship status; interest in federal agency and/or Congressional office placement; and five essay questions.
Submission of three letters of recommendation online, including one recommendation letter from a school district official.
School district officials do not include department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring their recommenders have the information needed to access the online Recommender form; requests can only be sent electronically through the online application system.
Provide proof of U.S. citizenship upon accepting a Fellowship offer.
Secure a leave of absence from teaching during the fellowship year.
Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment (mid-August through mid-July) in Washington, DC.
Meet the terms and conditions in the offer letter of appointment, including requirements for ethical conduct, and financial disclosure and conflict of interest.
Participate in the official professional development meetings, conferences and field trips organised for Fellows by the AEF Programme.
Have health care coverage during the fellowship appointment; Fellows are eligible to participate in the ORISE health insurance plan if they do not have other health insurance coverage.
Establish an individual Professional Development Plan for the year, which must be completed by early October.
Submit the requested written reports, presentations and surveys related to the Fellowship experience before the published deadlines.
Represent themselves as educators in a responsible and professional manner.
Only use the AEF Programme name or the Fellow's affiliation with the AEF Programme in an authorised manner.
In managing their responsibilities throughout the fellowship, give priority to the duties assigned to them by their host office.
application_method: Create a new User ID and Password in the online application system (click 'Create New Account').
Complete all required fields of the online application.
Draft the five essay responses offline in word processing software, spell-check them, and copy and paste into the appropriate areas of the online application.

Request recommendations from three individuals familiar with the applicant's professional and education background and their experience, aptitude or promise relevant to the AEF Programme, entering their names and email addresses on the Request Recommendations page; requests can be made as soon as the application system is accessed, without waiting for the application to be complete.

Confirm that one recommender is a school district official and select the correct Type option (a school headmaster/headmistress or equivalent to a school principal qualifies; choose 'Other' and enter the position title in the Other District Official text box).
Monitor the 'Check Your Status' page to confirm that all three recommendations have been submitted; use the 'Resend Email' button on the Recommendations tab to chase recommenders.
Submit the completed application, including all three letters of recommendation, by 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026.
Check Your Status periodically before the deadline; the applicant is responsible for confirming completeness, as the programme will not tell them what is missing.
If selected as a semi-finalist, travel to Washington, DC on Saturday February 27, 2027, attend orientation on Sunday February 28, and be interviewed Monday March 1 and possibly Tuesday March 2.
Finalists selected for a Congressional office placement return to Washington, DC in mid-June 2027 for a week of placement interviews.
records.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.
records.notes: Not deferrable and not renewable: the fellowship is for a single eleven-month period from mid-August with initial programme Orientation, and there is no flexibility in start and end dates. There is no return-home requirement, but relocation to the Washington, DC area is a programme requirement if the Fellow does not already live there. The Fellow cannot maintain a teaching position while serving; a leave of absence must be secured or employment terminated. The AEF Programme does not arrange housing. Fellows receive a monthly stipend and are not considered employees of the hosting office, so they do not earn sick or annual leave, although up to ten personal days and ten sick days are allowed without stipend reduction. All stipends are reportable to the Internal Revenue Service and the AEF Programme does not withhold taxes; fellows may need to file Form 1040-ES and pay estimated income tax. Current and former AEF Fellows are not eligible to apply for a second fellowship. No clinical restriction is published.

official_details.description: The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program provides a unique opportunity for accomplished K-12 educators in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to serve in the national education arena. Fellows spend eleven months working in Federal agencies or in U.S. Congressional offices, applying their extensive knowledge and classroom experiences to national education program and/or education policy efforts. At the end of the Fellowship, educators are equipped with access to a national network of education leaders and programs, a better understanding of the challenges and possibilities in STEM education, and a renewed passion for teaching, ready to make significant contributions to the educational community. The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship Act (Fellowship Act Public Law 103-382, Improving America's Schools Act of 1994) was signed into law in November 1994 and gives the DOE the responsibility for managing the program. The DOE Office of Science's Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS) manages this program for DOE in collaboration with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) and other partners.
purpose: Provide a unique opportunity for accomplished K-12 educators in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to serve in the national education arena.

Allow Fellows to spend eleven months working in Federal agencies or in U.S. Congressional offices, applying their extensive knowledge and classroom experiences to national education program and/or education policy efforts.
Support the intellectual and professional development of K-12 STEM teachers who have the desire to share their education and classroom expertise with Federal agencies and U.S. Congressional offices.
Equip educators with access to a national network of education leaders and programs, a better understanding of the challenges and possibilities in STEM education, and a renewed passion for teaching.

Advance national K-12 STEM education through contributions to programme design, legislation and policy, federal agency partnerships, web-based science education tools, and evaluation of national and regional school reform and teacher preparation programmes.
Inspire the next generation of scientific and technological leaders by strengthening K-12 STEM teaching.
degree_levels: Not a degree programme; the fellowship is an eleven-month professional appointment for K-12 STEM educators and school district officials
study_type: Full-time eleven-month appointment in a Federal agency or U.S. Congressional office in Washington, DC
Education policy and/or programme related activities

official_details.application_cycle: Annual. For the 2027-2028 programme the online application opened August 3, 2026 and closed 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.

official_details.deadline_note: All parts of the online application, including all three letters of recommendation, must be completed before the deadline. Recommendation letters must be submitted through the online application system; WDTS will not accept mailed or emailed recommendation letters. A limited number of personal and professional travel days are allowed, but dates and length of absence from the host office are subject to AEF Programme guidelines and approval by the sponsoring agency and/or host office.
official_details.funding_type: Stipend plus capped travel, education, relocation and health insurance allowances
official_details.funding_label: $8,200 monthly living stipend, plus up to $5,000 travel allowance, up to $1,000 education allowance, up to $3,500 relocation reimbursement, and up to $550/month (individual) or $1,300/month (family) health insurance stipend
official_details.funding_period: per month over the eleven-month fellowship
official_details.living_cost_coverage: A monthly living stipend of $8,200.
official_details.travel_coverage: A travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency. Limitations on foreign travel will vary by agency. All travel requests must be pre-approved by the AEF Programme prior to making any travel arrangements. The travel allowance is primarily to support travel the host office may require, and Fellows may also use part of it for travel related to their individual Professional Development Plan objectives. Separately, up to $3,500 is reimbursed for relocation inbound and outbound between home and Washington, DC if the distance is more than 50 miles one way.
official_details.tuition_rule: Not applicable. The AEF Programme is not a degree programme and no tuition, fees or education costs are involved.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Not applicable. There is no tuition; the Fellow is on an eleven-month leave of absence from teaching or has terminated employment with their school.
official_details.tax_status: In general, all stipends paid to the Fellow are reportable to the Internal Revenue Service. The AEF Programme does not withhold taxes from these payments. Fellows will need to consider whether filing Form 1040-ES on a quarterly basis and paying estimated income taxes is necessary in order to avoid late payment penalties. Federal agencies and ORISE cannot give participants tax advice.

No tuition or formal education costs are covered, because the programme is not a degree programme.

Tax liability: the programme does not withhold taxes, so fellows bear their own estimated tax payments and any penalties.
benefits: Develops a professional development plan to guide individual professional development objectives outside their host office responsibilities with ongoing mentoring provided by the AEF Program.

Placement in a Federal agency or U.S. Congressional office, with DOE sponsoring up to five placements in congressional offices.
Current sponsoring agencies include the Department of War (DOW), the Department of Energy (DOE), the Library of Congress (LOC), and the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).
eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum full-time teaching requirement.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.

official_details.selection_notes: To be considered, an applicant must meet all eligibility criteria and submit all required materials by the application deadline. An initial eligibility and compliance review is conducted by the AEF Program to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation and selection, and the materials uploaded and received through the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation and selection. The merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination of eligible applicants based on pre-established criteria; application evaluators must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies and must comply with all applicable DOE rules or directives on evaluation and merit review. Applications are evaluated in four areas: teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Program. Following merit review, highly reviewed applications are viewed by the Federal agency sponsors, who evaluate on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of experience and subject matter expertise with host office interests, and quality of recommendations; the sponsors select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days for individual interviews and information sessions with one or more sponsoring agencies and/or host offices. Following the semi-finalist interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring Federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers from the Federal agencies. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements, who return to Washington, DC in the June-July timeframe for placement interviews with Congressional host offices. The number of Fellowships awarded is contingent upon the availability of funds by the sponsoring agencies; in recent years the program has awarded between ten and twenty Fellowships a year. Recruitment and selection of participants is done without regard to race, gender, age, color, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will hold U.S. citizenship by the November 5, 2026 deadline; naturalising later does not help.
Confirm you will have completed five full years of full-time classroom teaching by the deadline, excluding student teaching and assistant teaching.
Confirm at least five of your last seven years were full-time STEM teaching in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school.
Confirm you are currently employed full-time in a U.S. K-12 school or school district right now.

Line up a school district official today - principal, superintendent, deputy/assistant superintendent, or school board member qualify; department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals and vice-principals do not.
Secure your school's or district's agreement to an eleven-month leave of absence, starting mid-August 2027, because you cannot hold your post while serving.
Create your online application account now and submit your three recommendation requests immediately; do not wait until your essays are finished.
Draft all five essay responses offline in Word, spell-check, then paste into the system, because it logs you out after 60 minutes.

important_advice_for_students: This is not a graduate scholarship and not a degree programme; it is an eleven-month paid appointment that ends your teaching job for a year, so treat it as a career decision rather than funding for study.
Do not count on it for tuition - there is no tuition element whatsoever.
Do not assume housing is covered; the programme explicitly does not arrange housing, and only $3,500 of relocation is reimbursed for moves over 50 miles one way.
Request your three recommendations first, not last; once a letter is received it cannot be removed, and all three must be in the system by the deadline.
Save your essay text locally before pasting, because the system times out after 60 minutes and unsaved work is lost.
Check your Check Your Status page yourself; the programme does not email you about missing components.
Prepare for interview travel; semi-finalists fund their own trip to Washington, DC in late February, and the $5,000 travel allowance is a fellowship benefit, not an application reimbursement.
Plan for federal ethics and financial disclosure compliance once in the role; the appointment carries 10 CFR Part 1010 and 5 CFR Part 2635 obligations.
Track the three-applications-in-six-years cap carefully, because a rejected application is not kept on file for the following year.
common_rejection_risks: Not a U.S. citizen by the deadline; a pending naturalisation does not qualify.
Fewer than five completed years of full-time classroom teaching, or relying on student teaching or assistant teaching to reach five years.
Fewer than five of the last seven years spent teaching STEM full-time in a U.S. K-12 school.
Not currently employed full-time in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school or school district, for example teaching abroad this year.
Recommendation set that does not include a qualifying school district official, or one that includes only department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.
Incomplete application at the deadline: any missing field, essay, or letter of recommendation means the application is not considered, and uploaded materials are the sole basis for evaluation.
Recommendation letters sent by mail or email instead of through the online system; WDTS does not accept them.
Applying more than three times within a six year period, or applying as a current or former Fellow.
Inability to secure an eleven-month leave of absence or to relocate to Washington, DC for the full appointment.
A final letter arriving after 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing in the Washington, DC area, which the AEF Program does not arrange or fund beyond a capped $3,500 relocation reimbursement.
Any health insurance cost above the $550/month individual or $1,300/month family stipend, including the cost of joining the ORISE health insurance plan.
Federal, state and local income tax on the stipend and allowances; the program does not withhold and fellows may need Form 1040-ES quarterly payments.
Personal and professional travel beyond the $5,000 host-agency travel allowance, including the applicant's own trip for semi-finalist interviews.
Professional development spending beyond the $1,000 education allowance.
School or district pension and benefits contributions that stop during the leave of absence, and any loss of seniority, which the programme does not compensate.
Relocation costs if the distance is 50 miles one way or less, or above the $3,500 cap.
Costs of maintaining or terminating employment arrangements at the home school.
Any dependent or partner costs beyond the family-plan health insurance stipend.

records.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.
records.best_fit: Full-time U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who have already obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, are enrolled in a thesis-based research Ph.D. in a DOE-supported STEM field at an accredited U.S. institution, and can arrange a 3 to 12 month in-person research residency with a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist at a participating laboratory.
records.funding_period: per month during the award period (up to $3,600), plus up to $3,000 total inbound and outbound travel reimbursement per award
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents aged 18 or older, full-time enrolled in a qualified thesis-based Ph.D. programme in a DOE-supported STEM field, have obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, and secure a collaborating scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory.
eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
coverage: A monthly stipend in the amount of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.

Reimbursement for in-bound and out-bound transportation to the host DOE laboratory/facility, limited to a total travel benefit of up to $3,000 per award, available only if the host DOE national laboratory/facility is greater than 50 miles from the awardee's home graduate institution.
The opportunity, after receiving the award, to apply for further funding to conduct a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit to select research institutions abroad, such as CERN or RIKEN.
benefits: Access to DOE national laboratory expertise, user facilities, instrumentation and leadership-class computing systems.
Professional network expansion and access to scientific user facilities not available at most universities.
The possible opportunity for a short international research visit of 6 weeks maximum to an institution such as CERN or RIKEN, applied for after the award is received.
Weekly virtual office hours and application assistance workshops offered by the SCGSR Program.
A running list of collaborating laboratory scientists who are ready to work with SCGSR awardees.
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts.
Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Submit two Letters of Support, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both completed through the online application system.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project aligns with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials.

The research proposal must address the stated aims in at least one of the SCGSR Priority Research Areas and must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets.

The proposed research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project and must be approved by the primary graduate thesis advisor, whose approval is made through the thesis advisor's Letter of Support.
Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
application_method: Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline.
Review the eligibility rules, priority research areas and merit review criteria before writing anything.

Identify a collaborating research scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory or facility, or ask the SCGSR Program Manager or the laboratory point of contact for candidates, and agree the project scope with them.
Consult your primary graduate thesis advisor and confirm Ph.D. candidacy, an approved thesis topic, and that the proposed laboratory work is part of your thesis project.
Obtain official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as a signed letter from the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, including the date of thesis committee approval of your topic.
Obtain your official graduate transcript stamped with the university seal, and redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth while keeping your name visible.

Co-develop the research proposal with the collaborating scientist, in consultation with your thesis advisor, addressing the stated aims of at least one priority research area and identifying how the laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used; keep it to three pages plus a one-page reference list.

Ensure both your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist review and approve the final proposal PDF before uploading it, because they receive an automatic notification when you upload or update it.

Enter your thesis advisor's contact information under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information' and the collaborating scientist's contact information under 'Host DOE Laboratory', then use 'Send Email' on the Request Letters of Support tab to send both requests.
Monitor the receipt of both letters of support through the online system and send reminder emails where needed.
Review and print or export your application as a PDF using the 'Print your Application' option before submitting.

Submit the complete application, including transcripts, proof of candidacy, research proposal and both letters of support, by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, and confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted'.
If selected, respond to the DOE Office of Science notification promptly; you will be given about a week to decide whether to accept.
records.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.
records.notes: Not deferrable in the ordinary sense, but the award period may be changed under exceptional circumstances, such as unexpected schedule changes at scientific user facilities, with the support of both the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and the primary graduate thesis advisor; such requests must reach the SCGSR Program Manager at least 20 business days in advance with signed consent letters from both, and the overall project period must remain the same length as proposed. Cumulative SCGSR award periods across all awards may not exceed 12 months. The award is not an internship and not a full graduate fellowship: the SCGF programme, which provided a stipend and tuition support for up to three years, is no longer accepting applications. Awardees are not employees of the host laboratory or DOE and are not entitled to employee benefits. Regular travel between the host laboratory and the university during the award period violates the terms and conditions, because a full-time schedule at the host is required during normal laboratory business hours; awardees may observe the host's holidays but must report any expected interruption to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager. Awardees become ineligible if, after applying, they accept a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host laboratory, such as an hourly paid intern or a full-time or temporary position. Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens, is not eligible, which excludes clinical and medical-degree routes; joint MD/PhD, joint JD/PhD, DVM, MBA, MD, JD and joint BS/MS programmes are all ineligible. Published work based on the research should carry the SCGSR acknowledgement statement, including contract number DE-SC0014664.
