records.name: Chevening ASEAN Scholarship
records.official_source: Chevening (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office scheme)
records.region: United Kingdom (ASEAN member states and Timor-Leste)
records.duration: One-year master's degree in the UK
records.deadline: Applications for Chevening Scholarships are now open! Applications close at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. 'The deadline for applications is 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. You will not be able to access the online application system after this date.'
records.application_period: Opened at 11:00 UTC on 4 August 2026 and closes at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026, for the 2027-28 Chevening Scholarship cycle. Studies begin in the UK in September/October 2027.
records.description: The Chevening ASEAN Scholarship is the ASEAN variant of the UK government-funded Chevening Scholarship programme. Applicants from ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste apply through the standard Chevening Scholarship process and, on top of all standard Chevening benefits, are considered for an enhanced UK programme of exclusive events, priority invitations, the ASEAN Chevening Conference and access to the global Chevening alumni community. Chevening states the scholarship is fully funded, covering a one-year UK master's degree; the highest-ranking applicant(s) from each participating country are considered for the ASEAN element. Chevening does not publish the monthly stipend figure on its public pages - the amount is stated in the applicant's Final Award Letter.
records.best_fit: Citizens or residents of an ASEAN member state or Timor-Leste who hold an undergraduate degree qualifying them for a UK master's programme, have at least two years (2,800 hours) of post-degree work experience, can commit to returning home for at least two years, and can apply to three different eligible UK taught master's courses. Opting in for the ASEAN element does not affect your chances of a standard Chevening Scholarship.
records.eligibility_summary: Must be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory (ASEAN member state or Timor-Leste for the ASEAN element), with an undergraduate degree, two years' work experience, three eligible UK master's course choices and a commitment to return home for two years.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.

If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country. This does not have to be the country of citizenship, but all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours.

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme. You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate; you will need the certificate by the time of your interview.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses.
You must have received an unconditional offer from at least one of these course choices by the deadline listed on the application timeline.
The ASEAN element is for outstanding individuals from ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste; the highest-ranking applicant(s) from each participating country will be considered.
coverage: Full tuition fees for a one-year UK master's degree at the university of the scholar's choice
A monthly stipend, stated in the Final Award Letter, which Chevening says is intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights between the nearest airport in the home country and the nearest airport to the UK university, booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge ('you don't need to pay the visa fee or the Immigration Health Surcharge')
Arrival allowance where confirmed in the Final Award Letter, which includes an element for warm clothing
Departure allowance for scholars on a full award
A travel grant
benefits: ASEAN element: exclusive events
ASEAN element: priority invitations
ASEAN element: ASEAN Chevening Conference
ASEAN element: membership of the global Chevening alumni community
Standard Chevening Scholarship benefits for all Chevening scholars
requirements: Applications must be submitted through the Chevening online application system reached from your own country/territory page.
Choose three different eligible UK master's degree courses in order of preference; duplicate courses at the same university cannot be considered.
Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses (not research-focused MRes programmes), based in the UK, starting in the autumn term (usually September/October) and lasting nine to twelve months.
Courses cannot be part-time, distance learning, a PhD or DPhil, or include more than one month of study outside the UK.
Provide the names and contact details of two referees in the application.
If shortlisted, upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate to the online application system no later than seven working days before your interview.
If successful at interview, submit at least one unconditional UK university offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
Apply for your own student visa; Chevening cannot apply on your behalf.
records.english_requirement: The application form must be completed in English: 'If the application form is not completed in English, it will be deemed ineligible.' Chevening also publishes that 'Though an English test score is not required for Chevening, strong English skills are necessary to write a successful application, conduct the interview, and apply to a UK university.' Reference letters must be in English. Separately, UK university applications 'typically requiring: A letter of motivation or personal statement. English language test results. Proof of previous qualifications. Academic and professional references.'
application_method: Check your eligibility against Chevening's published eligibility criteria.
Read the Chevening application criteria and preparation guidance.
Research and choose three different eligible UK master's courses using the Chevening course finder.

Register via the 'apply today' link on your country/territory page on chevening.org, read and consent to the terms and conditions and Privacy Notice, then register your email address and mobile phone number.
Pass the online eligibility checker (you get four more attempts if you fail but believe it was an error).
Note and keep your unique access code.

Complete each application section: personal details, immigration details, education history (up to 15 entries), work history (up to 15 entries), programmes of study (three UK master's choices), and the essay answers.
Submit; sift against eligibility criteria runs from October 2026.
If shortlisted, upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate at least seven working days before your interview.
Attend your interview at a British embassy or high commission, March to April 2027.
If successful, secure and upload an unconditional offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
records.selection_notes: Applications are sifted against the eligibility criteria from October 2026, then independent reading committees assess all eligible applications from mid-October 2026 to January 2027. British embassies and high commissions produce shortlists and interview candidates in March to April 2027; results are announced from mid-June 2027. Applicants are assessed on leadership and influencing skills, the ability to build professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes, the reasons for the course and university choice (linked to UK priorities such as promoting growth and prosperity, building climate resilience, strengthening security and stability, and supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies), and a realistic short, mid and long-term career plan. For the ASEAN element specifically, 'the highest-ranking applicant(s) from each participating country will be considered'. Chevening states: 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited.'
records.notes: Applicants must commit to returning to their home country (country of award) for at least two years after the scholarship ends. The award is for one year only and is not renewable; Chevening publishes no renewal or deferral provisions, so those fields are left null. Reference letters must be uploaded at least seven working days before the interview - 'Failure to do so will result in your application no longer being considered for a Chevening award.' Applicants must not have previously studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship (a former Chevening Fellow may apply for a scholarship only after five years have passed since completing their fellowship). No clinical or medical restriction is published.

official_details.description: The Chevening ASEAN Scholarship is an opportunity for outstanding individuals from ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste to pursue a one-year master's degree in the UK. Applicants apply for a Chevening Scholarship through the standard application process and 'the highest-ranking applicant(s) from each participating country will be considered'. In addition to the standard benefits of a Chevening Scholarship, it includes an enhanced UK programme comprising exclusive events, priority invitations, the ASEAN Chevening Conference and membership of the global alumni community. It is open to all fields of study with no specific subject areas prioritised.
purpose: Enable outstanding individuals from ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste to pursue a one-year master's degree in the UK as part of the Chevening Scholarship programme.
Add an enhanced UK programme - exclusive events, priority invitations, the ASEAN Chevening Conference and alumni community access - on top of standard Chevening benefits.

Support Chevening's stated commitment across all themes to under-represented groups, advancing women's leadership, and strengthening the UK's international alliances by equipping individuals to become part of a global community of influential future leaders.
study_type: Taught master's course
Full-time
official_details.degree_award: Full one-year UK master's degree qualification (not a PhD/DPhil, not a research-focused MRes)
official_details.duration: One-year master's degree in the UK. Courses must be between nine and twelve months in duration, though Chevening states studies begin in the UK in September/October 2027.
official_details.application_cycle: 2027-28 Chevening Scholarship cycle
official_details.deadline_central_display: 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC
official_details.deadline_institutional: Individual UK university course deadlines also apply, and an unconditional offer must be secured by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
official_details.deadline_note: Applications opened at 11:00 UTC on 4 August 2026 and close at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. 'You will not be able to access the online application system after this date.' Reference letters must be uploaded at least seven working days before the interview.
official_details.funding_label: Chevening Scholarships are fully-funded
official_details.tuition_coverage: Full tuition fees for a one-year UK master's degree at the scholar's chosen university.
official_details.living_cost_coverage: A monthly stipend stated in the Final Award Letter. Chevening publishes that 'Your monthly stipend (as stated in your Final Award Letter) is intended to cover all of your living costs, including accommodation.'
official_details.travel_coverage: Return air travel from the nearest airport in the home country to the nearest airport to the UK university, confirmed in the Final Award Letter and booked by Chevening's designated travel agency; plus a travel grant.
official_details.tuition_rule: Chevening pays full tuition fees directly for the one-year UK master's course at the scholar's chosen university. Chevening's own wording is 'Study in the UK on a fully-funded scholarship with Chevening' and 'Apply today for a fully funded Chevening Scholarship to study for a one-year master's degree at any UK university.'
covered_expenses: Full tuition fees for the one-year UK master's degree
Monthly living stipend (amount stated in the Final Award Letter), intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee
Immigration Health Surcharge
Arrival allowance where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Departure allowance for scholars on a full award
Travel grant
Contribution towards the cost of a TB test for scholars from countries where TB testing is required
not_covered_or_excluded: Accommodation: the Scholar's responsibility - 'As a Chevening Scholar, it is your responsibility to find accommodation for the duration of the scholarship', funded from the stipend
Accommodation deposits and agency or administration fees for private accommodation - 'The Secretariat cannot make deposit payments on your behalf or reimburse accommodation deposits'
Utility costs such as gas, water and electricity if not included in private accommodation rent
Travel insurance - 'The Secretariat does not provide travel insurance for scholars.'
Excess or additional baggage - 'If you require additional/excess baggage, you will need to pay and arrange this directly with the airline.'
Travel for any dependents - 'Travel for any dependents will not be paid for by the Secretariat but can still be booked through our travel agency.'
Onward travel, stopovers in other countries, and premium/business class - travel is economy class, one way only, nearest airport to nearest airport, most economical route
Application support or advice from third parties - Chevening 'does not endorse or work with third parties who charge for application support or advice'
Cost of a TB test up front (Chevening makes a contribution after arrival in the UK)
Stipend beyond the end of your course end date or UK departure date, whichever is earlier
benefits: Exclusive events
Priority invitations
ASEAN Chevening Conference
Join our global alumni community
eligibility: Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.
If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country, with a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country for at least two years after the scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience (2,800 hours) acquired after completing your undergraduate degree.
Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme, completed at least two years before the application deadline.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses and secure an unconditional offer from at least one by the offer deadline.
For the ASEAN element: be from an ASEAN member state or Timor-Leste.
general_eligibility: Chevening states: 'There is no upper age limit.' Gender, age, sexual orientation, religion, marriage or parenthood status, caste and class do not affect eligibility.
You must apply from your country of citizenship, regardless of where you currently live.
European overseas territory residents may apply through the Chevening award scheme for the European country of which they are a citizen.
Having a master's degree does not prevent you from applying for a second master's degree in the UK.
ineligibility_conditions: Hold British or dual British citizenship (unless you are a citizen of a British Overseas Territory or hold BN(O) and are applying from Hong Kong).
Hold refugee status in a country not eligible for Chevening. (If you are a citizen of an eligible country and hold refugee status in another eligible country, you are eligible.)
Are resident in the UK at the time of application (excluding the British Overseas Territories).

Are an employee, an immediate relative of an employee, or a former employee (within the last two years from the opening of Chevening applications) of a government department, the British Council, a partner UK university, or any of their wholly owned subsidiaries. Individuals contracted to work on any British Council programme or project, and their relatives, are ineligible.

Have previously studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship. Applicants who previously received UK Government funding through a Chevening Fellowship may apply for a scholarship only after five years have passed since completing their fellowship.

Immediate relatives are defined as parents or step-parents, siblings or step-siblings, children or step-children, spouse, civil partner or unmarried (where the couple have been in a relationship akin to marriage or civil partnership for at least two years).
official_details.citizenship_residency: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries or territories. The ASEAN element is restricted to citizens of ASEAN member states and Timor-Leste. Applicants must apply from their country of citizenship regardless of where they live, and must not be resident in the UK at the time of application.
official_details.international_eligibility: Explicitly for international applicants: British, dual British, and UK-resident applicants are ineligible, and previous UK government-funded scholarship holders are barred.

undergraduate: You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate.
You will need your degree certificate by the time of your interview.
Work experience counted towards the 2,800-hour requirement must be gained after completing your undergraduate degree.
masters: Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme.
Chevening Scholarships are for UK master's degrees only - three master's degree courses must be chosen on the application form.

Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses (not research-focused MRes programmes), leading to a master's degree qualification, based in the UK, starting in the autumn term (usually September/October).
Courses cannot be part-time or distance learning, less than nine months or more than 12 months in duration, a PhD or DPhil, or taught with more than one month of study outside the UK.
Your three course choices must be three different courses; applicants who enter duplicate courses at the same universities cannot be considered.

Count your post-degree work hours: the system multiplies weeks worked by hours per week and you need at least 2,800 hours (typically 35-60 hours per week, 40-50 weeks per year).

important_advice_for_students: Do not pay anyone to help you apply. 'Applying for a Chevening Scholarship is free' and Chevening 'does not endorse or work with third parties who charge for application support or advice.'

Do not use AI tools such as ChatGPT to write your essay answers. 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited' and Chevening 'uses tools and software to identify fraud, plagiarism, and AI-generated answers in applications.'
Do not ignore the 6 October 2026 deadline. The system locks at 11:00 UTC and you will not be able to access your application afterwards.
You must apply to your UK universities yourself as well as to Chevening. Chevening does not submit anything for you.
Budget for what Chevening does not pay: accommodation deposit and agency fees, travel insurance, excess baggage and any dependent's travel.
Budget your housing choice around the stipend - your stipend is intended to cover living costs including accommodation, so a more expensive area leaves less for everything else.
Start your TB test or ATAS clearance as soon as you get your conditional offer email; each certificate is only valid for six months and the processes can take weeks or months.

common_rejection_risks: Failing or not passing the online eligibility checker.
Not being a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country, holding British or dual British citizenship, or residing in the UK at the time of application.
Having studied in the UK previously on a UK government-funded scholarship (five-year bar after a Chevening Fellowship).
Being an employee, relative, or recent ex-employee of a government department, the British Council, a partner UK university or their subsidiaries.
Under 2,800 hours of post-degree work experience, or entering work history wrongly (wrong weeks, duplicate entries, unrealistic hours).
Not completing the application form in English - the application is deemed ineligible.
Entering duplicate courses, or three courses at the same university.
Choosing an ineligible course: part-time, distance learning, a research MRes, a PhD/DPhil, under nine or over twelve months, or more than one month of study outside the UK.
Missing the reference letter upload deadline - 'Failure to do so will result in your application no longer being considered for a Chevening award.'
Using AI-generated, plagiarised or copied content, which Chevening detects and disqualifies.
Being unable to show a realistic short, mid and long-term career plan, or examples of leadership and influencing with clear results.

records.description: The Chevening SIDS Scholarship is the Small Island Developing State variant of the UK government-funded Chevening Scholarship programme. Applicants from Commonwealth SIDS apply through the standard Chevening Scholarship process and must study on courses that address a national development priority or capacity shortage - human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; or supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives. On top of standard Chevening benefits, SIDS scholars receive an enhanced UK programme of exclusive events, an FCDO welcome event where they network with SIDS scholars from the Commonwealth Scholarships Commission and FCDO officials, and eligibility for Chevening Alumni Programme Fund support. Chevening publishes no stipend figure on its public pages; the amount is stated in the applicant's Final Award Letter.
records.best_fit: Citizens or residents of a participating Commonwealth Small Island Developing State who hold an undergraduate degree qualifying them for a UK master's programme, have at least two years (2,800 hours) of post-degree work experience, can commit to returning home for at least two years, and can choose three eligible UK taught master's courses relevant to a national development priority or capacity shortage. Opting in for the SIDS element does not affect your chances of a standard Chevening Scholarship.
records.eligibility_summary: Must meet the standard Chevening eligibility criteria and be a citizen of a participating SIDS country, and must study on a course addressing a national development priority or capacity shortage.
eligibility: To be eligible for a Chevening SIDS Scholarship, you must meet the standard eligibility criteria for Chevening, and be a citizen from one of the participating countries shown on the map on the official page.
Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.

If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country. This does not have to be the country of citizenship, but all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours.

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme. You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate; you will need the certificate by the time of your interview.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses, and receive an unconditional offer from at least one by the deadline listed on the application timeline.

Applicants are required to study on courses that help to address a national development priority or capacity shortage. This includes courses relating to: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives.
coverage: Full tuition fees for a one-year UK master's degree at the university of the scholar's choice
A monthly stipend, stated in the Final Award Letter, which Chevening says is intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights between the nearest airport in the home country and the nearest airport to the UK university, booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge ('you don't need to pay the visa fee or the Immigration Health Surcharge')

Standard Chevening Scholarship benefits for all Chevening scholars

In addition to the standard benefits of a Chevening Scholarship, the scheme includes an enhanced UK programme of exclusive events, exclusive networking opportunities including an FCDO welcome event, and membership of the global Chevening alumni community with eligibility for Chevening Alumni Programme Fund support.

eligibility: Meet the standard Chevening eligibility criteria and be a citizen from one of the participating SIDS countries shown on the official map.
Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.
If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country, with a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country for at least two years after the scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience (2,800 hours) acquired after completing your undergraduate degree.
Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme, completed at least two years before the application deadline.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses and secure an unconditional offer from at least one by the offer deadline.
Study on a course that helps to address a national development priority or capacity shortage.
general_eligibility: Chevening states: 'There is no upper age limit.' Gender, age, sexual orientation, religion, marriage or parenthood status, caste and class do not affect eligibility.
You must apply from your country of citizenship, regardless of where you currently live.
European overseas territory residents may apply through the Chevening award scheme for the European country of which they are a citizen.
Having a master's degree does not prevent you from applying for a second master's degree in the UK.
ineligibility_conditions: Hold British or dual British citizenship (unless you are a citizen of a British Overseas Territory or hold BN(O) and are applying from Hong Kong).
Hold refugee status in a country not eligible for Chevening. (If you are a citizen of an eligible country and hold refugee status in another eligible country, you are eligible.)
Are resident in the UK at the time of application (excluding the British Overseas Territories).

Are an employee, an immediate relative of an employee, or a former employee (within the last two years from the opening of Chevening applications) of a government department, the British Council, a partner UK university, or any of their wholly owned subsidiaries. Individuals contracted to work on any British Council programme or project, and their relatives, are ineligible.

Have previously studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship. Applicants who previously received UK Government funding through a Chevening Fellowship may apply for a scholarship only after five years have passed since completing their fellowship.
Not a citizen of one of the participating SIDS countries - the SIDS element is restricted to those countries.

Immediate relatives are defined as parents or step-parents, siblings or step-siblings, children or step-children, spouse, civil partner or unmarried (where the couple have been in a relationship akin to marriage or civil partnership for at least two years).
official_details.citizenship_residency: Citizens of participating Commonwealth Small Island Developing States. Applicants must apply from their country of citizenship regardless of where they live, and must not be resident in the UK at the time of application.
official_details.international_eligibility: Explicitly for international applicants: British, dual British, and UK-resident applicants are ineligible, and previous UK government-funded scholarship holders are barred.

undergraduate: You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate.
You will need your degree certificate by the time of your interview.
Work experience counted towards the 2,800-hour requirement must be gained after completing your undergraduate degree.
masters: Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme.
Chevening Scholarships are for UK master's degrees only - three master's degree courses must be chosen on the application form.

For the SIDS element, the chosen course must help address a national development priority or capacity shortage: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; or supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives.

Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses (not research-focused MRes programmes), leading to a master's degree qualification, based in the UK, starting in the autumn term (usually September/October).
Courses cannot be part-time or distance learning, less than nine months or more than 12 months in duration, a PhD or DPhil, or taught with more than one month of study outside the UK.
Your three course choices must be three different courses; applicants who enter duplicate courses at the same universities cannot be considered.
phd: Not applicable: Chevening Scholarships are for UK master's degrees only. Courses cannot be a PhD or DPhil.

host_requirements: The host must be a UK university offering an eligible course listed in the Chevening course finder.

The applicant must apply directly to each chosen university through its website, typically providing a letter of motivation or personal statement, English language test results, proof of previous qualifications, and academic and professional references.
The applicant must secure an unconditional offer from at least one of the three chosen courses; the only acceptable condition is financial (for example, paying a deposit).
The university issues the Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) needed for the student visa application.
The university must share the scholar's accommodation address with the Programme Officer if it changes during the Chevening year.
requirements: Apply through the Chevening online application system via the 'apply today' link on your country/territory page.
Opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship as part of the standard application.

Choose three different eligible UK master's degree courses that address a national development priority or capacity shortage, and secure an unconditional offer from at least one by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
Provide the names and contact details of two referees; they can be two professional referees, two academic referees, or one of each.
A referee should know you in a professional or personal capacity but not be a friend or relative.
Upload two reference letters and your undergraduate degree certificate at least seven working days before your interview.
Chevening will not contact your referees for you - you must collect and upload the references yourself, though the British embassy or high commission may contact them later for verification.
Attend an interview at a British embassy or high commission, March to April 2027.
Apply for your own student visa; Chevening cannot apply on your behalf. You will need both your CAS and your FAL, and the FAL is issued by Chevening by August.
Applying for a Chevening Scholarship is free.

Your undergraduate degree certificate - an official document from your university proving your degree and grade
Unconditional offer letter from one of your three chosen UK courses

document_format_rules: The undergraduate degree certificate must be an official document from your university proving your degree and grade. Undergraduate degree transcripts will not be accepted.
Chevening 'require the original documents which do not need to be translated into English.'

Reference letters must be in English. 'If the reference is in another language, upload it with a notarised English translation in one file. References without a notarised translation won't be accepted.'
Upload reference letters as two separate files to the online application system.
No file size limit, no accepted file-type list and no document date rule are published on the Chevening pages read on 1 October 2026.
UKVI, not Chevening, sets the format requirements for the student visa application: 'Provide evidence in the exact format required by UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI).'
Your passport must be valid for the full duration of your study.
selection_criteria: Quality and relevance of the submitted answers across four assessed areas: leadership and influencing skills; the ability to build professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes; reasons for making the course and university choice; and commitment to achieving the career plan and long-term impact.
Leadership and influencing: 'The top 1% of applicants awarded a Chevening Scholarship can provide examples of taking the lead and influencing others. They focus on examples with clear results.'
Networking: examples of building strong working relationships and collaboration leading to real, measurable outcomes.

Course choice: must explain, focusing only on the first choice course, how it connects to your background, career aspirations and the impact you hope to make, and how specific modules will equip you with the skills needed.
Career plan: a short, mid and long-term plan with clear, measurable goals, and a genuine willingness to collaborate with the UK on shared global and local challenges.

UK priority areas named by Chevening: promoting growth and prosperity; building climate resilience; strengthening security and stability; supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies.
For the SIDS element: the chosen course must address a national development priority or capacity shortage. The official page publishes no separate SIDS selection weighting.
Applications are first sifted against eligibility criteria, then assessed by independent reading committees.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications open 4 August 2026 and close 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. From October 2026 applications are sifted against eligibility criteria. Mid-October 2026 to January 2027: independent reading committees assess all eligible applications. Mid-February 2027: applicants shortlisted for interviews. March to April 2027: interviews take place at British embassies and high commissions. Mid-June 2027: results announced from mid-June onwards. 8 July 2027: unconditional offer deadline, 17:00 BST. September/October 2027: studies begin in the UK.

application_steps: Step 1: Check your eligibility against the published Chevening eligibility criteria and confirm you are a citizen of a participating SIDS country.
Step 2: Choose three UK master's degree courses relating to a national development priority or capacity shortage and apply to them directly at the universities.
Step 3: Prepare your references and education documents (two referees' details; reference letters and degree certificate for upload if shortlisted).
Step 4: Submit your online application via your country/territory page on chevening.org and opt in for the SIDS Scholarship.
Step 5: Wait for an interview invitation (shortlists produced by British embassies and high commissions, mid-February 2027).
Step 6: Secure an unconditional offer from a UK university by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits the Chevening application themselves through the Chevening online application system; there is no nominating agency or intermediary.
The applicant must also apply directly to each of their three chosen UK universities.
award_holder_conditions: Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after the scholarship ends.
Study on a course that addresses a national development priority or capacity shortage as defined by Chevening.
Use the knowledge and skills gained in the UK to tackle shared challenges with impact and integrity.
Adhere to the Chevening terms and conditions consented to at registration.
Scholars and fellows are ambassadors for Chevening and their home country under the Chevening Code of Conduct.

arrival_rules: Scholars typically arrive in the UK one or two weeks prior to their scheduled course start date.
You must not arrive in the UK before the start date on your student visa.
Consider your course start date, accommodation start date and visa start date when planning travel.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of a participating SIDS country - Chevening shows the participating countries only on a map on the participating-countries page.
Confirm you are applying from your country of citizenship and are not a UK resident, and do not hold British or dual British citizenship.

Pick three eligible UK master's courses that map to a named national development priority or capacity shortage: human rights/democracy/rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; or supportive societies.
Count your post-degree work hours: at least 2,800 (weeks multiplied by hours per week, typically 35-60 hours per week, 40-50 weeks per year).
Check you finished your undergraduate degree at least two years before the 6 October 2026 deadline.
Use the Chevening course finder to confirm all three courses are eligible.
Choose three different courses; duplicate courses at the same university cannot be considered.
Ask two referees now - two professional, two academic, or one of each. Not a friend or relative.
Register on chevening.org via your country/territory page and complete the eligibility checker; keep your access code safe.
Have your university application materials ready: motivation letter, English test results, proof of qualifications and references.
important_advice_for_students: Opting in for the SIDS Scholarship does not affect your chances of a standard Chevening Scholarship, so there is no downside to ticking it.
Do not pay anyone to help you apply - applying is free and Chevening does not endorse paid third parties.
Do not use AI tools to write your answers; that is strictly prohibited and Chevening detects AI-generated content.
You must apply to your UK universities yourself as well as to Chevening.
Budget for what Chevening does not pay: accommodation deposit and agency fees, utilities not in rent, travel insurance, excess baggage and any dependent's travel.
Alumni Programme Fund support is something you apply for after graduation, not money you can count on now.
Start TB test or ATAS clearance as soon as you get your conditional offer email; each certificate is valid for only six months.
common_rejection_risks: Failing or not passing the online eligibility checker.
Not being a citizen of a participating SIDS country, holding British or dual British citizenship, or residing in the UK at the time of application.
Having studied in the UK previously on a UK government-funded scholarship (five-year bar after a Chevening Fellowship).
Being an employee, relative, or recent ex-employee of a government department, the British Council, a partner UK university or their subsidiaries.
Under 2,800 hours of post-degree work experience, or entering work history wrongly.
Not completing the application form in English - the application is deemed ineligible.
Entering duplicate courses, or three courses at the same university.
Choosing a course that does not address one of the four published national development priority or capacity shortage areas.
Choosing an ineligible course: part-time, distance learning, research MRes, PhD/DPhil, under nine or over twelve months, or more than one month of study outside the UK.
Missing the reference letter upload deadline - your application is then no longer considered.
Using AI-generated, plagiarised or copied content.

records.name: Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship
records.official_source: Chevening (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office scheme), delivered by Cranfield University
records.region: United Kingdom (citizens and residents of 35 listed non-ODA eligible European countries)
records.duration: Six weeks, in two cohorts: Cohort 1 25 January - 5 March 2027; Cohort 2 15 March - 23 April 2027
records.deadline: Open for applications until 12 October 2026, at 11:00 (UTC)
records.application_period: Applications are open and close at 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026. The programme itself runs in two cohorts in 2027: 25 January - 5 March 2027 and 15 March - 23 April 2027.
records.description: The Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and delivered by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom, Shrivenham. It is a six-week applied programme for mid-career professionals from non-ODA eligible European countries who have leadership responsibilities for national or international security. Fellows study six integrated themes - global leadership in an era of complexity; people, culture and organisations; cyber resilience; AI, governance and emerging technology; decision-making under pressure; and resilience and future leadership - complete a research project, and present their findings to the FCDO in London. The award covers full programme fees, living expenses for the duration including pre-arranged accommodation, and return economy airfare; the stipend figure is not published and is confirmed in the Final Award Letter.
records.best_fit: Mid-career professionals who are citizens AND residents of one of the 35 listed European countries, hold a postgraduate qualification or equivalent professional training, have at least five years' relevant professional experience (7,200 hours) in defence, security, government, diplomacy, policing, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, academia, media, energy/infrastructure or international organisations, and can show leadership potential and a commitment to applying what they learn on return.
records.eligibility_summary: Must meet the general Chevening Fellowship eligibility criteria plus the programme-specific rules: citizenship and residence in one of 35 listed European countries, a postgraduate qualification, at least five years' relevant professional experience, and a security-related role with influence potential.
eligibility: In addition to meeting our standard eligibility criteria, you must be a citizen of and resident in one of the following countries at the point of application: Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Holy See, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.
If you live in a European overseas territory, you may apply through the relevant Chevening award scheme for the European country of which you are a citizen.
Hold a postgraduate qualification (or equivalent professional training or experience in a relevant field).
Have at least five years' relevant professional experience.

Be a mid-career professional with responsibilities for national or international security, and employed within government, public or private sector, academia, defence, security, law enforcement, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, or an international organisation.
Be working in a role with the potential to influence organisational capability, policy, strategy, or operational effectiveness within their organisation and/or country.

Be able to demonstrate leadership potential and a commitment to applying the knowledge and networks gained through the fellowship within their organisation and/or country on completion of the programme.

General Chevening Fellowship criteria: be a citizen of a fellowship-eligible country or territory; demonstrate the potential to rise to a position of leadership and influence; demonstrate the personal, intellectual, and interpersonal attributes reflecting this potential; return to your country of citizenship (country of award) for at least one year after your fellowship ends; and meet all programme-specific fellowship eligibility requirements.

General work-experience rule for Chevening Fellowships: a minimum of five years' work experience in a relevant related field, which equals 7,200 hours, calculated by multiplying weeks worked by hours per week (a working week comprises 35-60 hours and a working year comprises 40-50 weeks). 'If you do not already have the level of work experience required for your chosen fellowship programme, you will be unable to submit your application.'
You do not need to meet the work experience requirement in one period of employment; applicants can submit up to fifteen different employment periods.

records.selection_notes: Chevening publishes the four general Fellowship objectives - supporting mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offering dynamic training/professional development/research relevant to professional interests and UK international strategic priorities, increasing the breadth and diversity of Chevening awards, and supporting FCDO foreign policy priorities by creating lasting relationships with future leaders, influencers and decision-makers. For this programme the assessment is against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries. Chevening Fellowships are 'an important element of Britain's public diplomacy effort', and fellows are active in their field or subject. Chevening does not publish a separate scoring framework or interview format for this programme; applications for Chevening Scholarships follow the published sifting, reading committee, embassy shortlist and interview stages, while Chevening states that 'Application timelines for Chevening Fellowships vary.'
records.notes: Deferral: 'Applications to defer awards will only be granted in the case of pregnancy.' Extensions: 'Extensions to the original fellowship duration may be permitted in exceptional circumstances, but the total duration must not exceed 12 months. All extensions are subject to the availability of funds and assessed on a case-by-case basis. Extensions are not automatic and should not be assumed.' Return home: 'You are expected to return to your home country for at least one year on completion of your fellowship.' Dependants: 'All Chevening Awards are calculated to support fellow costs only. There are no financial or welfare provisions for dependants of Chevening Fellows. It is strongly advised that Fellows do not bring dependants to the UK', and 'The Chevening Programme will not endorse the visa applications of, nor provide travel for, dependants.' Other conditions: no transfer to any course other than that confirmed in the Final Award Letter; no other publicly funded award during the fellowship period; approval required before any part-time employment or internship outside the approved programme; cannot serve as an official government representative during the fellowship; must not be outside the UK for more than 30 days in total (pro-rata: 3-month tenure up to 7 days outside the UK), and absences without prior notice may suspend the stipend or end the award; must cite Chevening Fellowships in publications; breach may result in withdrawal of the award. Stipend suspension may occur if fellowship terms and conditions are not complied with, if compulsory documentation is not returned, or if the Fellow elects to return home early and submit work from overseas.

official_details.description: The Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship is funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and delivered by Cranfield University at the Defence Academy of the United Kingdom, Shrivenham. It is open to all non-ODA eligible European countries and is designed for mid-career professionals from across Europe who have demonstrated leadership potential in security and defence. Through six weeks of teaching, discussion, practical exercises, site visits, individual research, and collaborative learning, fellows develop practical insight into leadership, organisational resilience, governance, strategic decision-making, cyber resilience, artificial intelligence, and international collaboration. Throughout the programme fellows work on a research project addressing a relevant policy, leadership, organisational, or security challenge, receive academic support, and present their findings to the FCDO in London at the end of the fellowship.
purpose: Develop leaders capable of operating effectively within complex and rapidly changing security and defence contexts.
Strengthen fellows' understanding of the strategic challenges facing governments, international organisations, and public institutions through an interdisciplinary and applied learning experience.
Build practical insight into leadership, organisational resilience, governance, strategic decision-making, cyber resilience, artificial intelligence, and international collaboration.
Create lasting professional networks across Europe and the UK.

Serve Chevening's stated Fellowship objectives: support mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offer training/research relevant to professional interests and the UK's international strategic priorities, and support FCDO public diplomacy and foreign policy priorities through lasting relationships with future leaders, influencers and decision-makers.

general_eligibility: Chevening Fellowships are aimed at mid-career professionals who have reached a position of influence and want to increase their knowledge, networks, and potential through tailored short courses, research, or professional placements at UK institutions.
Fellows are often people of significant standing in their home countries and will usually have completed some element(s) of higher education already.
Eligible work experience types include full-time employment, part-time employment, voluntary work, and paid or unpaid internships.
If you have held more than fifteen positions, enter the periods which make up the greatest number of hours worked.
You do not need to resign from your work position, but it is your responsibility to ensure your employer will release you.
Chevening Fellowship programmes typically have varying eligibility requirements; programme-specific requirements are on individual programme pages.
ineligibility_conditions: Hold British or dual British citizenship (unless you are a citizen of a British Overseas Territory).

Have received UK Government scholarship funding (including Chevening) within the last five years - 'You will only be eligible to apply for a Chevening Fellowship after a period of five years following the completion of your first UK Government-funded scholarship.'

Be an employee, a former employee, or relative of an employee of His Majesty's Government, or have been within the last two years from the opening of Chevening applications (including the FCDO, all British Embassies/High Commissions, the Home Office, the Ministry of Defence, the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy, the Department for International Trade and the UKVI), the British Council, or a sponsoring UK university. Individuals contracted to work on any British Council programme or project, and their relatives, are ineligible.

Employees, former employees, or relatives of an employee of Chevening partner organisations may apply, but if that employment took place within the last two years you cannot receive a Chevening partner award from the organisation you work for, previously worked for, or are affiliated with through relatives.
Not be a citizen AND resident of one of the 35 listed European countries at the point of application - the fellowship is open to all non-ODA eligible European countries only.

Not meet the five-year (7,200 hour) work experience minimum: 'If you do not already have the level of work experience required for your chosen fellowship programme, you will be unable to submit your application.'

Immediate relatives are defined as parents or step-parents, siblings or step-siblings, children or step-children, spouse, civil partner or unmarried (where the couple have been in a relationship akin to marriage or civil partnership for at least two years).

alerts.message: Check the five-year bar: you are only eligible to apply for a Chevening Fellowship after five years following completion of your first UK Government-funded scholarship.
You must be a citizen and resident of one of the 35 listed European countries. Verify your country is on the list before spending time on the form.
Confirm the automatic work-experience total reaches 7,200 hours - below the minimum you will be unable to submit.
Return the acceptance form; it is what activates your cash card, stipend and award.
Attend the pre-departure briefing at your British embassy or high commission.
Attend the Chevening welcome reception and/or induction, give the Secretariat a UK address and email, and do not be outside the UK for more than 30 days in total.
You are expected to return to your home country for at least one year, and must complete the departure survey and feedback session.

submission_workflow: Go to the Chevening apply page for your European country and select the Chevening Europe Defence and Security Fellowship.
Register on the Chevening online application system and pass the eligibility checker.
Complete each application section, including your employment history with enough detail for the system to calculate your hours.
State your research interest and how you will apply the fellowship on your return.
Disclose any other award applications on the form.
Submit before 11:00 (UTC) on 12 October 2026.
post_award_requirements: Return to your home country for at least one year on completion of the fellowship.
Attend the pre-departure briefing before travel and the Chevening welcome reception and/or induction on arrival.
Give the Secretariat a UK address and email on arrival and an overseas address and email at the end of the award.

Inform your programme officer immediately of any change of address (even temporarily), change of marital status, injury or illness, legal action, or any absence of more than four days at one time from your place of study.
Return any form or request for information promptly; failing to do so can result in your stipend being withheld.
Complete and return all report requests, surveys and the arrival and departure surveys.
Remain in the UK, observing the travel allowance, for the duration of the fellowship.
Seek Secretariat approval before any part-time employment or internship outside the approved programme.
Acknowledge Chevening in any publications produced during or after your UK visit.
Attend the feedback session at the end of the award.
questions_to_ask_host: Where exactly is the pre-arranged accommodation, given the programme is delivered at Shrivenham? The Chevening page states accommodation 'close to Oxford', which appears inconsistent with the Cranfield/Shrivenham delivery location - confirm with the host before accepting.
What is the adjusted stipend amount for my cohort given that accommodation forms part of the award?
Which cohort am I expected to join, 25 January - 5 March 2027 or 15 March - 23 April 2027, and how is that decided?
Does my research project carry a research allowance, and what does it cover?
What visa route will Cranfield University sponsor for a six-week programme, and what is the medical clearance requirement?
Who is my Chevening programme officer, and how do I contact them after arriving in the UK?
How do I report an absence, and what evidence of immigration status will you require from me?

records.name: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship (2027 competition)
records.official_source: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation
records.region: Canada (Canadian students may study abroad; international students must be enrolled at a Canadian university)

records.application_period: Applications open September 1, 2026 and close November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET. records.description: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship is a three-year doctoral award for students with an outstanding academic record whose humanities and social sciences research aligns with at least one of the Foundation's four themes. It provides an annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies, plus an annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years for research and travel. The application period for the 2027 competition runs from September 1 to November 6, 2026, so the competition is open on 2026-10-01. Scholars also gain membership in a multidisciplinary community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors and structured mentorship programming.
records.best_fit: First- or second-year PhD students in the humanities and social sciences whose research maps onto one of the Foundation's four themes (Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment), who already have an outstanding academic record and who want mentorship and a non-academic network alongside funding.
records.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students in the first or second year of a PhD at the time of application whose research is broadly humanities/social sciences and aligns with at least one of the Foundation's four themes, who are either a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university, a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada, or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university.
eligibility: At the time of application the applicant must be in the first year or the second year of a PhD program.
The field of study must be broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and address issues relevant to Canada's future.
The PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment.

The applicant must be one of the following: a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university.
Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability, assessed across the whole application including transcripts and letters of recommendation.
Three letters of reference are required: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia.
There is no age limit to apply.
There is no requirement to be fluent in both official languages; applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English.
coverage: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work
Membership in the Foundation's community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors
Lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network of more than 500 individuals
Mentorship and experiential learning: meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences
benefits: Participation in Foundation programming such as summer schools, retreats and public conferences
Access to Mentors matched through the Mentorship Program (Mentors are non-academic leaders matched with one or two Scholars per year)
Networking and professional development through interaction with Fellows and Scholars across disciplines and sectors
Interviews and group meetings conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference

records.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English. The Foundation states: "Do I need to be fluent in both French and English to receive the scholarship? No. You do not need to be fluent in both official languages. However, you must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English." The application form may be completed in English or French, in one language only, and referees may respond in either language regardless of the language of the application.
application_method: Read the published eligibility criteria and confirm your profile meets all requirements.
Complete the short eligibility screening form on the SmartSimple portal (https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca) by October 2, 2026.
Wait for the Foundation to confirm eligibility and grant access to the full application form.
Attend a mandatory information session in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026.
Complete the full application form, including the research proposal and the Special Circumstances section where relevant.

Submit the complete application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
Receive a confirmation email acknowledging submission once your application is received.
records.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on academic excellence, the clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. Only applications meeting the programme's eligibility criteria are assessed. Applicants who pass review are notified by email; all other applicants are informed at the end of the application review period. Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference. Final decisions are approved by the Board of Directors. The application form is removed from the portal once the competition ends; the confirmation email is the only proof of receipt.
records.notes: The Scholarship is a three-year program. It is not deferrable in the sense that the value is adjusted: Scholars may accept other awards, but the value of the Trudeau Scholarship is adjusted based on amounts received from other organizations, institutions or universities, and all additional sources of income must be declared annually. Regardless of other funding, every Scholar receives the full annual $20,000 research, travel and networking allowance and a minimum of $25,000 from the annual stipend. For Scholars studying outside Canada who receive external funding in foreign currency, the Foundation converts that amount into Canadian dollars; the location of study does not affect the Scholarship amount. Scholars may work part-time (up to 20 hours per week) while continuing to receive full benefits, including university or campus-based roles such as research assistant, teaching assistant or lecturer. Scholars may suspend the Scholarship for up to one year for parental, medical, personal or professional leave; the Foundation states Scholars are not employees of the Foundation and it does not provide paid parental leave, and payments are paused until the Scholar re-enrols full-time. Funds begin only after Board of Directors approval, signature of the funding agreement and submission of required documentation. The annual Scholarship is disbursed in three instalments per year. There is no return-home requirement for Canadian students studying abroad or for international students.

Confirm you are a Canadian student at a university anywhere, or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university. International students living outside Canada and students at non-Canadian universities (other than Canadians) are ineligible.

Book a slot in the mandatory information session in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026.
Line up three referees now: your PhD supervisor, a second academic referee, and one person outside academia. Exactly three, no more.
Brief your three referees on the deadline of October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET and on the fact that they must upload through your application file.
Choose the language of your application (English or French) and use it throughout — the form must be in one language only.

important_advice_for_students: Treat October 2, 2026 as the real deadline. Everything else in the process depends on passing the eligibility screening first.

Do not wait until November to approach referees. The reference deadline (October 30) is a week before the application deadline, and letters cannot be submitted independently — they must be attached inside your file.

If your thesis supervisor has not been chosen or does not know you well, you may ask a former supervisor or another professor to act as referee, and the Foundation strongly recommends explaining this in the Special Circumstances section.

Do not bother over-polishing referee selection on prestige. The Foundation asks for referees who collectively cover academic, research, community involvement and personal qualities, and explicitly says a family member cannot serve as referee.

Budget your expectation realistically: the $50,000 is a ceiling, not a fixed award, and it is reduced by other funding you hold, with a guaranteed floor of $25,000 from the annual stipend. The $20,000 research/travel allowance is never reduced.

If you are studying outside Canada, be aware foreign-currency external funding is converted to Canadian dollars when the Foundation calculates the value of the award — the geography does not increase the amount.
Decide early whether you want to work. Part-time work up to 20 hours per week is allowed with no reduction in benefits.

If you may need parental, medical, personal or professional leave, note that the Scholarship can be suspended for up to one year but the Foundation does not pay parental leave and payments pause until you re-enrol full-time.

records.description: The UBC International Scholars Program funds international students who enter UBC directly from secondary school for their first undergraduate degree and who show both exceptional academic achievement and a significant level of financial need. Awards are need-based rather than fixed-value: UBC states that applicants are automatically considered for whichever of four awards they qualify for, and that individual award amounts are not selected by the applicant. Only the Vantage One Excellence Award is described as ranging in value up to the full cost of a student's academic program and living expenses, so full funding is not established for the programme as a whole.

records.selection_notes: UBC states there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria. As part of the evaluation process a financial assessment is carried out, reviewing documents outlining family gross income, expenses and family assets. Applicants are assessed on demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, and outstanding academic performance (all As or equivalent standard). Applicants may be invited to a video interview to share more about themselves and reflect on past educational and leadership experiences beyond the written application. You do not select which award you wish to receive; the team automatically considers you for the awards you are eligible for. Applicants who apply to the International Scholars Program will not be considered for merit-based awards.
records.notes: Non-renewable status, deferral and return-home requirements are not published on the programme page. There is no published clinical restriction, but the following degrees are explicitly not eligible for UBC International Scholars Program awards: Bachelor of Nursing degree (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management degree, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions. Applicants may only be considered for either UBC's merit-based or its financial need-based award programme. Applicants must hold a Canadian study permit. Applicants started shortly before the deadline are less likely to be successful. Housing should not be applied for until award decisions are released, because the housing application deadline is May 1.

official_details.description: The UBC International Scholars Program is for international students who have demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, outstanding academic performance, and who require meaningful financial support to attend UBC. By bringing together Scholars from diverse countries and cultures, the programme fosters a vibrant and globally connected learning community. There are four award categories: the Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award, the Donald A. Wehrung International Student Award, the International Impact Award, and the Vantage One Excellence Award.
purpose: Recognise exceptional prospective international undergraduate students who demonstrate superior academic achievement and exemplary leadership skills that support and empower others through collaboration, empathy and active listening.

Recognise outstanding international undergraduate students from impoverished or war-torn areas who have achieved academic excellence under challenging circumstances and who would be unable to attend university without significant financial assistance.

Support exceptional students who have demonstrated leadership and commitment to and solutions for sustainability and climate change, natural resource conservation and management, social justice, equity and inclusion, or societal health and wellness.
Offer the Vantage One Excellence Award to academically outstanding international students who do not yet meet the English Language Admission Standard for direct admission to UBC.
Build a globally connected learning community of Scholars from diverse countries and cultures.
Provide dedicated advising, developmental support and skill building to Scholars over the course of their degree.

Applicants do not select which award they will receive; the team automatically considers them for the awards they are eligible for. Applicants who apply are not considered for merit-based awards. Results are released on a rolling basis throughout February to April, and by early to mid-April applicants are told whether they received an award.
