application_steps: 1. Set up the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission and register the consortium (step 1).
2. Write and submit the pre-proposal in English on the mandatory template, with the topic and French partners' TRL levels, before 12/05/2026 (closed step).
3. Wait for the step 1 evaluation and the M-ERA.NET invitation, which requires a recommendation by at least three funding agencies from at least three countries.
4. Assemble Annexe 1 with the Partner profiles and the CVs of all consortium participants.
5. Write the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, keeping the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives unchanged and respecting the 60% and 70% person-month caps.
6. Set the ANR aid request within the published ranges and, if applicable, plan the 20 000 € European-preparation Work Package and budget.
7. On receipt of the ANR email, deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
8. Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET and keep the confirmations.
9. If a change is needed, obtain acceptance from the funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
applicant_submission_route: Central deposit on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site (https://www.m-era.net/joint-calls/joint-call-2026) by the project coordinator, in English.
For ANR aid at step 2: parallel deposit on the ANR submission site (https://aap.agencerecherche.fr/), with the exact link and deadline communicated by email to the partners requesting ANR aid.
At step 1 the ANR does not require a deposit on its site, though other national or regional agencies may require a parallel national application under their own rules.
M-ERA.NET contact: office(at)m-era.net. ANR contacts: Léa Gardie (Lea.GARDIE@agencerecherche.fr) and Larissa Chaperman (Larissa.CHAPERMAN@agencerecherche.fr).
official_details.application_portal: https://www.m-era.net/joint-calls/joint-call-2026 (central deposit) and https://aap.agencerecherche.fr/ (ANR parallel deposit, step 2 only)
award_holder_conditions: Only the eligible costs of the partners that requested ANR aid are financed, and the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation and eligible cost sheet no. 3.
A consortium agreement is mandatory except where the call provides otherwise, under the conditions of ANR Financial Regulation sheet no. 4.
Requested aid amounts may not be increased between the two steps; non-conformity with the aid limits or with ANR budgetary adjustments renders the project ineligible.

The 20 000 € European-preparation supplement is conditional on adequate planning and activities within the M-ERA.NET project with a dedicated Work Package and budget under an ANR-funded partner, on activities leading to a research proposal involving consortium members in continuity with the M-ERA.NET work, and on the follow-up targeting clearly identified FP10 calls coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; it is subject to a final assessment and a supplementary deliverable to the ANR.

Immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL with the mandated ANR acknowledgement, FAIR data approach, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence software with Software Heritage archiving.
Compliance with the national research professions deontology charter and the ANR deontology and scientific-integrity charter, ensured by French scientific leads for all partners.
Nagoya Protocol compliance for genetic resources, with the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment where applicable.

Annual or periodic reporting to both the ANR (via aap.agencerecherche.fr/) and M-ERA.NET (via the central platform or monitoring@m-era.net), with intermediate and final reports on the deadlines set in the call text and/or the aid award decision.
Any change affecting the whole project, such as extensions or consortium modifications, must be approved by all partners, their respective funding agencies and M-ERA.NET.
A negative SHFDS/MESR opinion under the PPST prevents selection of the project.
Possible transmission of proposals and project documents to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and possible mandatory publication by certain national funders.
timeline_rules: Ouverture de l'appel : 31/03/2026 à 09:00 CEST.
Étape 1 (pré-propositions) : 12/05/2026, 12 h 00 (CEST) - closed.
Étape 2 (propositions détaillées) : 18/11/2026, 12 h 00 (CET) - the only open window on 2026-10-01, and only for coordinators invited after step 1.
Information webinar on 18 March 2026, 12:00-14:00 CET, with presentations and recording on the M-ERA.NET call site.
A pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries to be invited to step 2.
Any change between steps must be accepted by the funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
Data Management Plan within 6 months of the scientific start of the project.
The ANR parallel deposit link and deadline are communicated later by email to partners requesting ANR aid.

official_contacts.general: Call secretariat: office(at)m-era.net. ANR scientific project officers: Léa Gardie (Lea.GARDIE@agencerecherche.fr) and Larissa Chaperman (Larissa.CHAPERMAN@agencerecherche.fr). ANR Data Protection Officer: dpd@agencerecherche.fr. For the applicable funding rate and cost types: categorisationbeneficiaire@anr.fr.

official_application_route: Central deposit in English on https://www.m-era.net/joint-calls/joint-call-2026 by the project coordinator, using the mandatory M-ERA.NET templates.

Parallel ANR deposit at step 2 for partners requesting ANR aid on the ANR submission site (https://aap.agencerecherche.fr/), with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated by email.
Other participating national or regional agencies may require a parallel national or regional application under their own rules.
Monitoring: ANR via https://aap.agencerecherche.fr/; M-ERA.NET via the central platform or monitoring@m-era.net.
official_details.region: France within a transnational European and associated consortium (EU Member States, Horizon Europe associated countries and further participating countries listed in Annex 3 of the call text)
coverage: ANR aid to French partners of 15 000 € to 180 000 € (non-coordinating) or up to 250 000 € (coordinating), total cap 350 000 € per project with several ANR partners
Optional 20 000 € per project for European project-preparation (FP10) activities, raising the caps to 200 000 / 270 000 / 370 k€
Up to 36 months of project activity, funded through each partner's national or regional organisation

application_readiness_checklist: First check whether you submitted a pre-proposal by 12/05/2026 and were recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries. If not, this call is closed to you: the 18/11/2026 date accepts only invited coordinators.

Confirm the work sits in one of the four ANR-eligible topics (materials for energy storage and distribution; materials for energy conversion; innovative functional materials with designed architectures; next-generation materials for electronics). Topics 3 (surfaces, coatings and interfaces) and 5 (materials for environmental challenges) are explicitly ineligible for ANR aid.
Verify the final TRL for the ANR-funded partner stays at or below 5 and that the work is positioned in the fundamental research segment or the first applied research segment.

Check the consortium math: at least 3 funded partners from 3 different countries with at least 2 EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries; no single partner above 60% and no single country above 70% of person-months; ineligible or non-invited partners below 15% of total effort.

Set the ANR aid request within 15 000 €-180 000 € (non-coordinating) or up to 250 000 € (coordinating), total 350 000 € max; if you want the 20 000 € European-preparation supplement, plan a dedicated Work Package and budget under an ANR-funded partner now, because the supplement is assessed on that planning.
Do not change the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives at step 2, and do not try to add partners from new countries.
Use the mandatory M-ERA.NET templates exactly; exceeding the page limit is the most common avoidable disqualification.
Prepare Annexe 1 with the Partner profiles and the CVs of every consortium participant, in English.
Watch for the ANR email with the ANR submission link and deadline for the parallel deposit, and make sure the two deposits carry identical information.

Get your institution's approval in writing: the scientific lead formally commits that their hierarchy approved the submission, and the ANR may send the list of its deposits to laboratory directors and the institution's administrative managers.
Contact your institution's defence and security officer about PPST before depositing, since the consortium includes foreign partners and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion blocks selection.
important_advice_for_students: Individuals cannot apply. The applicant is an institution and the money goes to a French partner's managing institution; there is no individual scholarship, tuition waiver or stipend created by this call.

If you are a doctoral student working on battery or advanced-materials R&D, your realistic route is employment on a funded partner's budget inside a consortium that has already passed step 1. Use Partnersearch and the Success Stories pages to identify active M-ERA.NET projects, then approach the French coordinator.
Do not invest time in drafting a proposal if your group did not submit a pre-proposal by 12 May 2026; watch the 2027 edition of this ERA-NET instead.

If your institution is new to EU project preparation, the 20 000 € supplement is the cheapest route to an FP10 proposal, and it is easier to obtain when the Work Package and budget are written into the step 2 proposal rather than added later.
common_rejection_risks: Not having been invited after step 1, or having missed the step 1 pre-proposal deadline of 12/05/2026.
A topic outside the four ANR-eligible ones, or a proposal whose relevance to the chosen topic is not clearly justified from step 1.
Final TRL above 5 for the ANR-funded partner, or work outside the fundamental/first applied research segments.
A single partner above 60% or a single country above 70% of person-months.
Ineligible or non-invited partners accounting for 15% or more of total effort, which discards the whole proposal.
Exceeding the page limit or otherwise modifying the mandatory M-ERA.NET templates.
Adding partners from new countries at step 2, or modifying the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives.
A similar proposal already under ANR evaluation or ANR-funded, or a second ANR request by the same researcher in this call.
Requested aid outside the ranges, or an increase between the two steps.
Partners subject to EU sanctions (Russia, Belarus, certain Ukrainian territories), or a negative SHFDS/MESR PPST opinion.
Missing the parallel ANR deposit at step 2, or information differing between the M-ERA.NET and ANR deposits.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All costs of the non-French partners, which are funded by their own national or regional agencies, not by the ANR.
French partners working on the two non-eligible topics, who may only participate on their own funds.
Work above TRL 5 or outside the fundamental and first applied research segments, which is outside ANR scope.
The difference between the requested aid and the amount actually granted, which depends on the ANR funding rate and the individual partner's economic-activity categorisation.
Any co-funding from the institution: the ANR aid is capped and does not cover the full budget of a large consortium.
document_audit: Detailed proposal: mandatory M-ERA.NET template, in English, on the central site, by 18/11/2026 12:00 CET.
Annexe 1: mandatory, in English, with Partner profiles and the CVs of all consortium participants.
Parallel ANR deposit on aap.agencerecherche.fr with information identical to the central deposit; link and deadline by email.
Theme statement and the TRL levels of each French partner's tasks, clearly indicated.
Justification of relevance to the chosen ANR-eligible topic, required from step 1.
Consortium agreement (accord de consortium) per ANR Financial Regulation sheet no. 4, unless the call provides otherwise.
Where applicable: the economic-activity declaration form for the applicable funding rate and cost types, and the Nagoya Due Diligence Declaration receipt.

referee_tracking.instructions: Experts are appointed by the call secretariat, not nominated by applicants. They evaluate centrally at both steps; applicants are not asked for referees. The ANR adds its horizontal objectives and may request the evaluation criteria in translation.

alerts.message: Confirm you passed step 1 (pre-proposal by 12/05/2026 and a recommendation by at least three agencies in at least three countries). If you did not, the 18/11/2026 deadline is not open to you.
Submit any required change to the funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, i.e. well before 18/11/2026 12:00 CET.

alerts.trigger: As soon as the ANR email arrives

Decide on the 20 000 € European-preparation supplement now; it needs a dedicated Work Package and budget under an ANR-funded partner, and it is judged on the adequacy of that planning.
Talk to your institution's defence and security officer about PPST: with foreign partners in the consortium, a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection.

Write the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template, keeping the pre-proposal's objectives unchanged and respecting the 60% and 70% person-month caps and the TRL 5 limit.
Assemble Annexe 1 with Partner profiles and all CVs, in English.
Set the ANR aid request within the published ranges and, if applicable, plan the 20 000 € European-preparation Work Package and budget.
On receipt of the ANR email, deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 12:00 CET and keep the confirmations.
If a change is required, obtain written acceptance from the funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
post_award_requirements: Deliver a Data Management Plan within 6 months of the scientific start of the project.

Guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY and deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL with the mandated ANR acknowledgement sentence and the ANR project reference with a Crossref DOI.

Adopt a FAIR approach to research data, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv citing the ANR project reference, and release software under a free licence with archiving in Software Heritage.
Submit intermediate and final progress reports to the ANR via aap.agencerecherche.fr and to the M-ERA.NET follow-up team via the central platform or monitoring@m-era.net.
Conclude and transmit the consortium agreement where required under ANR Financial Regulation sheet no. 4.
Obtain approval from all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET for any change affecting the whole project, such as extensions or consortium modifications.

Ensure compliance with the Nagoya Protocol where genetic resources are used and provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the final payment date where applicable.
Take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research where relevant and give equitable visibility to the work produced.

records.name: Bourse d'excellence WBI IN (WBI Excellence Scholarship for international researchers — Wallonia/Brussels postdoctoral stay)
records.official_source: Wallonie-Bruxelles International (WBI), Service des bourses internationales
records.region: Belgium (host: Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles institutions in Wallonia and Brussels; applicants: researchers from all countries, WBI states 'WBI accueille des chercheurs du monde entier')
records.duration: Long duration: postdoctoral level, minimum 1 year, renewable once. Short duration: postdoctoral level, 1 to 3 months, renewable provided the 3-year interval between two stays is respected.
records.deadline: Long duration: 'Au plus tard le 1er février (UTC/GMT +1) précédant l'année académique durant laquelle le séjour est souhaité' with departure at the latest 1 October. Short duration: 'Au plus tard le 1er octobre (UTC/GMT +2) précédant les séjours prévus entre mars et juillet' and 'Au plus tard le 1er avril (UTC/GMT +2) précédant les séjours prévus entre septembre et février'.
records.application_period: Continuous annual cycle with three separate cut-offs. Short-duration stay of March–July 2027: file due 1 October 2026 (this is the cycle open on 2026-10-01). Long-duration stay for academic year 2027-2028: file due 1 February 2027. Short-duration stay of September 2027–February 2028: file due 1 April 2027.
records.description: WBI funds researchers from any country who hold a doctorate awarded by a foreign institution to carry out a postdoctoral research programme at a higher-education institution organised or subsidised by the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. The support is a net monthly grant of 2,120 EUR paid for the duration of the research programme, plus return international economy-class travel and health, civil-liability and repatriation insurance. WBI states explicitly that this is a monthly grant and not a salary, and that it is awarded as a mobility allowance. Priority research themes are the Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness clusters, though any field including humanities, fundamental or applied sciences will be considered.
records.best_fit: Researchers of any nationality who completed a doctorate outside Belgium and want a postdoctoral research stay in Wallonia or Brussels, at a maximum of 12 months spent in Belgium during the three years before applying.
records.eligibility_summary: Any researcher from any country holding a doctorate from a foreign higher-education institution who plans a postdoctoral research programme at a Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles higher-education institution, with no more than 12 months spent in Belgium in the preceding three years.
eligibility: Researchers from all countries are accepted: 'WBI accueille des chercheurs du monde entier'.

Must hold a doctorate (diplôme de l'enseignement supérieur de docteur) delivered by a foreign institution, or be a doctoral candidate still awaiting the degree (proof of success must be supplied by the published dates).
The postdoctoral programme must take place at a higher-education institution organised or subsidised by the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.
IN candidates may have spent at most 12 months in Belgium during the three years preceding their application.
coverage: Net monthly grant of 2,120 EUR for the duration of the research programme (mobility allowance, not a salary)
Return international travel in economy class from home to the place of assignment, based on a simulation established by WBI
Health care insurance
Civil liability insurance
Repatriation insurance
benefits: Three insurances (health care, civil liability, repatriation) are taken in charge and are named separately from the grant and travel support
Travel and other non-grant costs are reimbursed, but only against a claim declaration accompanied by the supporting documents
The grant is paid monthly
Long-duration grants may be renewed once; short-duration grants may be renewed subject to the 3-year gap between stays
requirements: Application file must be complete, signed and dated
Research project written in a maximum of 4 pages
At least 2 recommendation letters on the mandatory template, sent by the referees directly to WBI
Invitation letter or agreement from the host university and the supervising research promoter
Proof that the doctorate was obtained abroad (mandatory for IN candidates)
If the project does not fit a Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness cluster, the applicant must comment on the possible societal impact of the project for Wallonia and the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
Excellence IN grants may not be combined with an F.R.S.-FNRS grant or mandate
application_method: Prepare the complete file: application form, Annexes 1 to 6 and the research project, as a single and unique PDF excluding the recommendation letters
Send the complete file by email to the International Scholarships Department at bourses@wbi.be; if the annexes are too voluminous, add an online sharing link (Google Drive, WeTransfer, Dropbox, etc.)
Ensure that the file is complete, signed and dated before sending it
Have at least 2 referees email their recommendation letters, written on the mandatory template, directly to WBI

If still a doctoral candidate, supply proof of successful defence by the published date (15 July for long-duration grants of a September–August stay; 1 December for short-duration stays of March–July; 1 July for short-duration stays of September–February)
Respond to WBI within 7 calendar days of the result to accept or decline the grant
Once selected, follow the practical guide for scholarship holders sent with the grant decision
records.selection_notes: Five-stage process: administrative verification of admissibility; admissible files passed to the selection jury; jury ranking sent to WBI; WBI allocates the grants according to available budget; WBI communicates results. The jury is composed of members of the Fonds de la Recherche Scientifique (F.R.S.-FNRS), the Direction générale opérationnel 'Economie, emploi et recherche' (DGO6) of the Walloon public service, and WBI. Files are ranked in three categories A–B–C; only files rated A (with sub-categories A- and A+) by at least one jury member can be selected. Selection is based on: link to Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness clusters; recommendation letters; academic records; interest of the field for Walloon universities and research centres; scientific publications; added value of the intended mobility; professional career path. Results are normally issued in early June for long-duration grants, early January for short-duration stays of March–July, and early July for short-duration stays of September–February.
records.notes: The grant is explicitly NOT a salary ('ne constitue aucunement un salaire') and is awarded as a mobility allowance. Long-duration grants may be renewed once; short-duration grants are renewable only while the 3-year interval between two stays is respected. No return-home obligation is published. Award holders must acknowledge WBI support with the wording 'Avec le soutien de Wallonie-Bruxelles International' and the WBI logo on any public document, and must submit periodic reports, a final mission report and an ALUMNI form. There is no clinical or field restriction published for this programme.

official_details.description: Wallonie-Bruxelles International supports researchers from all countries who hold a doctorate delivered by a foreign institution and who wish to carry out a postdoctoral programme within a Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles higher-education institution. The support consists of a monthly grant, not a salary, for the duration of the research programme; return travel costs are also covered.
purpose: Encourage the development of research in Wallonia in the themes of the Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness clusters
Encourage networking between research institutions
Provide expertise that does not yet exist in Wallonia
Support research and innovation development
study_type: Postdoctoral research programme
official_details.degree_award: Not a degree award. This is a postdoctoral research stay; no degree or diploma is conferred by the grant.
official_details.duration: Long duration: minimum 1 year, renewable once. Short duration: 1 to 3 months, renewable provided the 3-year interval between two stays is respected.
official_details.application_cycle: Annual, with three published cut-offs: 1 February (long duration), 1 October preceding March–July short stays, and 1 April preceding September–February short stays.
official_details.deadline_central_display: Short-duration scholarships for stays planned between March and July: 'Au plus tard le 1er octobre (UTC/GMT +2) précédant les séjours prévus entre mars et juillet'.

official_details.selection_notes: Five stages: (1) administrative verification of admissibility; (2) admissible files transmitted to the selection jury; (3) the jury sends its ranking to WBI; (4) WBI allocates the grants according to available budgetary resources; (5) WBI communicates the results. Jury members come from the F.R.S.-FNRS, the DGO6 'Economie, emploi et recherche' of the Walloon public service, and WBI. Files are ranked A-B-C; only files obtaining an A grade (with A- and A+ sub-categories) from at least one jury member are selectable. Results normally arrive early June (long duration), early January (short duration, March-July stays) and early July (short duration, September-February stays). The candidate then has 7 calendar days to respond so as not to penalise stand-in candidates. Priority research themes published: transport and logistics; mechanical engineering; life sciences; agro-industry; aeronautics-space; environmental technologies. Any other domain, whether humanities, fundamental or applied, will be considered.

records.name: AFdoc – Aides à la formation doctorale (FNR PhD funding scheme)
records.official_source: Fonds National de la Recherche (FNR), Luxembourg
records.region: Luxembourg (funding body). Host institutions are either public PhD-awarding institutions abroad, or Luxembourg-based private companies active in R&D and accredited by the Minister responsible for the Economy. Applicants of any nationality may apply provided they can demonstrate a clear link to Luxembourg.
records.duration: Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training.
records.deadline: First call: 'a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET'. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, and the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET.
records.application_period: The very first call was launched mid-September 2026 with a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, so the scheme is open on 2026-10-01. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, funding decisions are communicated in July and funded projects must start no later than 1 February of the following year; the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET, decisions are communicated in March of the following year and funded projects must start no later than 1 October.
records.description: AFdoc is a new PhD funding scheme launched by the Luxembourg National Research Fund following the entry into force of the new FNR law on 1 August 2026. It supports talented doctoral candidates with a clear link to Luxembourg who undertake PhD projects in established research environments abroad, or through collaborations involving Luxembourg-based companies active in R&D. Funding is granted to the eligible Host Institution, which employs the selected candidate under an employment contract, and may cover up to four years of doctoral training. Based on the salary index applicable on 1 June 2026, the maximum annual salary contribution is EUR 54,574 including employer charges, social security and pension contributions.
records.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who already hold a Master's degree, can demonstrate a clear link to Luxembourg, and want to do a funded PhD at a public university abroad or at a Luxembourg R&D company working with a public PhD-awarding institution.
records.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates holding a Master's who can demonstrate a clear link to Luxembourg, will be enrolled in a PhD programme by the project start date, do not already hold a PhD, and are not in receipt of an old-age pension.
eligibility: Researchers at the career stage 'PhD Candidate (with Masters)'

Applicants must meet cumulative eligibility conditions: demonstrate a link to Luxembourg, be enrolled in a PhD programme by the project start date, not already hold a PhD, and not benefit from an old-age pension
Each applicant may submit one proposal per call
Bottom-up: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible
coverage: Maximum annual salary contribution of EUR 54,574 per funded doctoral candidate, including employer charges, social security and pension contributions, based on the salary index applicable on 1 June 2026
Up to four years of doctoral training
benefits: Funding is paid to the Host Institution, which employs the candidate as beneficiary under an employment contract, so the doctoral position is a job

Bottom-up scheme: projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities, provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner
Company-based PhDs can be hosted by a Luxembourg R&D company as long as the research involves a public-sector PhD-awarding institution such as the University of Luxembourg or a university abroad
requirements: Demonstrate a clear link to Luxembourg
Be enrolled in a PhD programme by the project start date
Not already hold a PhD
Not be in receipt of an old-age pension
Submit only one proposal per call
Applications must be submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System
records.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System.
application_method: Prepare the proposal using the AFdoc call documents (application guidelines, selection guidelines, project description template and commitment letter)
Submit the proposal in English through the FNR Grant Management System at https://grants.fnr.lu/login
Submit no more than one proposal per call
Wait for the funding decision in March of the following year (second/September call) or July (first/April call)
records.selection_notes: Eligible proposals are assessed on the scientific quality and potential of the project, the applicant's profile and potential, the quality of the Host Institution, supervision and training environment, and the expected impact of the project. AFdoc follows a bottom-up approach: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible, and projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner. The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects.
records.notes: Tuition fees and related research costs are not eligible. No renewal, deferral, return-home or clinical restriction rule is published on the instrument page. Because funding goes to the Host Institution and the candidate is employed, the award is a salary rather than a stipend; the beneficiary has an employment relationship with the host, not with the FNR.

Funding is granted to eligible Host Institutions, which employ the selected doctoral candidates as beneficiaries through an employment contract. Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training, with a maximum annual salary contribution of EUR 54,574 including employer charges, social security and pension contributions.

records.name: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
records.official_source: Government of Flanders — Flanders Trainee Programme (Departement Buitenlandse Zaken)
records.region: Belgium (Government of Flanders). The internship itself is taken at the headquarters or a field office of a qualifying multilateral organisation within the jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders. Published monthly grant amounts cover Antwerp, Brussels, Luxembourg, Geneva, London, Montreal, Nairobi, New York, Paris, Pretoria, Rome, Strasbourg, The Hague, Vienna, Warsaw, Washington D.C., Bonn, Madrid, Stockholm, Copenhagen, Maputo, Lilongwe and Midrand. Applicants may be of any nationality and resident anywhere, but must hold a Flemish secondary or higher education diploma.
records.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
records.deadline: No more grants for 2026: 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Within a funded budget year: 'You can submit your grant application up to six months in advance until one day before the start of your internship.'
records.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.
records.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme gives young people who hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant is made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, both set in advance; the monthly amount depends on the host city. Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant, and the programme targets people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again for 2027, with applications reopenable from January 2027.
records.best_fit: Anyone under 35 with a secondary or higher education diploma earned at a Flemish institution, of any nationality, who has already secured or is about to secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation such as the UN, NATO-adjacent bodies, the OECD, the WHO family, the Council of Europe, the Benelux Union or an EU institution.
records.funding_period: month for the living-expense component, plus a one-off travel payment
records.eligibility_summary: You must be under 35 when the internship starts, hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders, and have secured an internship of at least two months with an organisation on the published list of qualifying multilateral organisations.
eligibility: You are younger than 35 on the start date of your internship.
You have obtained a secondary or higher education diploma in Flanders. So your nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant.
You have secured an internship with a multilateral organisation from the published qualifying list.
The internship lasts at least two and up to six months.
The internship must take place at the headquarters or a field office of the organisation, within the areas of jurisdiction of the Diplomatic Representations of Flanders.
coverage: One-off payment of 200 EUR for travel expenses if the internship is within Europe (all Council of Europe member states, Belarus and Kosovo)
One-off payment of 500 EUR for travel expenses if the internship is located outside Europe
Monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, set annually and multiplied by the number of months your internship is active, varying by host city (published city matrix)
No travel reimbursement if the internship is in Belgium
benefits: The grant is not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, so it is not an obstacle to the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit you may still be entitled to for 12 months after finishing your studies
Payment in two instalments: 85% of the total grant after approval, and the remaining 15% after the internship once you submit the internship report and the supervisor's evaluation report
The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders
requirements: Be under 35 on the internship start date
Hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained at a Flemish educational institution
Have secured the internship; you may apply up to six months before it starts or after it has started
Your internship supervisor must complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
If you apply after the internship has started, the remaining period counted from the first day after you submit must be at least two months
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and have your supervisor complete and submit the evaluation form, at the latest two months after the end of the internship
Take part in an intake interview before the internship and a follow-up conversation afterwards
You must not receive a salary from the hosting organisation if you want to keep the Flemish Growth Package/child benefit
Inform the programme if you end the internship early; you may have to repay part of the grant
application_method: Check you meet the eligibility conditions
Secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation, either through a vacancy published on the programme's internships page or by a spontaneous application
Submit the online application form with the required documents
Have your internship supervisor complete the attestation regarding the internship offer and submit it to stages.dkbuza@vlaanderen.be
Receive approval once all documents are provided and the requirements are met
Take part in the intake interview with the programme coordinator
During the internship, stay in contact with the coordinator and provide visual material
After the internship, submit the personal evaluation form and the supervisor's evaluation form within two months
Take part in the follow-up conversation with the coordinator
records.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
records.notes: The grant is explicitly not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, made up of a one-off travel allowance and an expense allowance for accommodation and living expenses. Coverage is partial: it does not pay tuition or course fees, there is no travel payment for an internship in Belgium, and the amounts are capped at a fixed 200 or 500 EUR travel payment plus a city-based monthly living amount. The internship can be extended to a total of six months, or nine months for internships linked to a project funded by the Government of Flanders. If you end the internship early you must inform the programme and may have to repay part of the grant, the amount being determined by the number of days you actually worked. There is no clinical or professional restriction published beyond the requirement that the host be a qualifying multilateral organisation.

official_details.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme offers young global citizens financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant consists of a one-off amount for travel expenses and a monthly amount for living expenses; both are lump sums, meaning they are set in advance. You must hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders, be under 35 when the internship starts, and secure the internship yourself with an organisation on the published qualifying list.
purpose: Give young people financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation
Recruit socially engaged young people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights
Give Flemish-trained young people international exposure and, through Flanders' diplomatic representatives abroad, involve them in Flemish foreign policy
Build a network between young Flemish graduates and multilateral organisations
degree_levels: Secondary education diploma or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders

official_details.selection_notes: The programme publishes no jury, no ranking and no competitive scoring. It is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: 'In principle, you can apply for a grant at any time of the year, but you can only get a grant if there is still budget available. If a budget is no longer available for the current year, it will be clearly announced on this website. If you submit an application when there is no more budget available, it will not be processed. The application is also not kept until a new budget is available.' The published procedure is: submit the application with the required documents; the supervisor submits the attestation; approval is given once all necessary documents are provided and the requirements are met, with an average administrative turnaround of three weeks; the coordinator contacts you for an intake interview; during the internship you stay in contact with the coordinator and provide visual material; afterwards you submit the personal evaluation form and the supervisor's evaluation form within two months and take part in a follow-up conversation.

records.region: Estonia (citizens of 38 listed countries)
records.duration: One academic year (2026/2027); scholarships are paid for undergraduate students for 12 months of the academic year, except for the final nominal year when the scholarship is paid for 10 months
records.deadline: 2026 application period will be open from 1st of October 2026 until October 31st 2026 (23:59, Estonian time)
records.application_period: Applications accepted 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026 (23:59 Estonian time); results announced personally by email
records.description: A monthly stipend for foreign students who already hold an admission confirmation from an Estonian higher education institution for the 2026/2027 academic year. The rate is EUR 350 per month for first-cycle (BA) and master's studies and EUR 660 per month for doctoral studies. The Board pays the scholarship to the host university, which then disburses it. The scheme is funded under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements and is run through the Estonian Scholarship Programme.
records.best_fit: Students from the 38 listed countries who already have an Estonian university admission letter for 2026/2027 and can fund the rest of their costs from other sources
records.eligibility_summary: Citizens of 38 listed countries admitted to an Estonian higher education institution for 2026/2027, with master's and PhD studies supported in all fields and BA only in Estonian language and culture.
eligibility: The scholarship can be applied for by foreign students who wish to study at a higher education institution in Estonia during the 2026/2027 academic year at formal studies or as an exchange student

records.description: A one-month funded research stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala for Africa-focused researchers and students already based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland. The scholarship covers return travel at the least expensive fare, free centrally located accommodation in Uppsala, a desk and computer in a shared office at the Institute, and a subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day. It is a short-term research stay award, not a degree programme.

records.description: The UC Doctoral Scholarship is a centrally funded Te Whare WÄnanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury award that supports study towards a first research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC. Its published value is financial assistance of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points. The same round can add recognition-only or top-up Prestige awards, but applicants who hold one of the Core scholarships are also automatically considered for Prestige awards with no separate application, and the Prestige value is added on top of the Core value (for example a $32,650 p.a. stipend becomes $37,650 p.a. with a $5,000 top-up). It is not a New Zealand Government scholarship; it is a university award and subject to funding availability and annual review.
records.best_fit: International and domestic applicants who intend to enter their first research doctoral degree at the University of Canterbury, can start before 1 July 2027, and hold academic results equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0 over the last two years of relevant academic study.
records.funding_period: per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, up to a total of 360 points
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be entering their first research doctoral degree at UC in any discipline, with a GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0, and international students may apply unless a scholarship's regulations restrict it to NZ citizens or residence class visa holders.
eligibility: You intend to study at UC towards your first research doctoral degree.
Your GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study is equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0.
The award is available in any discipline at UC.
International students can apply for any UC scholarship unless the regulations specifically restrict the scholarship to NZ citizens or holders of NZ residence class visas.
Most scholarships require that you have admission to the University, so you must also meet the criteria for admission to your research doctoral programme.

You must have also submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications (point 2.2 of the Regulations); this is done in your myUC account.

coverage: Financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points.
Tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points, as stated in the published value of the award.

Automatic consideration for Prestige top-up awards if awarded one of the Core scholarships, with no separate application; for example the Brownlie Scholarship and Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship each add $5,000 per 120 points to the Core value, and the Roper Scholarship in Science is $30,000 per 120 points of thesis enrolment.
benefits: Recognition-only award with no extra money: the Canterbury Scholarship, which recognises high-ranked domestic recipients of a centrally funded Core UC Doctoral Scholarship.

Prestige awards that add value on top of the Core award: Brownlie Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), William & Ina Cartwright Scholarship (Faculty of Education, $24,500 per 120 points of thesis enrolment), Doctoral Graduate Women Canterbury (Inc.) Trust Board Scholarship ($24,500 per 120 points, Arts, Education or Health), RÄtÄ Foundation Scholarship ($24,500 per 120 points).

The UC Commitments Doctoral Scholarship adds an additional $5,000 for research expenses across the duration of the degree, and UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships are co-funded with external agencies, but both are separate applications with their own project lists and their own closing dates (UC Commitments closes 27 October; UC Connect closes 15 September).

records.name: Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS)
records.official_source: Charles Darwin University
records.region: Northern Territory and other Australian campuses (Charles Darwin University)
records.duration: The minimum time in which the course can be completed, or until the maximum scholarship value is exhausted, the course is completed, or the recipient no longer meets the ongoing eligibility of the scholarship.
records.deadline: Applications close 31 January 2027 for Semester 1, 2027 intake, and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2, 2027 intake.
records.application_period: Applications are open at the time of checking on 1 October 2026. CDU publishes closing dates of 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027, but does not publish a separate opening date for the scholarship.
records.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship is a Charles Darwin University award for international students with a record of academic excellence. CDU publishes that it covers 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course, and that it is neither transferable for cash nor refundable and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. Applicants must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, must be paying international student fees, and must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency. Results are announced during Orientation Week.
records.best_fit: International applicants with a 95% or higher overall score in their highest completed qualification who are applying to commence study at CDU in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027 in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree and who can fund the remaining 50% of their tuition fees themselves.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be international students paying international student fees who apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, meet CDU's academic and English language entry requirements for their course, hold a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, and not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
eligibility: Applicant must apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, in the intake they are first offered.
Applicant must meet the University's academic and English language entry requirements for their chosen course.
Applicant must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification.
Applicant must be an international student paying international student fees.
Applicant must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
Applicants must be able to pay their portion of the tuition fees on or before the payment due date, which CDU states is the first day of teaching of each semester.
The scholarship applies to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree.
coverage: 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course.
benefits: Results are announced during Orientation Week, earlier than the start of teaching.

CDU's international student scholarships page also lists automatic, no-application-required awards that can sit alongside a study offer, including the CDU Global Merit Scholarship (30% of the tuition fee for select courses, for new international TAFE, undergraduate, postgraduate coursework and higher degree by research students commencing in 2026 and 2027, automatically assessed after submitting a course application) and the CDU Bachelor of Nursing Scholarship (up to 20% of the tuition fee for the Bachelor of Nursing, for new international students commencing in 2027, automatically assessed).
requirements: Step 1: apply to study at CDU.
Step 2: submit your application for the VCIHAS.
The application form requires an application intake, an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC) and an email address that matches the one provided in the Studylink application.
The form requires an average overall score in your highest completed qualification, expressed as a percentage.

The applicant statement is mandatory and answers why you should be selected, how you will become an outstanding ambassador of CDU, your extracurricular activities with a focus on community engagement, work experience, creative arts and sport, and how you will use your CDU qualification to make a difference in your community.

A declaration must be ticked confirming the information is true and correct, that you have read and understood the conditions of application, that the decision of the University selection panel is final, that you cannot hold more than one tuition fee scholarship from CDU at a time, that you do not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsorship agency, and that you accept you may be asked to provide a student story or testimonial as a scholarship recipient.
The form must be signed and dated.

Ongoing eligibility: continue to be an international student liable for international student fees, pay your portion of tuition fees on or before the first day of teaching of each semester, maintain satisfactory academic progress each semester with a minimum GPA of 5.3 and no fail grade in any unit, and maintain a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless you have approval to reduce your study load or take a leave of absence for the semester.
records.english_requirement: CDU requires all higher education applicants to satisfy the English Language Proficiency Requirements for their chosen course and to supply evidence of this at the time of application. CDU's published minimum English test scores are: IELTS Academic overall minimum 6.5 with no band below 6.0 for postgraduate and overall minimum 6.0 with no band below 6.0 for undergraduate; PTE Academic overall minimum 58 with no score below 50 for postgraduate and overall minimum 50 with no score below 50 for undergraduate; TOEFL overall minimum 79 with a minimum writing score of 21 for postgraduate and overall minimum 60 with a minimum writing score of 21 for undergraduate; Cambridge English Advanced overall minimum 176 with no skill below 169 for postgraduate and overall minimum 169 with no skill below 169 for undergraduate; CDU ELICOS EAP004 for postgraduate and EAP003 for undergraduate; and an approved English test completed within two years of commencement. IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted, allowing a single skill to be retaken within 60 days. Alternative evidence routes published on the same page include Year 12 in an approved English-speaking country, 0.5 FTE of higher education study in an approved country completed within the past five years where relevant, an enabling course, a TAFE qualification at Certificate III or higher, current AHPRA registration, two years of full-time equivalent employment in English-medium roles within the last five years in a recognised English-speaking country, or a primary language pathway declaration.
application_method: Apply to study at CDU and obtain an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC).
Use the same email address in the scholarship form as in your Studylink application.

Complete the Vice-Chancellor's High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS) Application form on CDU's website, including your intended intake, your average overall score as a percentage, and the four applicant statement questions.
Tick the declaration, sign the form and enter the date.
Submit the form before the closing date for your intake: 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 or 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027.
Await the outcome; CDU states results will be announced during Orientation Week.
records.selection_notes: CDU publishes the selection criteria as the overall score in your highest completed qualification plus a supporting statement. The application form adds that the decision of the University selection panel is final, and the declaration confirms the process is competitive. CDU publishes no interview requirement, no weighting for the two criteria, no offer round structure and no appeal process for VCIHAS; other CDU International College scholarships on the same page do publish an interview requirement, so confirm whether an interview applies to VCIHAS.
records.notes: This is not full funding: it covers 50% of the tuition fee only, and the recipient must pay their portion of tuition on or before the first day of teaching of each semester. The scholarship is neither transferable for cash nor refundable, and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. It is conditional rather than open-ended: it ends at the earliest of course completion, exhaustion of the maximum scholarship value, or loss of ongoing eligibility, and retaining it requires a minimum GPA of 5.3 with no fail grade in any unit and a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless a reduced load or leave of absence is approved. Only one CDU tuition fee scholarship may be held at a time, and holding another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency disqualifies the applicant. No deferral, return-home, clinical restriction, tax treatment or award renewal terms are published on the pages read. Official pages disagree on the statement length: the scholarship page says up to 600 words, the application form says 500 words or less.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your overall score in your highest completed qualification is 95% or above, because that is the hard published floor.

important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a living-cost scholarship: it reduces tuition by half and nothing more, so accommodation, living costs, travel and visa are entirely yours.

Do not accept another sponsoring-agency scholarship in the hope of holding both; the declaration makes it a disqualifier.
Do not let your GPA slip below 5.3 or take a fail grade in any unit, because that ends the scholarship mid-course.
Do not plan a reduced study load without approval; staying at 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) is an ongoing condition.
Do not spend effort on referees or an English test specifically for this scholarship: neither is requested in the published form fields.

Applying for an intake outside Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027.
Missing the intake closing date of 31 January 2027 or 4 July 2027.

records.name: ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award
records.official_source: The Australian National University
records.region: Canberra, Australia (applicants who hold residential status in China including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR, Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea)
records.duration: Payment made for 1 year (payments are made for a fixed number of years; for this award that is one year)
records.deadline: Application period: Open for applications. ANU publishes no closing date for this award; consideration is automatic with the admissions application.
records.application_period: Continuous. ANU's scholarship page shows the application period as 'Open for applications' with no closing date, because no separate scholarship application is required: all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the University are considered automatically.
records.description: The ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award is an Australian National University award whose stated objective is to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs at ANU, funded by the University. ANU publishes the value as 20% off first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester for the one year of the award. It is restricted to residents of China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and excludes the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE). Recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study.
records.best_fit: International students resident in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea who are applying for admission to an eligible ANU undergraduate, honours, graduate certificate or postgraduate coursework program, meet a Selection Rank of 85 or equivalent (undergraduate) or a GPA of 5.5 or equivalent (postgraduate), and are not already covered by external sponsorship of their tuition fees.
records.eligibility_summary: The award is available to an international student who is a new commencing student, or a continuing student with an offer of admission to a higher AQF level, who holds residential status in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, meets the minimum academic entry requirements (Selection Rank of 85 or equivalent for undergraduate, minimum GPA of 5.5 or equivalent for postgraduate), is not the recipient of an external sponsorship covering all or part of their tuition fees at ANU, and accepts that the award can be offered only once at each level of study.
eligibility: You are an international student.
You are a new commencing student, or a continuing student who has received an offer of admission to a higher AQF level of studies.

You hold residential status in one of the following Countries or Regions: China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, Republic of Korea, or The Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

You meet the minimum academic entry requirements: undergraduate applicants a Selection Rank of 85 (or equivalent as determined by the University) or above, or postgraduate applicants a minimum GPA of 5.5 (or equivalent).
You are not the recipient of an external sponsorship that covers all or part of your tuition fees at the University.

You acknowledge that the award can be offered only once at each level of study, except where you progress from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), or accept a packaged offer such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree.
Your program is an eligible program, excluding the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE).
Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters and Graduate certificate. Selection basis: academic merit.
coverage: 20% off your first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester.
One year of payments; ANU states the duration of the Award is one year.
benefits: No separate scholarship application: all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the University are considered automatically.
You accept the academic offer and the scholarship offer separately; more information is provided with the scholarship offer letter.

ANU publishes a separate ANU International Achievement Award for applicants resident outside this award's country list, with published values of 20% for Undergraduate, 20% for Postgraduate, 25% for South East Asia and 50% for Pacific.
requirements: There is no need to apply for the scholarship; all eligible students applying for admission to commence at the university will be automatically considered.
Press the 'Apply now' button to start the Admissions application process.
You will need to accept both your academic offer and your scholarship offer separately; more information is provided with your scholarship offer letter.
The recipient is responsible for making payment of all tuition fees by the prescribed date as set out by the University each session.
The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer.
Only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered.
ANU publishes a Conditions of Award document numbered 63/2026, linked from the scholarship page.
application_method: Choose an eligible ANU program; the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE) are excluded.
Press the 'Apply now' button on the scholarship page to start the ANU Admissions application process.
Submit the admission application; there is no separate scholarship application, and eligibility is assessed automatically.
Receive the academic offer and, if selected, a separate scholarship offer stating the value of the Award.
Accept the academic offer and the scholarship offer separately.
Pay your share of the tuition fees by the prescribed date set out by the University each session; the tuition scholarship is applied towards tuition at the start of each semester of the award year.
records.selection_notes: ANU states that selection is based on academic merit, that only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered, that qualifications submitted for admission will be converted to the common scale which determines whether an applicant is eligible, and that eligible applicants with multiple qualifications will be ranked according to the qualification used as the basis of admission. The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer. ANU publishes no interview, no referee requirement, no offer rounds and no appeal process for this award.
records.notes: This is not full funding and should not be budgeted as such: the published value is 20% off first-year tuition fees for one year only, and recipients pay the balance of all tuition fees by the prescribed date each session. ANU states recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study. The award can be offered only once at each level of study, with two published exceptions: progression from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), and packaged offers such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree. Eligibility is by residential status, not citizenship, and is restricted to China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea; residents of all other countries apply to the separate ANU International Achievement Award. Holding external sponsorship covering all or part of your ANU tuition fees disqualifies you. Deferral, renewal, return-home obligations, clinical restrictions and tax treatment are not published on the page read; the Conditions of Award (63/2026) PDF is the document that governs them and could not be read.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your residential status is in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea; if it is not, apply to the ANU International Achievement Award instead.

important_advice_for_students: Do not spend time preparing a scholarship application; there is none.

Do not rely on this award to cover living costs; ANU puts accommodation and all other costs of study squarely on the recipient.
Do count on the automatic assessment happening at the time your admission application is assessed, so a strong academic record in the qualification used for admission is what matters.
Do remember the award can generally be held only once at each level of study, with exceptions only for a one-year Honours progression or a packaged Graduate Certificate to Master's offer.

records.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
records.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan - administered in-country through Japanese embassies/consulates
records.region: Japan (applicants from countries served by Japanese embassies/consulates; field and type of application vary by country)
records.duration: Embassy Recommendation: irregular course within 2 years; regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)
records.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
records.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.
records.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
records.best_fit: Applicants who already hold (or are close to) a bachelor's degree and can enter a Japanese graduate school's master's or doctoral programme, who are under 35, who sit the embassy/consulate's Japanese and English examinations, and whose country runs the Research Student track.
records.eligibility_summary: Research students must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's programme or a doctoral programme (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
eligibility: Research students: You must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's program or a doctoral program (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
Embassy Recommendation: scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

The type and field of application may vary from country to country. Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for.
All required documents and interviews will be conducted by the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission abroad in your country.
coverage: Tuition exempted
Monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000 per month for research students
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided
Preliminary training of Japanese etc.: 6 months (only those who need this training)
benefits: Preliminary training of Japanese etc. of 6 months for those who need this training, where offered by the institution
Placement into a Japanese graduate school at no application cost
requirements: Application must be made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's own country (Embassy Recommendation route).
Applicants must take the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations, which for research students are Japanese and English.
The applicant must submit a 'Configuration Preference for University of Placement' (配置希望大学申請書) as part of the application forms.
Application fee is not charged; MEXT warns that organisations or individuals charging application fees or deposits have no relation with the Japanese Government.
application_method: Confirm with the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your own country whether the Research Student type and the field you wish to apply for are open this year.
Sit the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations for research students (Japanese and English).

Complete the MEXT application forms: Application Form, Configuration Preference for University of Placement, Field of Specialization and Research Plan, Certificate of Health, and the University Acceptance Consent format.
Submit all required documents and attend the interview conducted by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country.
The embassy/consulate screens applicants and forwards its recommendations to MEXT.
MEXT makes the scholarship offer and the receiving graduate school is identified for placement.
Receive round-trip airfare funded by MEXT and begin study in Japan.
records.selection_notes: Applicants are recruited and initially screened by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country, which sits its own qualifying examinations (Japanese and English for research students), conducts the interview and collects all required documents; MEXT then selects the scholarship students and allocates them to host graduate schools, subject to the host university's acceptance.
records.notes: No published deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction terms were readable on the official pages read. MEXT publishes rules on extending the scholarship period (applications for extension from newly admitted students in April 2026 and from early-completers are handled by notice), rules on combining the scholarship with other awards, and rules on part-time work by scholarship students, but these notices are in Japanese and were not readable in the English sources used for this record. Application is free of charge.

official_details.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship supports foreign students who study in higher education institutions, selected on the recommendation of Japanese Embassy/Consulate General, University, or Authority. This record covers the 2027 Research Student track under Embassy Recommendation. The Study in Japan types table gives research students: level of studies 'Graduate school level'; duration '[Embassy Recommendation] Irregular course: within 2 years; Regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)'; preliminary training of Japanese etc. '6 months (Only those who need this training)'; field of study 'Major in field of specialty at a graduate school etc.'; scholarship '¥143,000~¥145,000 per month'; tuition 'Exempted'; travel allowance 'Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided'.
purpose: The national scholarship system exists to accept excellent students from overseas, thereby promoting international exchange and friendship, contributing to the development of human resources in foreign countries, advancing the internationalisation of universities and other institutions in Japan, improving educational and research capacity, and contributing to the internationalisation and vitalisation of society as a whole and to the development of Japan and the world.
For Embassy Recommendation, scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).
study_type: Research student at a graduate school (major in field of specialty at a graduate school etc.)
Regular course or irregular course (regular course may include 6 months preliminary Japanese training where necessary)
official_details.degree_award: Short-term award: the applicant is placed as a research student at a Japanese graduate school. The published information does not state that the scholarship itself confers a degree.
official_details.duration: [Embassy Recommendation] Irregular course: within 2 years. Regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added). Preliminary training of Japanese etc.: 6 months (only those who need this training).
official_details.application_cycle: Annual cohort cycle; this record covers the 2027 cycle. MEXT lists '2027 Embassy Recommendation Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship Students (Research Students)' under '募集中のプログラム' (programmes currently being recruited).
official_details.deadline_central_display: No central deadline published. MEXT: 'All application procedures for Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho:MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan.' Study in Japan: 'Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for.'
official_details.deadline_institutional: Set and published by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's own country; MEXT does not publish it centrally.
official_details.deadline_note: No deadline is published centrally because Embassy Recommendation deadlines, qualifying-examination dates and interview dates are set by each Japanese embassy/consulate general. deadline_date is therefore left null rather than estimated.

official_details.living_cost_coverage: Monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000 per month for research students (published as a range, so no single figure is recorded).
official_details.travel_coverage: Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided.
official_details.tuition_rule: The scholarship page states tuition is 'Exempted' for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship types, including research students under both Embassy Recommendation and University Recommendation.
