Prepare the 'Field of Specialization and Research Plan' and a dated Certificate of Health.
Prepare your 'Application Form for Configuration Preference for University of Placement' listing your preferred Japanese universities.
Arrange the 'University Acceptance Consent' step with the universities you list.
Never pay an application fee or deposit: MEXT states the application is free and that anyone charging fees or deposits has no relation with the Japanese Government.
important_advice_for_students: Do not apply directly to MEXT on the Embassy Recommendation route - every application goes through your embassy or consulate general, and MEXT publishes no central deadline.
Get the deadline from your embassy or consulate general directly; it is the only binding date for your application.
Study in Japan publishes past qualifying-examination subject test papers as samples; use them to prepare for the Japanese and English examinations.
Budget separately for anything the scholarship does not explicitly state it pays, such as accommodation costs; the pages read do not establish that rent is covered.
If you want a University Recommendation route instead, contact the Japanese university first - only MEXT-approved universities with a recommendation quota can recommend.
common_rejection_risks: Being 35 or older at the point of application.
Not being eligible for admission to a master's or doctoral programme at a Japanese graduate school.
Not sitting or failing the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations in Japanese and English.
Applying through a channel other than the embassy/consulate general, which invalidates the Embassy Recommendation route.
Assuming an open programme: the embassy may not have opened your field for that year.
Missing the embassy-level deadline, since MEXT publishes no central closing date that an applicant could rely on.
Paying a third party claiming to process a MEXT application; MEXT warns that such organisations are unrelated to the Japanese Government.
estimated_uncovered_costs: University dormitory or private housing rent and any deposit - not stated as paid by the scholarship on the official pages read.
Books, study materials and laboratory or equipment charges.
Any expenses beyond the mandatory health insurance and any personal medical costs.
Visa, residence and re-entry permit issuance fees (not published as covered on the pages read).

records.name: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
records.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) - applied for by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
records.region: Japan (candidates must be citizens or permanent residents of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan)
records.duration: 14 to 60 days
records.deadline: FY2027 2nd Recruitment (Short-term): Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS) April 23, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST)). The first FY2027 recruitment deadline was August 28, 2026. Note that host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which 'depending on the institution, it may have its own deadline more than one month before the application deadline set by JSPS'.
records.application_period: FY2027 2nd recruitment: host-institution submissions to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; selection results published in early August 2027; periods for arrival in Japan 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028. The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before each JSPS deadline.
records.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.
records.best_fit: Established overseas researchers holding a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (or researchers more than six years past a doctorate who have continuously conducted research), who already have an agreed collaboration plan with a Japanese host researcher and can spend 14 to 60 days in Japan.
records.eligibility_summary: The candidate must be a citizen or permanent resident of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine treated likewise) and must hold a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor at a foreign university or research institution.
eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
coverage: Round-trip air ticket (economy-class), based on JSPS's regulations
Maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day (Short-term)
Overseas travel insurance
Research support allowance: up to JPY 150,000, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
benefits: JSPS provides fellows with useful information on living in Japan, opportunities to foster interactions among researchers, and avenues for conducting outreach activities.
JSPS supports the Science Dialogue Program, enabling fellows to give lectures in English on their research work at high schools in the vicinity of their Japanese host institutes.
Access to the JSPS Fellows Plaza network and alumni follow-up activities after the fellowship.
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution.
The host researcher must choose the review section in which the application will be screened from the FY2027 Review Section Table, referring to the FY2027 Review Section Set.

The host institution's application must be sent to the president of JSPS by the application deadline for the programme, verified as approved by the head of the institution and confirmed that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved.
Before sending the application, the institution must check the 'List of Applications' on the JSPS Electronic Application System to verify that the registered information is correct.
A Research Proposal Document (S-2) must be completed jointly by the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate.
A Fellow's Curriculum Vitae (S-3) must be completed by the candidate.
application_method: Agree a concrete activity plan with the prospective host researcher in Japan; JSPS requires that the two 'have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan'.
The host researcher selects the appropriate category from the FY2027 Review Section Table, checking the FY2027 Review Section Set for the paired reviewers.
The host researcher obtains approval from the head of their institution and collects the candidate's S-3 Curriculum Vitae, then completes S-2 jointly with the candidate.
The host researcher submits the application through the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host institution's internal deadline, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline.
The host institution transmits the application to the president of JSPS by the JSPS deadline (5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027 for the FY2027 2nd recruitment).
JSPS conducts a document review by three examiners, then a panel review; results are published in early August 2027 for the 2nd recruitment.
The fellow arrives in Japan within the published arrival period (1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028 for the 2nd recruitment).
records.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.
records.notes: The pages read publish no deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction term, so those fields are left null. Published exclusions: for a candidate who has been living in Japan (and has a mailing address) before the fellowship starting date, the outbound 'airfare' and a 'settling-in allowance' will not be paid. JSPS states the number of selectees with Japanese nationality must be no more than about 3% of all selectees under one recruitment for an application deadline. Selection policy also states that, as much as possible, unbalance should be avoided in the selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization. The host institution, not the fellow, applies for the research support allowance.

official_details.description: The programs provide excellent researchers from other countries an opportunity to conduct collaborative research, discussions, and opinion exchanges with researchers in Japan. These programs are intended to help advance the overseas researchers' research activities while advancing science and promoting internationalization in Japan. JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan consists of two options of Long-term, and Short-term. Grantees are selected by going through the selection process following the submission of applications by a host researcher in Japan who wishes to invite a researcher from overseas via the head of their university or institution. The recruitment and selection for the Long-term program is announced and conducted once a year, and twice a year for the Short-term.

application_readiness_checklist: Identify a host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible Japanese institution who will submit the application through their institution's head - you cannot apply alone.
Agree a concrete written activity plan with that host; JSPS selection policy explicitly requires prior contact and a concrete plan.

Confirm you hold a position equivalent to Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor, or that it is six or more years since your doctorate and your host institution judges you to have continuously conducted research.

Confirm you are a citizen or permanent resident of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine treated alike); Japanese nationals need 10+ years' residence abroad and an active role in that country's scientific community.
Ask the host institution for its internal deadline - it may be more than one month earlier than the JSPS deadline of 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027.
Prepare the candidate's curriculum vitae using the official S-3 Word template.
Have the host pick the correct review section from the FY2027 Review Section Table using the FY2027 Review Section Set.
Have the S-2 Research Proposal Document completed jointly by you and the host researcher using the official Word template.
important_advice_for_students: The candidate never submits an application: everything goes through the Japanese host institution, so start the relationship with the host before anything else.
Read the FY2027 Application Guideline PDF (923KB) for the full document list and rules; the web pages only summarise.
The research support allowance is not automatic - the host must apply for it through their institution, so ask the host to include that step.
If you already live in Japan with a mailing address before the start date, the outbound airfare and settling-in allowance are not paid.
Budget for accommodation and living costs beyond the JPY 18,000 per day maintenance allowance: none of those are listed as covered.
Choose a review section carefully - document and panel reviews are conducted on an individual basis, each unit based on Review Section Sets.
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a KAKENHI-eligible host institution, or with a host who is not a full-time researcher and cannot guarantee a suitable research environment throughout the tenure.
No prior contact with the host and no concrete activity plan - this is an explicit selection policy criterion.
Not holding a position equivalent to Japanese professor/associate professor/assistant professor and having fewer than six years since the doctorate.
Missing the host institution's internal deadline, which may be more than a month before the JSPS deadline.
Registered information on the 'List of Applications' not verified before transmission.
A plan limited to the host institution only, when the Short-term policy expects lectures, discussions or exchange activities in other institutions too, plus opportunities to foster young researchers.
Selecting the wrong review section, which affects which reviewers assess the application.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation in Japan.

Local travel in Japan and any expenses for activities at other institutions not covered by the host's research support allowance application.

records.description: The Young Leaders' Program is a Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship that brings young government officials from designated countries to Japan for a one-year Master's course in public policy at GRIPS, awarding the Master of Public Policy degree. Recipients are nominated through their own country's nominating authority rather than applying directly. Funding covers a monthly scholarship of ¥242,000, full tuition exemption and round-trip airfare, and the programme requires the fellows to return to their home administration after graduation.

official_details.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) was introduced by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in 2001. GRIPS runs two courses: School of Government, introduced in 2001, and School of Local Governance, started in 2009. The programme awards a Master of Public Policy degree, is taught in English, runs for one year with October enrolment and September graduation, and the scholarship for international students is the Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship. In the Study in Japan types table, YLP students are shown with: level of studies 'Master course at a graduate school', duration '1 year', preliminary training of Japanese etc. 'None', field of study 'Master course at a graduate school', scholarship '¥242,000 per month', tuition 'Exempted', travel allowance 'Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided'. YLP is the one MEXT scholarship type available only by recommendation from official overseas recommending organizations - neither embassy recommendation nor university recommendation is shown for it.
purpose: Foster future national leaders in designated countries.
Build up comprehensive human networks among the leaders of nations.
Establish friendly relationships among the countries involved, including Japan.
Improve the quality of policy making in the participating countries.
Expand students' comparative as well as historical knowledge of international/regional politics and economics while providing them with an in-depth understanding of Japanese politics and economy.

On GRIPS's own statement: 'The Young Leaders Program (YLP) is a scholarship program launched by MEXT in 2001. YLP contributes to the cultivation of future national leaders in Asian and other countries, to building human networks among the leaders of each country, and to promoting friendship among the countries involved, including Japan.'
sdg_requirement_details: GRIPS operates a GRIPS SDGs Award for graduates, but the pages read do not state an SDG requirement for admission or for the scholarship.

Missing your nominating authority's internal timetable, since no central deadline is published and the window is short.

Paying a third party claiming to process a MEXT application.

records.description: The Korean government-invited scholarship degree programme that funds a year of Korean language training followed by an associate degree (2-3 years) or bachelor's degree (4-6 years) at a designated GKS university in Korea. The published benefits list is airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances. Selection runs through two routes: an Embassy Track that applies through the Korean embassy/consulate, and a University Track in which the student applies directly to a GKS-designated university (UIC specialisation and Associate Degree).
records.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals under 25 who hold a high-school diploma (bachelor's track) or are entering an associate degree programme, and who meet the published academic-performance threshold; also international students from R-GKS partner countries applying through the Embassy Track.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants and both of their parents must hold non-Korean citizenship, be under 25 as of the applicable year, hold the published minimum educational qualification for the track, and meet the published academic-performance requirement.
eligibility: Nationality: Applicants and both of their parents must hold non-Korean citizenship
Age: Applicants must be under 25 years of age as of the applicable year
Education: Associate Degree Program - High school graduate or expected to graduate; Bachelor's Degree Program - High school or associate degree graduate or expected to graduate

Academic Performance: Applicants must meet the academic performance requirements, such as a cumulative score of 80% or higher, ranking within the top 20% of their class, or meeting the required CGPA threshold
Embassy Track General and Overseas Korean applicants may apply to up to three universities, including at least one Type B university
Embassy Track R-GKS applicants may apply to up to two Type B universities
The UIC Program under University Track provides customized curriculum and field experience through industry-university cooperation focused on the fields of natural science and engineering
Specialization (UIC) is available only for associate and bachelor's degree programs

records.description: KAIST's own scholarship for international graduate students, selected as part of the admission application rather than as a separate scholarship application. It covers full tuition fees plus national health insurance and a monthly stipend, and 94% of KAIST's international student body receive it. Two higher tiers are awarded automatically to those selected: the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KRW 1,000,000 per month for 4 regular semesters) and the KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KRW 300,000 per month for 8 regular semesters). The published cost-of-study table shows the student still carries on-campus housing, food, books, travel and telecommunications costs.
records.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals applying to KAIST master's, Master's-Ph.D. integrated or Ph.D. programmes who meet KAIST's English proficiency requirement (or a published exemption) and can satisfy a doctoral or master's-level qualification by the start of the course.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to international applicants for KAIST graduate programmes who are citizens of countries other than Korea, hold a bachelor's degree (master's/Master's-Ph.D.) or a master's degree (Ph.D.) by the start of the course, and provide a qualifying English proficiency test score unless a published exemption applies.

records.english_requirement: KAIST's official language of communication and instruction for international students is English. All applicants must provide at least one English proficiency test score, and the scores must be valid as of the online application deadline. Published minimums: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026); IELTS Academic 6.5 band; TOEIC 720 (Listening & Reading, TOEIC Public Testing Program); TEPS 326. TOEFL institutional code 0195, department code 99; Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores are NOT accepted; IELTS Online is accepted but IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted; test scores from Institutional Testing Program (ITP) are NOT accepted. Exemption: no EPT score is required if you hold citizenship of, or have physically studied and completed a bachelor's-equivalent or higher qualification at an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A. A further exemption applies if you hold citizenship of one of a listed group of countries AND have physically studied and completed a qualification equivalent to a bachelor's degree or higher in English as the medium of instruction at an institution physically located in one of those countries, in which case a certificate from the school attended indicating English as the medium of instruction (e.g. English Lecture Certificate) must additionally be provided. Applicants expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course also do not need to provide a score. Programs that do not require an EPT score: GDI-ITTP track, KINS-KAIST.
application_method: Check the published admission window for your entry term (Spring: mid August - early September; Fall Early: early December - late December; Fall Regular: early March - late March)
Create an ApplyWeb account and complete the KAIST International Graduate online application
Select the KAIST scholarship option as your financial resource in the application
Request your recommendation letter through the KAIST online Letter of Recommendation system during the designated submission period
Submit the application before the online application deadline (the EPT score must be valid as of that deadline)
If selected, you are automatically considered for the KGPS and/or KPS; no separate scholarship application is needed
Respond to the offer, register for school, prepare the certificate of admission and apply for a student visa
records.selection_notes: Scholarship status is decided inside the admission process: applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the application are automatically considered for the KAIST Scholarship and, where the degree programme matches, for the KGPS or the KPS. For the KGPS, no separate application is made and only highly competitive applicants will be recommended by the department head. For the KPS, applicants demonstrating outstanding academic and research achievements receive recommendations from the department head, with final selection by the college dean. KAIST states that 94 percent of its international students benefit from the scholarship and that the scholarship rate may vary by student.
records.notes: Not a standalone scholarship application: the award is attached to admission. The monthly stipend of the base KAIST Scholarship is stated to be dependent on research involvement, and no base stipend figure is published; KAIST also states the stipend amount may vary depending on individual colleges, with the College of Engineering publishing its own stipend terms separately. The KPS stipend for Master's-Ph.D. integrated entrants begins at the start of the Ph.D. programme, not on entry. The published Cost of Studying at KAIST figures are for the 2023 academic year. The Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) is excluded from KAIST Scholarship applications.

official_details.description: KAIST offers a simple yet generous scholarship program specifically designed for international students. The KAIST Scholarship covers full tuition fees and provides stipends, benefiting 94% of our international student body. This support is often complemented by research opportunities, enabling most students to achieve financial self-sufficiency and minimize their dependence on external funding. International applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource during the admission application process will be automatically considered for the following scholarship programs, based on their chosen degree program or major.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you do not hold Korean citizenship; if you are of Korean descent with foreign citizenship, start the renunciation paperwork or confirm that all of Grades 1-12 were completed outside Korea with certified certificates and transcripts
Confirm your bachelor's (master's/Master's-Ph.D.) or master's (Ph.D.) qualification will be complete by the start of the course
Book your English proficiency test early - TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, TOEIC or TEPS - and make sure the score is still valid on the online application deadline date

Check whether you qualify for a published EPT exemption before paying for a test; if you use the citizenship-plus-English-medium-instruction exemption, obtain an English Lecture Certificate from your school
Pick your entry term against the published windows: Spring (mid August - early September), Fall Early (early December - late December), Fall Regular (early March - late March)
Avoid iBT MyBest Scores, IELTS One Skill Retake and Institutional Testing Program results, all of which are rejected
Confirm your intended department accepts KAIST Scholarship applicants; the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) does not
Agree the recommendation letter timetable with your referee well before the submission window closes, because the letter cannot be changed after the deadline
Review the College of Engineering's own stipend terms if you are applying to Engineering, since the base stipend varies by college
important_advice_for_students: There is no separate scholarship form to file - the scholarship is chosen inside the admission application, so prioritise the admission deadline

Do not expect a single stipend figure: the base stipend depends on research involvement and varies by college, and only the KGPS (KRW 1,000,000/month for 4 regular semesters) and KPS (KRW 300,000/month for 8 regular semesters) tiers have published amounts
Do not assume housing or food are covered; the published cost table shows you must budget for both
If you are a Master's-Ph.D. integrated entrant, the KPS stipend does not start until you begin the Ph.D. programme
Do not rely on a MyBest TOEFL score or an IELTS One Skill Retake result; both are explicitly rejected
Do not file before your English test result is out and valid, or you will not meet the published condition
Use ApplyWeb rather than any emailed route; KAIST publishes an online system for both the application and the recommendation letter
common_rejection_risks: Holding Korean citizenship, or being of Korean descent with foreign citizenship without the renunciation documentation or the fully-foreign Grades 1-12 record
Studying part of primary or secondary school in Korea, which breaks the completed-outside-Korea condition without exception; international schools inside Korea do not count
Missing the degree qualification deadline for the course start
An English test score that expires before or on the online application deadline
Submitting iBT MyBest Scores, IELTS One Skill Retake, or an Institutional Testing Program score
Claiming an EPT exemption without the additional English-medium-of-instruction certificate when the published conditions require it
Applying to the Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) expecting KAIST Scholarship support
A late or missing recommendation letter - it cannot be modified after the deadline
Assuming KGPS or KPS is applied for separately; it is automatic, and KGPS still needs department-head recommendation of highly competitive applicants only

records.description: KAIST awards its scholarship automatically to every admitted international undergraduate student, with no separate application: the applicant simply ticks "KAIST scholarship" on the Statement of Financial Resources section of the admission application. The award pays tuition exemption for 8 semesters, a living allowance of 350,000 KRW per month, and medical health insurance. It is not full funding: KAIST's own cost table shows the scholarship offsets 11,738,360 KRW of a 14,885,680 KRW essential annual budget, leaving roughly 3,359,000 KRW per year for housing, food and books.

records.notes: Automatic award tied to admission, not a competitive scholarship. Applicants pay the application fee and may not change their application track afterwards (for example from Early to Regular). Interviews are not required for all applicants; selected applicants are contacted individually by email with further instructions and the interview date is subject to change. Admission announcement dates are also published as subject to change. KAIST students hold an undeclared major during the freshman year and may choose any major at the end of the second semester, with no per-department quota. official_details.description: KAIST offers the KAIST Scholarship to applicants of International Student Admission. Subsidies: full tuition fee (tuition exemption for 8 semesters), living expenses of 350,000 KRW per month, and medical health insurance. We offer KAIST Scholarships to admitted students; students must maintain GPA over 2.7 out of 4.3 at KAIST after their freshman year. There is no separate process for applying for the scholarship: just check 'KAIST scholarship' on the Statement of Financial Resources section of the online application for admission. All applications will be thoroughly and equally reviewed during the admission process; upon being selected for admission you will automatically be entitled to the KAIST Scholarship.

records.name: ICSSR Participation in International Seminar Abroad (Travel Grant Scheme)
records.degree_levels: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and doctoral/postdoctoral scholars)
records.official_source: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education, Government of India
records.region: India (Indian social science scholars; conferences held outside India)
records.duration: Period of stay abroad not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates
records.deadline: Applications can be submitted online throughout the year. The applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
records.application_period: Rolling - applications are submitted online throughout the year, and must be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
records.description: This scheme gives partial financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who have been formally invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad. Assistance covers air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance for the stay, and registration fee up to US$200. Regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit, while SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability, and postgraduate/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection may be considered for the full cost of the visit.
records.best_fit: Indian social science scholars (faculty, PhD scholars, postdocs, and some independent senior professionals) with a formally accepted oral paper at a high-value international conference outside India, who need help with the cost of attending.
records.eligibility_summary: Indian social science scholars in regular service at a UGC-recognized university/deemed university/college, an Institute of National Importance, or an ICSSR research or recognised institute, holding a PhD, or post-graduate/PhD/post-doctoral scholars at an advanced stage of study, or certain independent senior professionals.
eligibility: Faculties with regular service in public funded Universities/Deemed-to-be-Universities/Colleges, Institutes of National Importance as defined by MoE / UGC, and ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognized Institutes having a PhD degree are eligible to apply.
Post-Graduate (Regular)/PhD/PDF scholars in Social Science disciplines who are in the advanced stage of their studies/research are eligible to apply.

Independent scholars having served as Civil servants, officers from Defence services, and other professionals with a social science perspective having not less than 20 years of regular service and demonstrable research experience through publications of books/research papers/reports/policy documents, etc. may also apply.
coverage: Air travel (economy class, purchased through the three government approved travel agencies)
Visa fee
Travel insurance
Local conveyance
Maintenance costs for the period of stay abroad (not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates)
Registration fee up to US$200

Up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit for regular faculty; the full cost of the visit may be considered for SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability and PG/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection, and for faculties from ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognised Institutes
benefits: Preference is given to younger scholars, scholars attending a conference or seminar for the first time, and scholars from remote and backward areas.

Invitations from global subject associations, reputed international organisations, universities or institutions are given preference, and due consideration is given to the peer review process used by the conference organisers.
requirements: The application will be considered only when the paper for oral presentation has been accepted by the organiser of the Conference through a formal invite. A formal invitation letter should be submitted along with the application. A simple email will not be considered as a formal invite.
The submission of the full length paper to be presented is mandatory and it should be either in English or Hindi.

Applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference; the application will not be entertained or considered in any case after participation and presentation of the paper in the Conference.
If the paper is co-authored, priority will be given to the first author, but a No Objection Certificate(s) from the second author(s) may be procured and attached with the application.
Air tickets (economy class) must be purchased only from M/s Ashoka Travels and Tours (ATT), M/s Balmer Lawrie & Company Ltd (BLCL), or Indian Railways Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd (IRCTC).
Application for the second time will be considered only after a gap of three years, and a scholar can avail of the award only twice in his/her lifetime.
It is mandatory to buy tickets through the three government approved travel agencies; it is the scholar's own responsibility to arrange travel, visa and accommodation.
records.english_requirement: The full length paper to be presented is mandatory and should be either in English or Hindi.
application_method: Obtain a formal written invitation to present an oral paper at the international conference.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your paper has been formally accepted for ORAL presentation, and obtain a formal invitation letter - an emailed acceptance that the ICSSR does not accept as a formal invite is the single most common disqualifier.

Check you are in one of the eligible categories: regular faculty in a public funded university/deemed university/college, an Institute of National Importance, or an ICSSR research/recognised institute with a PhD; or a PG/PhD/postdoctoral scholar at an advanced stage of research; or an independent scholar with 20+ years of regular service as a civil servant, defence officer or similar professional with social science research output.

Make sure you are not applying for a poster presentation, to chair a session, as a convener or rapporteur, or to attend a workshop, training, refresher, summer or winter course - all of these are expressly ineligible.
Work backwards from the Conference due date: the online application must be uploaded at least three months before it.
Write or finalise your full-length paper in English or Hindi - submission of the full paper is mandatory.
If the paper is co-authored, you are most likely first author; obtain No Objection Certificates from the other author(s) and attach them.
Get your Head of Department or supervisor to forward/sign the hard copy application - applications not duly forwarded are rejected.
Register an account on https://app.icssr.org/ well before the three-month cut-off; postal delays are not the responsibility of the ICSSR.

If you are claiming full assistance (SC/ST, benchmark disability, or PG/doctoral/postdoctoral without salary protection), be ready to demonstrate you have received no financial assistance from other sources.
Plan your budget on the assumption that regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of total visit cost, with registration fee capped at US$200.
important_advice_for_students: Do not wait for a published ICSSR deadline - this scheme is open all year, but your real deadline is the Conference date minus three months.
Do not spend effort chasing a generic 'call for applications'; ICSSR advertises these travel grants on an open, rolling basis.
Do not apply if your participation is a poster, a chair role, or a course/workshop attendance; that is published as ineligible.
Do not buy air tickets yourself before you know the award position, and when you do, use only Ashoka Travels and Tours, Balmer Lawrie & Company, or IRCTC - economy class.
Do not skip the hard copy. The online submission is not sufficient; the printed application with all documents must reach ICSSR, and ICSSR is not responsible for postal delay or loss.
Remember the lifetime cap: you can take this award at most twice, and a second application is only considered after a three-year gap.
If you are a first-time conference presenter, younger scholar, or from a remote or backward area, say so in your application - these are published preference criteria.

Conference organised by an Indian organisation conducting seminars/conferences abroad - not eligible under this scheme.
Claiming full financial assistance without confirming no other financial assistance has been received.
A second application inside the three-year gap, or a third application in a lifetime.

The total expenditure on the foreign visit, including economy class airfare, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance and maintenance, is supported within the prescribed norms of Government notifications.

records.description: The AKF International Scholarship Programme funds postgraduate study for outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing their studies. Awards are structured as half grant and half loan, so 50 percent of the award amount must be repaid with a guarantor co-signing the agreement. The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses, but explicitly does not cover international travel, clothing, furniture, or living expenses for family members.
records.best_fit: High-achieving scholars from AKF ISP countries, including India, who are financially unable to fund postgraduate study themselves, are entering the first year of a Master's or PhD, and can show a credible multi-source funding plan.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must have excellent academic records, hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent, demonstrate genuine financial need, show a reliable multi-source funding plan covering all years, be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution, be starting the first year of the programme, and show strong leadership potential and achievements; preference is given to those under 30.
eligibility: have excellent academic records;
hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience;
demonstrate genuine financial need;
demonstrate a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study;
be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution;
be starting the first year of the programme; and
have strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Note: preference is given to young professionals under 30 years of age.

The programme is available in Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, and Uganda. In countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, applications are accepted from those who are originally from one of the countries listed above. At this time, AKF ISP is not available to students who wish to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.

benefits: For Master's studies, scholarships are granted for the entire duration of the degree course.

requirements: Awards are provided according to need, but the AKF ISP should be considered a resource of last resort; applicants should secure multiple sources of funding to reduce the amount requested.
Applicants must be entering their first year of study in a postgraduate programme. Students who have already enrolled in, or have commenced their postgraduate studies, are not eligible.
Applications for part-time programmes and short-term courses are not considered.
A guarantor is required to co-sign the award agreement.

Repayment of the loan component, which includes a service charge, begins six months after the first of the following events: a) graduation, b) termination of studies, or c) withdrawal of support following failure to meet the academic standards expected of ISP students.
To maintain an AKF ISP award, the award holder must demonstrate good academic standing as well as ongoing financial need during the course of the postgraduate programme.
application_method: Verify eligibility and find the local contact using the AKDN eligibility chatbot on the AKDN international scholarships page.
Contact the AKF team in the applicant's country, since applications are handled by contacts in countries where AKF ISP is available.
Apply through that local contact for the cycle, which opens annually; the 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next opens in early 2027.
If selected, obtain a guarantor to co-sign the award agreement before the award is confirmed.
records.selection_notes: Award recipients are selected through a global, annual and competitive application process. The AKF ISP offers a limited number of new awards in each cycle. The published criteria are academic record, financial need, quality of the funding plan, quality of the admitting institution, first-year status, and leadership and achievement profile, with preference given to young professionals under 30.
records.notes: Half grant, half loan: 50 percent of the award amount must be repaid, including a service charge, and a guarantor must co-sign the agreement. Repayment begins six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support for failing the expected academic standards. For PhD students the award covers the first two years only, after which alternative funding must be found, so it is not renewable beyond that. To keep the award, the holder must maintain good academic standing and demonstrate ongoing financial need. Study in the United Kingdom or Russia is not covered. Applications for part-time programmes and short-term courses are not considered.

official_details.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme (AKF ISP) is an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries, who have no other means of financing their studies, to pursue postgraduate education. Established in 1969 by His Highness the Aga Khan IV, the AKF ISP has supported more than 1,500 students to date. Award recipients are selected through a global, annual and competitive application process, and the programme offers a limited number of new awards in each cycle.

important_advice_for_students: Do not treat this as a full scholarship with no strings: 50 percent is a repayable loan with a service charge, and a guarantor must co-sign.
Do not apply if you have already started your postgraduate degree; first-year status is a hard eligibility requirement.
Do not apply to part-time or short-term programmes; they are excluded.
Do not ask for the full cost of your degree without showing other funding sources. The Foundation explicitly asks applicants to reduce the amount requested.

Do not wait for a printed deadline. The cycle opens in early 2027 and there is no published closing date; contact your local AKF office early in the window because applications run through country contacts.
If you are a PhD applicant, plan your own funding from year three onward - the award only covers the first two years.
Keep continuous evidence of financial need and academic standing; the award is withdrawn if these lapse.
common_rejection_risks: Applying when already enrolled in, or having commenced, the postgraduate programme.
Applying to a part-time programme or a short-term course.
Failing to demonstrate genuine financial need, or appearing not to be financially reliant on the award.
Presenting no multi-source funding plan, or a request for the full cost with no other sources identified.
Planning to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.
Being outside the AKF ISP country list without the required original nationality.
Having no guarantor available to co-sign the award agreement.
Applying to an institution that is not considered reputable, or to a distance-learning/local programme whose course quality cannot be maintained.
Missing the country contact's local window, since the global page publishes no closing date.
estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel to and from the study destination.
Clothing and furniture.
Living expenses for family members accompanying the scholar.
PhD study from year three onwards - alternative funding must be found.
Fifty percent of the award amount, plus a service charge, which is repaid after graduation or termination.

records.name: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students
records.official_source: University of Sharjah
records.region: United Arab Emirates (open to UAE nationals and non-nationals, with a separate CGPA threshold published for each)
records.duration: Tied to enrolment in a full master's degree programme; continuation is subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah. No scholarship duration is published.
records.deadline: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
records.application_period: Master's applications are open 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026 for the published 2026/2027 intake. The University publishes no separate RA/TA scholarship application window; it states that meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee a scholarship and that selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability and approval.
records.description: The University of Sharjah offers work-based Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant scholarships to eligible master's students, who must commit 20 hours per week at the University and may not be employed elsewhere during the scholarship period. The award is awarded by the concerned academic department based on its academic and research needs and available opportunities. The official page read does not publish the benefit amount, whether tuition is waived, or any list of expenses the scholarship covers, so this record is deliberately left unquantified rather than assumed to be full funding.
records.best_fit: Master's applicants with a very high undergraduate CGPA — 3.60 out of 4.00 for non-nationals, 3.20 for UAE nationals — who can commit 20 hours a week and are not employed elsewhere, and who can apply to a programme that is not on the published exclusion list.
records.eligibility_summary: Master's students holding a bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.60 out of 4.00 for non-nationals or 3.20 for UAE nationals, committed to 20 hours of work per week at the University and not employed outside it.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students.
Be committed to working 20 hours per week at the University as part of the scholarship requirements.
Not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period.
Meet any additional requirements established by the concerned academic department and the University.

Regular master's admission also requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent from a university recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR), a minimum CGPA of 3.00 out of 4.00, and a bachelor's degree in a field relevant to the intended master's program.
coverage: No coverage list is published on the official page read. The page states only that the University offers Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) scholarships to eligible Master's students, subject to the University's applicable bylaws, regulations, and available opportunities.
requirements: Scholarship eligibility and continuation are subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah.
Remedial courses are not covered by the scholarship.
Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award of a scholarship; selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability, and approval.
The concerned academic department reserves the right to select eligible candidates based on its academic and research needs and the applicable selection criteria.
Applicants to Master's programs taught in English must obtain TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL PBT 550, or IELTS Academic 6.0.
The University does not accept Home Edition or other online home-based English language proficiency examinations.
AED 500 non-refundable application fee.

Applicants nominated for admission must reserve their seat by paying AED 10,000 within the specified deadline; the amount paid is applied toward tuition fees upon enrollment, and on withdrawal or non-enrollment AED 5,000 is non-refundable.
records.english_requirement: Applicants to Master's programs taught in English must obtain one of the following minimum scores: TOEFL iBT 79; TOEFL PBT 550; IELTS Academic 6.0. Applicants to the Master of Applied Sociology, Master in Private Law, Master in Public Law, Master in Conservation Management of Cultural Heritage, and Master of Arts in Applied Criminology and Criminal Justice must either obtain a minimum TOEFL ITP score of 450, or its equivalent, or a minimum IELTS Academic score of 4.5, or successfully complete the prescribed English language course (ESL - 0 credit hours) during the first semester; students who do not satisfy the requirement by the end of the first semester will not be permitted to continue in the program. For Master's programs taught in Arabic, English language proficiency is not required unless specifically required by the selected program. English language proficiency test results are valid for two years from the date of the examination. The University does not accept Home Edition or other online home-based English language proficiency examinations.
application_method: Discover your program and select a college to view the master's programs and specializations offered.
Check your eligibility against the regular and conditional master's admission requirements.
Complete the required English language test, or provide official proof the bachelor's degree was taught in English.
Get your documents ready (passport, certified bachelor's certificate and transcript, photograph, Emirates ID, recommendation letters, MoHESR equivalence where applicable).
Explore scholarships and benefits, including RA/TA scholarship eligibility and the programme exclusion list.

Submit the online application through the University of Sharjah Online Admission Portal, upload all required documents, and pay the AED 500 non-refundable application fee between 5 October 2026 and 12 November 2026.
If nominated for admission, reserve the seat by paying AED 10,000 within the specified deadline.
records.selection_notes: The concerned academic department reserves the right to select eligible candidates based on its academic and research needs and the applicable selection criteria. Selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability, and approval; meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award of a scholarship.
records.notes: The scholarship carries a 20 hours-per-week work commitment at the University, and the holder must not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period. Remedial courses are not covered. Nine master's programmes are barred from RA/TA eligibility (all five Master of Dental Surgery programmes, Master of Science in Leadership in Health Professions Education, Master of Leadership in Higher Education, Executive Master in Business Administration, Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)), and the Master of Science in Molecular Medicine and Translational Research is eligible for Research Assistant scholarship only. No deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction terms are published. No tuition, housing, insurance or travel coverage is stated on the official page read, and the AED 500 application fee and AED 10,000 seat reservation are not described as scholarship-covered.

Programmes not eligible for RA/TA scholarships: Master of Dental Surgery in Orthodontics; Master of Dental Surgery in Oral Surgery; Master of Dental Surgery in Endodontics; Master of Dental Surgery in Periodontology; Master of Dental Surgery in Prosthodontics; Master of Science in Leadership in Health Professions Education; Master of Leadership in Higher Education; Executive Master in Business Administration; Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD).
The Master of Science in Molecular Medicine and Translational Research is eligible for a Research Assistant scholarship only and not for a Teaching Assistant scholarship.

Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee an award - the department may decline even eligible candidates.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students.

alerts.message: Master's applications open. Complete the English test, MoHESR equivalence and two recommendation letters first so the file is ready on day one.
Last day to submit the online application, upload documents and pay the AED 500 non-refundable application fee.
Pay the AED 10,000 seat reservation within the specified deadline; AED 5,000 is non-refundable on withdrawal or non-enrollment.
Ask the concerned academic department for the current RA/TA benefit terms in writing, because the public page publishes no stipend figure and no tuition rule.

submission_workflow: Confirm the programme is RA/TA eligible.
Secure the qualifying English score (test-centre format only).
Obtain MoHESR equivalence if the degree is from outside the UAE.
Collect the certified certificate and transcript, photograph, passport copy, Emirates ID and two recommendation letters.
Submit the online application via the University of Sharjah Online Admission Portal and upload the documents.
Pay the AED 500 non-refundable application fee.
Watch for the admission-status email within 7 working days.
If nominated, pay the AED 10,000 seat reservation before the stated deadline.
post_award_requirements: Complete 20 hours per week of University work for the duration of the scholarship.
Do not take outside employment during the scholarship period.
Remain compliant with the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah, which govern scholarship eligibility and continuation.
Pay any remaining tuition fees within the specified deadline and in accordance with the University's financial regulations.
No return-home, deferral or renewal obligation is published; confirm continuing obligations with the College of Graduate Studies.

Can the 20-hour weekly commitment be arranged in the morning shift alongside a part-time master's programme?

Is the scholarship renewable, and what happens if the student's performance or department changes?

records.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate study at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. AfDB states it covers tuition for the 24-month study programme, a monthly living stipend, air travel between the scholar's home country and the host university at the start and end of the scholarship period, and health insurance usually obtained through the university, plus an additional six months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation. It is not complete funding in AfDB's own terms: the Bank publishes an explicit exclusion list covering visa application costs, family members, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the study programme, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central call date, so the amount and the closing date must both be confirmed with the chosen partner university and the JADS Secretariat.
records.program_type: Government scholarship (multilateral - African Development Bank and the Government of Japan)
records.best_fit: Citizens of an African Development Bank regional member country who are 35 or younger and in good health, hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or a related field with an excellent academic record, and have at least one year of paid employment in their home country or another African country obtained within the past three years of completing that degree. Applicants must already be able to apply to an approved master's course at a JADS partner university, must not be enrolled in another graduate degree programme, and cannot be AfDB Group staff or a close relative of AfDB Group staff.
records.funding_period: Monthly living stipend for the duration of the study program (24 months), or the duration of the graduate program if shorter
records.eligibility_summary: Must be 35 or younger, in good health, a citizen of an African Development Bank regional member country, hold a relevant bachelor's degree with an excellent academic record plus at least one year of paid employment earned within the past three years, and secure admission to an approved master's course at a JADS partner university.
eligibility: Should have a minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering studies or related areas; and have excellent academic records and relevant professional experience, and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts.

Applicants should have at least 1 year of paid employment in their home country or in other African countries after receiving their Bachelors (or equivalent university) degree within the past 3 years.
Candidates should be 35 years old or younger, and in good health.

Candidates should gain admission to an approved master's degree course at a Japanese or African partner university - application for admission to be done directly through the partner universities (Refer to list of universities and approved courses).
Candidates should not be enrolled in another graduate degree programs - the program does not support applicants who are already enrolled in graduate degree programs.
Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries.

Applicants must not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of all types of appointments of the African Development Bank Group or a close relative of the aforementioned by blood or adoption with the term "close relative" defined as: Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew.

Note published on the AfDB eligibility page: "All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to unless otherwise communicated. Eligibility criteria will not change during an open call for applications. However, this information is subject to change between the close of one application process and the opening of the next."

records.selection_notes: All eligible applications are comparatively evaluated by the Program Implementation Unit hired by the African Development Bank, and the final selection is approved by the JADS Secretariat. Evaluation focuses on educational and professional excellence, commitment to home country development priorities, the quality of the statement of purpose, financial status and geographic diversity of awardees. The Bank's management decision and approval of the finalist also takes into consideration geographical diversity, gender balance, equity and inclusiveness (unusual circumstances or hardships when assessing employment experience), financial needs (applicants are financially constrained), and special consideration for applicants with special needs.
records.notes: There is no separate application to the African Development Bank - "Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program", and a university admission offer alone is not a scholarship award. The scholarship "may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support/fellowship you might have"; finalists and awardees must inform the JADS Secretariat of other funding, and "The JADS stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if during the scholarship period the program has evidence of additional sources of support." Deferral and renewal are not addressed on the AfDB pages. Scholars "are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development, using the newly acquired knowledge and skills." No clinical or field-of-practice restriction is published, but the approved master's courses are limited to energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering and related areas. "The scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less."

official_details.description: "The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building program by the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan. The overarching goal of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan is to enhance human resources capacity in Africa, in keeping with the Bank's High 5 strategic priorities, namely Feed Africa, Light up and power Africa, Industrialize Africa, Integrate Africa, and Improve the quality of life of the people of Africa. These priorities are also in line with key Japanese development assistance initiatives. The program offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship opportunity to pursue post-graduate studies at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, and engineering."

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of an African Development Bank regional member country before anything else - this is the first gate.
Confirm you are 35 years old or younger and in good health on the date you apply.

Confirm you hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or a related field, with the academic record and professional experience to match.

Confirm you have at least 1 year of paid employment in your home country or another African country, earned within the 3 years after your bachelor's degree, and start collecting proof of employment for every job in that period.
Shortlist an approved JADS partner university and the exact approved master's course, using the AfDB List of Universities page, before contacting anyone.
Contact the partner university using the contacts published on the AfDB List of Universities page and request its application forms, procedure and current dates.
Take the TOEFL iBT or TOEC English proficiency test and keep the result, because AfDB names it as a preparation step.
Write the research plan and proposal, and identify two professional referees in advance.
Do not apply to the African Development Bank directly and do not pay any application fee to the Bank - AfDB states no separate application to the Bank is necessary.
important_advice_for_students: Do not treat a university admission offer as a scholarship offer. AfDB states plainly: "Admission by the JADS partner university does not mean that you have been accepted for scholarship support; accordingly you should not take any action with respect to your current employment or otherwise, until you have been informed by the African Development Bank that you have been awarded the scholarship."
Do not apply directly to the African Development Bank. There is no Bank-side JADS form or portal, and the Bank warns this is the only route.

Do not wait for a single central deadline. AfDB publishes no central call date; the dates belong to the partner universities, and they differ widely between October and the following spring, so drive the schedule from the university you have chosen.
Do not carry undeclared outside funding. The programme supplements and never duplicates other support, and the stipend can be withdrawn wholly or partly if other funding is found during the award.

Do not budget on the assumption that everything is paid. Visa application costs, family travel and support, extra-curricular courses, additional travel, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers are all excluded.
Do not plan on the 24 months being flexible. The scholarship covers the duration of the graduate programme or two years, whichever is less, so overrun beyond the approved course length is not funded.
Do not assume the stipend figure - AfDB publishes none, so get the current monthly amount in writing from the partner university or the JADS Secretariat before you commit.
Do not ignore the age limit of 35 or the one-year-paid-employment-in-the-past-three-years rule; both are stated as strictly adhered to, and criteria are fixed for the duration of an open call.
common_rejection_risks: Not a citizen of an African Development Bank regional member country.
Older than 35 at the point of application.
No bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in an approved field, or an academic record that does not meet the "excellent academic records" standard.
No 1 year of paid employment in the home country or another African country within the past 3 years after the bachelor's degree, or no proof of that employment supplied.
Already enrolled in another graduate degree programme.
Applying to the African Development Bank instead of, or as well as, the partner university - such an application is not considered.
Applying for a course that is not on the approved programme list for the chosen partner university.
Being an AfDB Group staff member, Executive Director, alternate, or a close relative by blood or adoption of such a person.
Not in good health, where health is assessed at selection.
Missing or uncertified copies of the most advanced university degree certificate.
Failing the English proficiency step (TOEFL iBT or TOEC).
Providing only one professional reference where two are required.

submission_workflow: Read the JADS pages on afdb.org and the eligibility criteria in full.
Pick an approved JADS partner university and approved master's course from the published list.
Request that university's information, forms and procedures using the published contact.
Assemble the CV, all employment proofs since the bachelor's degree, and a certified copy of the highest degree certificate.
Identify two professional referees and prepare the research plan and proposal.
Sit the TOEFL iBT or TOEC test and hold the score report.
Submit the application for admission to the partner university within that university's published window.
Await the university's provisional offer letter; the university then forwards your name to the African Development Bank.
The Bank's Program Implementation Unit evaluates and the JADS Secretariat approves; the Bank then contacts successful candidates and informs the universities.
Take no employment or relocation action until the Bank confirms the award.
post_award_requirements: The scholarship is time-limited to the duration of the graduate programme or two years, whichever is less - there is no published renewal or extension mechanism.
Scholars are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development after completing their studies.
Any other source of financial support must be declared to the JADS Secretariat; undisclosed support can lead to the stipend being withdrawn completely or partially.
AfDB publishes no progress-reporting or publication obligation for scholars, and no deferral rule.
questions_to_ask_host: Which JADS-approved master's courses are open for the next intake, and which of them are in my field?

records.name: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders (2027 Fellowship)

records.application_period: Application opened 22 September 2026 and closes at 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026 for the 2027 Fellowship. Semi-finalists are interviewed by U.S. embassies and consulates from October 2026 to January 2027; applicants are notified of their status in February/March 2027; visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities for finalists run from March to May 2027; the Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027, with institutes running from mid-June through early August 2027.
records.description: The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the flagship programme of the U.S. Government's Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI) and the exchange component of that initiative. It brings up to 550 young African leaders to the United States in the summer of 2027 for a six-week executive-style institute at a U.S. college or university, placed in groups of approximately 25, with an academic track of Business and Trade, Emerging Technologies, or Governance and Security. The 2027 instructions state that "If you are selected for the Fellowship, the U.S. Government will cover all program costs", listing J-1 visa support, round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States plus required domestic U.S. travel, the six-week institute, a limited accident and sickness benefit plan, housing and meals, and the optional four-week Professional Development Experience for up to 50 Fellows. It is not a degree programme and no tuition is charged or funded, and the U.S. Government does not pay for a Fellow's salary while away from work or for personal purchases. The programme is fully cost-covered for the six-week (or ten-week with PDE) stay, with no application fee.
records.program_type: Government scholarship (U.S. Department of State educational and cultural exchange programme, administered by IREX)
records.best_fit: Citizens and permanent residents of any of the 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries, aged 25 to 35 on the application deadline of 13 October 2026 (exceptional applicants aged 21-24 may be considered), proficient in reading, writing and speaking English, with a proven record of accomplishment in business and trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and with a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants must not be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, must be eligible for a U.S. J-1 visa, must not be U.S. Government employees or their immediate family, and must not be alumni or prior participants of the Fellowship.
