requirements: Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; "Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered."
You must complete all fields marked with a red asterisk (*).
You must answer all application questions in English, and answers must reflect your own experiences and ideas.

You do not have to finish your application in one session. You may save your work and return as many times as necessary; however "Once you have submitted your application, however, you can no longer add any additional information or make any changes."
All answers in the application, including written responses to essays and optional PDE questions, must be your own original work, based on your own creativity and effort.

Your application will be disqualified if you copy language from other Fellowship applications (including those of other applicants or Fellowship alumni) or from other sources (including websites or blogs), as this is considered plagiarism.

Responsible use of technology is permitted with transparency: "If you use any technology (including AI) to help prepare your responses, you must disclose this where asked in the application, and you remain responsible for the content you submit."

In the online application system, after fully completing a section it will be marked as "Completed." When all required sections are marked as "Completed," click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard; your application is not complete until you submit it.
If selected as a semi-finalist, you must provide a copy of your international passport (if available) or other government-issued photo identification at the interview.
If your technical eligibility for the Fellowship changes at any point, you must email MWFellowship@irex.org, as well as your local U.S. embassy or consulate, immediately.
The Fellowship Terms and Conditions require all Fellows to attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by their institute.

All individuals who are selected for the Fellowship will be required to have a passport from an eligible Fellowship country that is valid through at least February 28, 2028, or through March 31, 2028, if selected for the Professional Development Experience.
records.english_requirement: Published and mandatory. Applicants must be "proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English" and the instructions state "High-level proficiency in written and spoken English is required for the Fellowship", because "All activities - including academic sessions, discussions, meetings, cultural activities, and social interactions - will be in English." Applicants complete a self-assessment against the levels Absolute Beginner, Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, or Very Advanced; no standardized English test score is required. Applicants who are deaf should indicate proficiency in reading and writing standard English and proficiency in American Sign Language, and are told that "interpretation in the United States may only be available in ASL, so selected Fellows who are deaf should be proficient in, or be prepared to learn, ASL prior to arrival in the United States."
application_method: Download and read the 2027 Application Instructions before beginning the application.

Access the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org using a computer, tablet or mobile device; the system works in low-bandwidth environments, on non-Apple and non-Android devices, and is accessible and compatible with screen readers for applicants who are blind or have low vision.
Complete the Eligibility section, which must be fully completed to continue; applicants who do not meet all technical eligibility requirements will not be able to participate in the 2027 Fellowship.
Complete the General Information and Résumé/CV sections; the instructions recommend completing the Résumé/CV before moving on because its entries automatically populate later sections.
Complete the optional Demographic Information section, used for statistical purposes only and not considered in selection.
Complete Contact Information, Current Professional and/or Educational Experience, YALI Engagement, Previous U.S. Experience, and English Language sections.
Complete Institute Track and Sector Alignment, including ranking the three tracks and the 200-word maximum essay on why the first-choice track fits.
Complete the Leadership Assessment and Personal Statements sections, including the four essay questions.
Optionally apply for the Professional Development Experience and answer the three additional PDE essays.
Complete the Technology Use Disclosure.

Check that all required sections show as "Completed", then click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard. All submitted applications are final and cannot be changed by any means.
records.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored against the published criteria: proficiency speaking, reading and writing in English; a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security; a demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals; a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents; the ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others; strong social and communication skills; and demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements "will not be forwarded to the selection committee." Semi-finalists are then interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027. Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa. The U.S. Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", requiring documentation of age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage; any discrepancy or false information means "the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible." PDE applicants are assessed separately on the ability to work professionally in a U.S. organization, articulation of clear and specific learning goals, flexibility, alignment between professional background, institute track and potential U.S. organizations, interest in sustaining engagement with U.S. professionals, and strong English proficiency.
records.notes: This is a non-degree exchange programme, so no tuition is charged or funded and no degree is awarded. It is not deferrable, not renewable, and a Fellow cannot re-apply: the technical eligibility rules exclude "alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship". The programme requires a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa, and applicants must be residents of an eligible country as of February 1, 2027 and at the start of the Fellowship in June 2027. "Fellows are not allowed to have dependents, including spouses and children, accompany them during the Fellowship." There is no clinical or field-of-practice restriction. Selected Fellows must complete a detailed Medical History Form and, if applicable, an Accommodations Form, and the programme "strongly encourages all eligible applicants to apply regardless of your medical history or accommodations you may require." Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions receive reasonable accommodations and support at no cost. Fellows must attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities, and housing may be shared: "Every effort will be made to provide single-occupancy housing; however, Fellows may share a double-occupancy bedroom with another Fellow of the same sex and a bathroom with one or more Fellows of the same sex." The U.S. Department of State and IREX reserve the right to alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time, and selection of finalists may be reviewed case by case for nationals of countries subject to a U.S. entry or visa suspension.

Fellowship activities prepare Fellows to collaborate with U.S. citizens on advancing U.S.-Africa trade and economic prosperity, promoting technological innovation, and enhancing peace and security. The Mandela Washington Fellowship is a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX."

All applications are submitted in one national open competition to apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org by 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026; the subsequent steps (embassy/consulate interview, notification, visa processing) are not applicant deadlines.
official_details.funding_label: U.S. Government funded - all program costs covered
official_details.tuition_coverage: Not applicable. The Fellowship is a non-degree exchange programme; no tuition is charged by the host institutions and none is funded. "the U.S. Government will cover all program costs."
official_details.living_cost_coverage: "Housing and meals during the program". "Fellows will be housed in university housing or similar accommodations that are appropriate for professional adults. Every effort will be made to provide single-occupancy housing; however, Fellows may share a double-occupancy bedroom with another Fellow of the same sex and a bathroom with one or more Fellows of the same sex. Most meals will be provided at campus cafeterias or restaurants, though Fellows may have access to a shared kitchen to cook some meals." For PDE Fellows, the PDE "will include support for housing, meals, and transportation".
official_details.travel_coverage: "Round-trip travel from Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program. Fellows must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa to the United States"
official_details.tuition_rule: Not applicable - no tuition is charged or funded because the Fellowship is a non-degree exchange programme.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Not published and not applicable, since the Fellowship is for working professionals and young leaders rather than enrolled degree students.
official_details.host_institution_fee: None published. The instructions state that "There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship" and that the U.S. Government covers all program costs, with no host university charge listed.
covered_expenses: J-1 visa support
Round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program
A six-week institute
A limited accident and sickness benefit plan
Housing and meals during the program
An optional four-week Professional Development Experience (for up to 50 Fellows), including support for housing, meals, and transportation
Reasonable accommodations and support at no cost for Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions
Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and the visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa for finalists
not_covered_or_excluded: "funds to cover Fellows' salaries while they are away from work"
"funds for personal purchases, such as support for Fellows' home organizations or gifts for family"
Any application fee: the programme states "There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship" - the absence of a fee is a benefit, but no cost is reimbursed either
Anything beyond the programme itself: "The Fellowship is not designed to help Fellows identify specific funding for projects or organizations."
Dependents: "Fellows are not allowed to have dependents, including spouses and children, accompany them during the Fellowship."
benefits: Six-week institute at a leading U.S. educational institution, in a group of approximately 25 Fellows, in urban and rural locations
Three academic tracks: Business and Trade; Emerging Technologies; Governance and Security
Academic sessions, site visits, networking, community service and cultural activities
Facilitated networking with established leaders from American businesses and industries

Optional four-week Professional Development Experience at a U.S. business, non-profit organization or government agency, competitively selected for up to 50 Fellows, with support for housing, meals and transportation
Access to an alumni network of nearly 7,800 alumni, with ongoing in-person and virtual professional development, networking and collaboration
Eligibility for Reciprocal Exchanges and other alumni opportunities
Reasonable accommodations and support at no cost for Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions

Are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the United States
Are eligible to receive a United States J-1 visa

Are proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English (applicants who are deaf should refer to the English Language instructions below)

Are citizens of one of the following countries: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, or Zimbabwe
Are residents of one of the above countries, and will be permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027, and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027
Are not alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship
general_eligibility: Age: 25-35 as of 13 October 2026; exceptional applicants aged 21-24 may be considered
Citizenship: citizen of one of 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries
Residency: resident of one of the above countries, permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027 and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027
Language: proficient in reading, writing and speaking English
Immigration: eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa
Travel: must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa to the United States
Passport (for finalists only): must hold a passport from an eligible Fellowship country valid through at least February 28, 2028, or through March 31, 2028 if selected for the PDE
Employment level: the application asks for the level of the current or most recent professional position (entry-level, mid-level non-supervisory, mid-level supervisory, or executive)
ineligibility_conditions: U.S. citizens and U.S. permanent residents are not eligible.
Alumni and prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship are not eligible.
Employees of the U.S. Government, including a U.S. embassy or consulate or other U.S. Government entity, and their immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, or siblings) are not eligible.

Current IREX employees and consultants and their immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, and siblings) are not eligible to apply for any IREX-implemented grant programs, either as individuals or as the responsible party representing an institutional applicant.
Anyone who is not eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa is not eligible.
Applicants who fail any technical eligibility requirement "will not be forwarded to the selection committee" and "will not be able to participate in the 2027 Fellowship".

Applications containing plagiarised content are disqualified: "The U.S. Department of State and IREX will be checking all applications for originality and plagiarism, and those who plagiarize their application materials will be disqualified."

Applications with false or unverifiable information: "In the event of a discrepancy, or if information found to be false, the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible."
Applicants whose date of birth does not appear in the dates provided within the application are not eligible to participate.
Applicants who fail the technical requirements are directed to other U.S. Department of State Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs exchange opportunities and the YALI Network instead.
official_details.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of one of 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries and residents of that country, permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027 and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027. The published list is: Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Republic of the Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe. Fellows must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa.
official_details.international_eligibility: Open to African citizens and residents only; U.S. citizens and permanent residents are excluded. Nationals of countries subject to a full or partial suspension of entry to or visa issuance from the United States "are eligible to apply, but selection of finalists from these countries will be considered on a case-by-case basis."
host_requirements: Fellows are "placed in groups of approximately 25 at leading educational institutions across the United States in both urban and rural areas" - host institutions are assigned, not chosen by the applicant.
Institutes will take place "from mid-June through early August 2027", and "each program agenda is unique and is based on the particular strengths and resources of each institute".
Each institute's academic curriculum and programming "will focus on one of three tracks: Business and Trade, Emerging Technologies, or Governance and Security".
"The Fellowship Terms and Conditions require all Fellows to attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by their institute."

For the PDE component, Fellows "must be available to be in the United States for a total of approximately 10 weeks" and placements "are typically not an exact match to their current position at home".
Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa.
requirements: Submit through the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; email and other submission methods are not accepted.
Complete all fields marked with a red asterisk (*).
Answer all application questions in English, with answers reflecting your own experiences and ideas.

Rank the three institute tracks in order of preference, and note that "if selected, you may not be placed in your first-choice track, but you may be placed in a different track that, based on your application materials, fits your profile."
Complete the Résumé/CV section before later sections, because its entries automatically populate them.

Answer the required essay questions within their word limits: 350 words maximum (significant professional accomplishment from the past 24 months), 250 words maximum (a specific challenge in your professional sector), 250 words maximum (a partnership with a U.S. organization to build after the Fellowship), 150 words maximum (a difficult or unpopular decision), and 200 words maximum (why the first-choice track fits). "You will have between 150 and 350 words to answer each of the long essay questions."

Optionally apply for the PDE with three additional essays: 150 words maximum (overview of current role and long-term career goals), 250 words maximum (two or three transferable skills to strengthen), 250 words maximum (how participation would benefit a U.S. host organization).
Complete the Technology Use Disclosure, listing the different types of technology used to prepare the application and how they were used.
Disclose any use of technology, including AI, "where asked in the application".
Provide documentation verifying age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage if selected as a semi-finalist.
documents: Full legal name as spelled on the passport and/or official government-issued identification
Date of birth as it appears on the passport and/or official government-issued identification
Biological sex as it appears on the passport and/or official government-issued identification
Country of current residence and country of permanent residence prior to the Fellowship if selected as semi-finalist
Passport details: country of issue and expiration date (a passport is not required to apply, but is required of finalists)
Contact details: phone number, email address and postal address; an alternate email address is highly recommended

Résumé/CV: up to five professional positions, up to five educational institutions, up to five professional trainings or certifications, up to five community or volunteer roles, up to 10 awards/honors/fellowships/grants/scholarships, up to eight languages and/or up to 10 computer or software skills, publications/conferences/presentations, and associations and affiliations
English language self-assessment: native-language indicator plus proficiency level (Absolute Beginner, Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, Very Advanced) for each skill

Current professional and/or educational experience, including the highest level of education completed or to be completed by June 2027, up to six sectors of expertise and/or interest, and professional level (entry-level, mid-level non-supervisory, mid-level supervisory, executive)
YALI engagement information and previous U.S. experience, including dates of entry and exit, visa type and purpose for each previous U.S. trip
Institute Track and Sector Alignment: ranked track preferences and selected sectors
Leadership Assessment responses (Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often, Very Often for each activity)
Personal Statements: four required essay answers plus the 200-word track-fit essay
Optional PDE application with three additional essays
Technology Use Disclosure
document_format_rules: Size limits: none are published. The 2027 instructions specify per-entry word limits rather than file-size limits, and no résumé file upload is described - the Résumé/CV is entered directly into the online application system.
Accepted file types: none are published, because the instructions describe entering all information into the online application system rather than uploading documents.

Word limits published: long essay questions 150-350 words each, with individual maximums of 350 (professional accomplishment), 250 (sector challenge), 250 (U.S. partnership), 150 (difficult decision) and 200 (first-choice track fit); PDE essays 150, 250 and 250 words maximum.

Per-entry word limits in the Résumé/CV: up to 100 words required for each professional position, up to 100 words optional for each educational programme, training/certification, community or volunteer role, and award or honor; up to five entries per professional/education/training/volunteer category and up to 10 awards.

Translation rules: "All information must be entered in English" and "All responses must be written in English." Translation applications may be used with disclosure: "Responsible use of technology is permitted with transparency. Many applicants use spell-check, grammar support, translation applications, or other technology to help with clarity or language mechanics; however, the substance of your responses ... must be your own. If you use any technology (including AI) to help prepare your responses, you must disclose this where asked in the application, and you remain responsible for the content you submit."

Originality rules: all answers "must be your own original work, based on your own creativity and effort", and copying language from other Fellowship applications, other applicants, Fellowship alumni, websites or blogs is plagiarism that leads to disqualification.

Date rules: date of birth "as it appears on your passport and/or official government-issued identification", and "If your birth date does not appear in the dates provided within the application, you are not eligible to participate." Employment and education entries require "Start and end dates"; awards require "Date received"; previous U.S. travel requires dates of entry and exit.

Identity rules: the full legal name and biological sex "as spelled on your passport and/or official government-issued identification"; the semi-finalist must present a copy of the international passport (if available) or other government-issued photo identification at the interview, and a photo-ID document to verify date of birth.
Signature rules: none are published. The application is submitted electronically through the online system with no signature requirement.
selection_criteria: Proficiency speaking, reading, and writing in English
A proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance, and/or security
A demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals
A commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents to build and serve their communities
The ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others
Strong social and communication skills
Demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments
official_details.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored according to the criteria above. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements are not forwarded to the selection committee. Semi-finalists are interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027 and must present photo identification and, if they have one, their passport. Applicants are notified in February/March 2027. Selected finalists attend mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa, with visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities from March to May 2027. PDE applicants are reviewed separately against their own published criteria, and up to 50 Fellows are selected. The Department of State and IREX reserve the right to verify all application information and may alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time.
application_method: Download and read the 2027 Application Instructions.
Access the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org from a computer, tablet or mobile device.
Fully complete the Eligibility section - this is a gate: failure means you cannot participate in the 2027 Fellowship.
Complete General Information and Résumé/CV (recommended early, because entries auto-populate later sections).
Complete the optional Demographic Information section (statistical purposes only, not used in selection).
Complete Contact Information, Current Professional and/or Educational Experience, YALI Engagement, Previous U.S. Experience, and English Language.
Complete Institute Track and Sector Alignment, including the 200-word track-fit essay.
Complete the Leadership Assessment.
Complete Personal Statements, including the four required essays within their word limits.
Optionally apply for the PDE and answer the three additional PDE essays.
Complete the Technology Use Disclosure.

Verify that every required section is marked "Completed" and click "Submit Application" at the bottom of the application dashboard before 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on 13 October 2026. Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered.
application_steps: Read the 2027 Application Instructions and the Application FAQs.

Confirm technical eligibility: age, citizenship, residence, English proficiency, J-1 visa eligibility, and that you are not a U.S. citizen, U.S. Government employee or relative, or a Fellowship alumnus.
Register and start an application in the online system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org.
Complete and pass the Eligibility section.
Complete General Information and the Résumé/CV in full.
Complete the remaining required sections, including the English Language self-assessment and the Leadership Assessment.
Write the personal statements in English within the published word limits, using your own original work and disclosing any technology or AI assistance.
Optionally apply for the four-week Professional Development Experience.
Complete the Technology Use Disclosure.
Review the whole application for completeness, then submit through the online system. "All submitted applications are final."

If selected as a semi-finalist, present photo identification and your passport (if available) at the embassy or consulate interview in your home country, and be ready to document your age, citizenship and residency.
If selected as a finalist, attend the mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation and the visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa.
applicant_submission_route: Direct submission by the applicant through the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org

No institutional nomination, employer letter, university reference or referee submission route is described in the 2027 instructions; "Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered."
award_holder_conditions: Fellows are committed to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents to build and serve their communities (a published selection criterion, and a technical eligibility condition is that the applicant will be permanently residing in an eligible country as of February 1, 2027 and in June 2027).
"The Fellowship Terms and Conditions require all Fellows to attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by their institute."
Selected Fellows must have a valid passport from an eligible Fellowship country, valid through at least February 28, 2028 (through March 31, 2028 if selected for the PDE).
Selected Fellows must complete a detailed Medical History Form and, if applicable, an Accommodations Form.
Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa.
PDE Fellows must be available for approximately 10 weeks in total in the United States and must dedicate preparation time before the PDE starts.
Fellows must not bring dependents: "Fellows are not allowed to have dependents, including spouses and children, accompany them during the Fellowship."
The U.S. Department of State and IREX reserve the right to verify all information included in the application and to alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time.
arrival_rules: "Fellows must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa to the United States"
Round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States is funded, as is domestic U.S. travel as required by the program.
The Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027; institutes run from mid-June through early August 2027.
Selected finalists complete visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities from March to May 2027, including a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa and mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your date of birth against 13 October 2026: you must be 25-35, or 21-24 for an exceptional candidate.
Check that you are a citizen AND resident of one of the 49 listed countries, and that you will still be permanently resident there on 1 February 2027 and in June 2027.

Check you are not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, not a U.S. Government employee (including at any embassy or consulate) or their spouse/parent/child/sibling, not an IREX employee or consultant or their immediate family, and not a Mandela Washington Fellow or alumnus.
Confirm you can realistically obtain a U.S. J-1 visa.
Apply only through apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; there is no application fee and no other accepted route.
Complete the Résumé/CV section before anything else, because its entries auto-populate later sections and you will be asked for more detail later.
Gather your passport-style identity details now: full legal name, date of birth and biological sex exactly as they appear on your passport or government ID.

Start your Résumé/CV entries with the facts in hand: up to five professional positions, up to five education entries, up to five trainings/certifications, up to five volunteer roles, up to 10 awards, up to eight languages and up to 10 software skills.
Draft the four required essays offline with their word limits in view (350 / 250 / 250 / 150 words) plus the 200-word track-fit essay, and check every one is in your own words.

Decide now whether you will apply for the optional PDE, because "Applicants who do not indicate they wish to be considered for the PDE in the application will not be able to apply for this component separately."
Do the English self-assessment honestly, and start your technical English work now if you are below Advanced.
Add an alternate email address to your contact details and check that email and phone regularly during the selection period.
Save and return to the application as often as you need; nothing is lost until you submit.
Submit well before 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on 13 October 2026, and confirm the success message appears.
important_advice_for_students: Do not email your application. The instructions are explicit that "Applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered."

Do not edit after submitting. "All submitted applications are final. Once you have submitted your application, you can no longer add any additional information or make any changes, either through the online system or via email."
Do not miss the time. The deadline is 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026, not midnight local time; a few hours of difference can cost the whole application.

Do not copy wording from other applications, from alumni, from websites or from blogs. "The U.S. Department of State and IREX will be checking all applications for originality and plagiarism, and those who plagiarize their application materials will be disqualified."
Do not hide AI or translation help. It is permitted with disclosure. Disclose it in the Technology Use Disclosure and keep the substance, examples and reasoning your own.

Do not expect to be placed in your first-choice track. The instructions warn you "may be placed in a different track that, based on your application materials, fits your profile", so rank honestly and write a track-fit essay that survives being moved.
Do not treat this as a degree scholarship. There is no tuition, no credit and no qualification; the return value is a professional network, alumni access and PDE placement.
Do not plan on being paid while you are away. The U.S. Government will not cover your salary, and it will not fund support for your home organisation or gifts for your family.
Do not skip the résumé section's optional 100-word descriptions. They are optional, but they are the only place you can show scale, results and context.
Do not bring or plan for family to travel with you. Dependents, including spouses and children, are not allowed to accompany Fellows.
Do not skip the résumé's publication section formatting advice: Chicago Manual of Style citations are "recommended, but ... not required", so a plain list is acceptable.
Do not ignore the medical and accommodation step. If selected you must complete a Medical History Form and an Accommodations Form if applicable; disclosure does not count against you.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting after 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on 13 October 2026, or by email or any non-system route.
Failing a technical eligibility requirement, which means the application "will not be forwarded to the selection committee".
Being a U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Being an alumnus or prior participant of the Fellowship.
Being a U.S. Government employee or the spouse, parent, child or sibling of one, or an IREX employee/consultant or their immediate family member.
Age outside 25-35 on the deadline date, where the 21-24 exceptional route is not met.
A date of birth that "does not appear in the dates provided within the application".
Plagiarised content, including wording lifted from another applicant's application, from alumni, from websites or from blogs.
A mismatch or false information: the Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", and a discrepancy immediately voids the application.
Missing mandatory red-asterisk fields or an unsubmitted application: "your application is not considered complete until you submit it."
Answers that do not demonstrate your own English proficiency, which is both an eligibility requirement and a scoring criterion.
A commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa that is not credible in the essays, given it is both a selection criterion and a residency condition for 1 February 2027 and June 2027.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Salary or wages lost during the six-week institute, or the approximately ten weeks including the PDE: "funds to cover Fellows' salaries while they are away from work" is explicitly not provided.
Personal purchases, "such as support for Fellows' home organizations or gifts for family".
Any cost of maintaining your work, project or organisation in your absence, since the Fellowship "is not designed to help Fellows identify specific funding for projects or organizations."
Any costs arising from travelling earlier than the programme or staying longer, beyond the funded round-trip travel and required domestic U.S. travel.
Cost of dependants' travel, which is prohibited rather than funded.

Any gap between the limited accident and sickness benefit plan and your own private health cover; the plan is described as "limited" and no excess, dental or pre-existing-condition terms are published.
Meals beyond those provided at campus cafeterias or restaurants, and any food costs arising from the limited variety available on campus.
document_audit: All entries are typed into the online system - no résumé or document upload is described, so no file format, file size or scan rule applies.
Identity block: full legal name, date of birth and biological sex exactly as spelled on your passport or official government-issued identification. Mismatches here are a documented rejection risk.

Passport: country of issue and expiration date if you hold one. Not required to apply, but finalists must hold a passport from an eligible Fellowship country valid through at least 28 February 2028 (31 March 2028 with the PDE).
Contact block: phone, email and postal address, plus an alternate email address, all of which must be ones you check regularly through selection.

Professional positions: up to five, each with organisation name and location (city and country), professional title, work format (in person, remote/virtual, or hybrid), start and end dates, and up to 100 words describing the position (required).
Education: up to five institutions, each with name and location, start and end dates, delivery method (online, in person, hybrid), type of degree, field of study, and up to 100 words (optional).
Trainings and certifications: up to five, each with type or name, format, start and end dates, and up to 100 words (optional).
Community and volunteer work: up to five, each with organisation name and location, work format, start and end dates, and up to 100 words (optional but recommended).
Awards, honors, fellowships, grants and/or scholarships: up to 10, each with title, awarding organisation or institution, date received, and up to 100 words (optional).
Professional skills: up to eight languages and/or up to 10 computer or software skills.
Publications, conferences and notable presentations: Chicago Manual of Style formatting is recommended but not required.
Associations and affiliations, including leadership roles.
English self-assessment: native-language indicator plus a proficiency level for each skill from the published five-level scale; deaf applicants also report American Sign Language proficiency.
Personal statements: all in English, your own original work, within the 150-350 word band and each individual maximum (350 / 250 / 250 / 150), plus the 200-word track-fit essay.
Optional PDE essays: 150 / 250 / 250 words maximum, all in English.
Technology Use Disclosure: list the types of technology used and how they were used.
Language rule: "All information must be entered in English" and "All responses must be written in English."

referee_tracking.instructions: The 2027 Application Instructions describe no referees, no reference letters and no third-party submissions at all. Every component is completed and submitted by the applicant alone, and applications or information sent by email are not considered. Do not prepare referee letters for this programme.

alerts.trigger: Immediately, and no later than 13 October 2026 at 16:00/4:00 PM GMT
alerts.message: The 2027 cycle closes at 16:00 GMT on Tuesday 13 October 2026. That is the only application deadline; after it, the process moves to embassy/consulate interviews, so there is no second chance in this cycle.

Semi-finalists are interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country. Have your passport or other government-issued photo ID and proof of your date of birth ready, and watch your phone and both email inboxes.
Decide on the PDE component now. It is optional and competitive, it adds three essays, and you cannot apply for it later if you do not flag it in the application.

submission_workflow: Read the 2027 Application Instructions PDF and the Application FAQs.
Confirm every technical eligibility condition, especially age on 13 October 2026, citizenship and residence, and the J-1 visa expectation.
Open the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org.
Complete the Eligibility section first; it gates the rest of the form.
Complete General Information, then the Résumé/CV, so entries auto-populate later sections.
Skip or complete the optional Demographic Information section; it is used only for statistics and accommodation planning, never in selection.
Complete Contact Information, Current Professional and/or Educational Experience, YALI Engagement, Previous U.S. Experience and English Language.
Complete Institute Track and Sector Alignment, the Leadership Assessment and the Personal Statements.
Optionally complete the PDE section with its three essays.
Complete the Technology Use Disclosure.
Proofread everything against the word limits, check the whole application for completeness, and submit through the online system before 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on 13 October 2026.
If shortlisted, attend the embassy or consulate interview with your photo ID and passport (if available) and any proof of date of birth, citizenship and residence.
post_award_requirements: Attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities scheduled by your institute, as required by the Fellowship Terms and Conditions.
Commit to returning to Sub-Saharan Africa and contributing skills to your community; the award is tied to permanent residence in an eligible country as of 1 February 2027 and in June 2027.
Complete a detailed Medical History Form and, if applicable, an Accommodations Form, and declare dietary, religious or medical needs as early as possible.
Hold a valid passport from an eligible Fellowship country through at least 28 February 2028, or 31 March 2028 if selected for the PDE.
Attend the mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and the visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa, with visa processing between March and May 2027.
If you join the PDE, be available for approximately 10 weeks in total in the United States and dedicate preparation time before the PDE starts.

After returning, the programme expects continued engagement: alumni access to networking, ongoing professional development, collaboration opportunities, events and virtual programming such as Reciprocal Exchanges.
questions_to_ask_host: The instructions say every Fellow must hold a passport valid through at least 28 February 2028 - what happens if my current passport expires before then and renewal is slow?
How is single-occupancy housing allocated, and how often do Fellows end up sharing a room and bathroom?
What exactly does the "limited accident and sickness benefit plan" cover, and what is excluded?
Are continuing professional development obligations created by the Fellowship Terms and Conditions, and how are they monitored?
How flexible is the track placement in practice, and how much notice do I get if I am placed outside my first-choice track?
What support exists for Fellows with specific dietary, religious or medical needs beyond the published accommodation process?
For PDE Fellows, who pays for local transport and are there any placements outside the main metropolitan areas?
Is the six-week institute accredited for any continuing professional development credit in my home country?
What are the exact visa processing steps and realistic timelines between March and May 2027?
How is my personal data handled, and what will be shared with my potential PDE host organization?

January intake (South African applicants): applications open August to October of the preceding year. As at 2026-10-01 the only window still running is the January 2027 intake for South African applicants, open August to October 2026. The AI for Science stream is not part of this window because AIMS states: "For the AI for Science stream we only have the September intake with applications open from January to March."
records.description: The AIMS Structured Master's Scholarship funds a full postgraduate master's programme at the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences in Muizenberg, Cape Town. AIMS publishes the covered items as a complete package: flights to and from South Africa, airport transfers, medical insurance, tuition and research fees, a monthly stipend of R2,200, on-site accommodation at AIMS, and three meals a day at the AIMS canteen - so tuition, living costs, travel and health cover are all established by the institute. AIMS handles the money itself: "the scholarship funds are managed by AIMS and are not paid into students' bank accounts", with only the stipend paid directly into a South African bank account. There are two intakes, and on 2026-10-01 the live one is the January intake, which AIMS restricts to South African applicants with an application window of August to October of the preceding year; the Africa-wide September intake window (January to March) is closed. The AI for Science stream has only the September intake and is therefore also closed.

records.best_fit: Applicants who are citizens of any African country and resident in Africa at the time of application, hold a four-year undergraduate degree or a three-year undergraduate degree plus an honours year (or the French LMD equivalent of an M1 year) in physics, mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering or another discipline with a strong computational and mathematical component, and have never previously held a scholarship to study at an AIMS centre. For the intake that is open on 2026-10-01, applicants must additionally be South African, and the degree must be completed by December.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide which intake you are targeting before anything else. As at 2026-10-01 the Africa-wide September intake (January-March window) and the AI for Science stream are both closed; the only window running is the January 2027 intake for South African applicants, open August to October.
If you are not South African, AIMS currently has no open intake for you - watch for the January-to-March window for the September intake.
Confirm you are a citizen of any African country and resident in Africa at the time of application, or that you are displaced by war, in which case the residency requirement does not apply.
Confirm you have never held a scholarship to study at an AIMS centre - this is a hard bar, not a scoring factor.
Confirm your degree status against the intake cut-off: December for the January intake, August for the September intake.
Check your discipline is acceptable: physics, mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, or any discipline with a strong computational and mathematical component.
If you studied in the French LMD system, confirm you hold the equivalent of an M1 year.
Gather your undergraduate and postgraduate transcripts, a CV, a cover letter and sample work before starting the form, because all five are uploaded.
Make sure you have a South African bank account ready, because the stipend is paid only into a South African bank account.
Apply early in the August-to-October window. AIMS publishes no closing day, only the months, so the effective deadline is unknown and could be the first working day of the window's end.
important_advice_for_students: Do not wait for a published closing date. AIMS says only "open August to October", so there is no day to plan around. Treat October as if it could end at any moment.

Do not expect to be reimbursed for anything. Tuition, research fees, flights, airport transfers, medical insurance, accommodation and meals are all paid by AIMS directly; only the R2,200 monthly stipend reaches your account.
Do not assume the stipend covers your living costs. It is R2,200 a month; the scholarship works because accommodation and three meals a day are included on top, not because the stipend is generous.
Do not apply to the wrong stream. The Mathematical Sciences and AI for Science streams use different portals, and only the Mathematical Sciences stream has a January intake.
Do not apply if you already hold or have held an AIMS study scholarship.
Do not skip sample work. It is one of five required uploads and is the item most likely to distinguish a computational or mathematical record.
Do not over-invest in a cover letter that repeats your CV. AIMS gives no weightings, so keep the CV factual and put your mathematical or computational evidence in the sample work.
Do not count on the Africa-wide intake being open now. If you are not South African you are waiting for the January-to-March window for the September intake.
Do not assume any published figure beyond R2,200 per month. AIMS publishes no other amount, no fee schedule and no other allowance.
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the August-to-October window has closed, since no day-level deadline is published and the effective cut-off is unknown.
Applying from outside Africa without a valid displacement exception, failing the "resident in Africa at the time of application" test.
Not being a citizen of an African country.
Having previously held a scholarship to study at an AIMS centre.
Applying to the January intake while not being a South African applicant.
Applying to the AI for Science stream expecting a January intake, which AIMS does not offer.
Missing the degree completion cut-off of December for the January intake or August for the September intake.
Applying with a discipline with no computational or mathematical component, where the degree is outside physics, mathematics, statistics, computer science and engineering.
Uploading an incomplete set - all five items are required: undergraduate transcripts, postgraduate transcripts, CV, cover letter and sample work.
Failing to attend or prepare for the online interview, which is the only published selection stage after shortlisting.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Nothing in the core package is left uncovered: tuition and research fees, on-site accommodation, three meals a day, medical insurance, flights to and from South Africa, airport transfers and the monthly stipend are all published as covered.
Books, stationery and course materials - not published either way, so unconfirmed.
Computing equipment, software licences and internet beyond the campus - not published either way.
Mobile phone and personal data - not published either way.
Personal travel outside the programme, weekend travel home, and guest accommodation for family - not published, and the on-site accommodation is the only housing AIMS describes.
Any cost arising if the January intake runs past the published academic year end of 30 June - no extension rule is published.
Anything a student spends from the R2,200 monthly stipend above what meals and accommodation do not cover, plus any personal purchases.
document_audit: Undergraduate transcripts - required upload; AIMS publishes no format, size or certification rule.
Postgraduate transcripts - required upload even where the degree is the qualifying one; AIMS publishes no format, size or certification rule.
CV - required upload.
Cover letter - required upload.
Sample work - required upload; AIMS publishes no page limit, no file type and no topic restriction.

No file-size limit, no accepted file type, no translation rule, no certification rule and no signature rule are published on the AIMS page, so confirm each portal's upload limits at the moment you apply.
Degree cut-off dates are the only hard date rules attached to documents: by August for the September intake, by December for the January intake for South African applicants.

referee_tracking.instructions: The AIMS prospective students page lists five required items - undergraduate transcripts, postgraduate transcripts, CV, cover letter and sample work - and describes no referees, reference letters or third-party submissions. Do not prepare referee letters for AIMS; if the portal asks for one, that is a portal rule rather than a published AIMS requirement.

alerts.message: The January 2027 intake window for South African applicants is published as open "August to October of the preceding year". With no closing day published, submit as early in October as possible rather than at the end of the month.

alerts.trigger: If you are not South African
alerts.message: There is no open AIMS intake for you on 2026-10-01. The Africa-wide September intake window is January to March, and the AI for Science stream is September-intake only, also January to March. Prepare your transcripts, CV, cover letter and sample work now and apply in the January window.

alerts.trigger: If you have held an AIMS scholarship before
alerts.message: Do not apply. "not have held a previous scholarship to study at an AIMS centre" is a hard eligibility bar.

Confirm all five uploads are in place and that your South African bank account details are correct, because the stipend is the only element paid to you and it is paid only into a South African account.
The online interview is the only published selection stage. Prepare to talk through your sample work, your computational or mathematical background and your research interests in an online format.

submission_workflow: Identify the correct live intake and confirm you are eligible for it.
Choose the stream portal: apply.aims.ac.za for Mathematical Sciences, or ai.aims.ac.za/apply for AI for Science (September intake only).
Complete the online application form.
Upload undergraduate and postgraduate transcripts.
Upload your CV.
Upload your cover letter.
Upload your sample work.
Submit the application inside the published window.
If shortlisted, sit the online interview.
Await final selection; AIMS publishes no results date.
post_award_requirements: Reside in AIMS on-site accommodation at 6 Melrose Road, Muizenberg, and take meals at the AIMS cantee, since both are inside the award.
Accept that the scholarship funds are managed by AIMS and are not paid into the student's bank account, with only the monthly stipend paid into a South African bank account.
Follow the AIMS academic calendar, which runs from September to the end of June.
AIMS publishes no return-home requirement, no renewal rule, no deferral rule, no progress-reporting requirement and no academic progression condition, so none should be assumed.
questions_to_ask_host: What is the exact closing date and time for the January intake, given that only 'August to October' is published?
What is the end date of the January 2027 programme, and is the full scholarship package funded to that date?
Which portal should a South African applicant use for the January intake - is it apply.aims.ac.za, and is there a separate stream?
What do I do if I have no South African bank account yet, given that the stipend is paid only into a South African account?
What file type and maximum file size does the portal accept for transcripts, CV, cover letter and sample work?
Do documents need to be certified or translated, and into which language?
What does 'sample work' mean in practice - a research paper, code, a problem set solution, or a project write-up?
Is medical insurance comprehensive or capped, and are pre-existing conditions and dental covered?
Who assesses my application, what are the weighting between the CV, cover letter and sample work, and when will I hear back?
Are AIMS alumni programmes, mentoring or conference funding available after the award?

verification.source_conflict_rule: AIMS presents two streams and three windows on a single page. Where the general statement "Applications are open from January to March" could be read as covering all intakes, the stream-specific sentence is treated as authoritative: it names the Mathematical Sciences stream's January intake and separately restricts the AI for Science stream to the September intake. The homepage claim of "full scholarships" is read together with the itemised seven-item package on the prospective students page rather than on its own.
verification.source_freshness_rule: The prospective students page carries no visible last-updated stamp, so the intake windows and the R2,200 stipend are treated as current-as-at-read but unversioned. Because the window is expressed in months only and the whole package is small enough to change between cohorts, any applicant relying on this record should re-read the prospective students page and the live portal in the same week they apply, and must not assume next year's window or amount is unchanged.

New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.
records.description: DAFI is UNHCR's dedicated tertiary scholarship programme for refugees and returnees, founded in 1992 and funded principally by the Government of Germany. The published scholarship package covers a range of costs including tuition and study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner may also cover academic preparatory, language and ICT courses as well as psychosocial support. It funds ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent programmes and ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary and TVET programmes of two years or more, and it explicitly does not cover master's studies. Applications are made through the DAFI Programme Management Platform, which was live and accepting registrations and submissions on 2026-10-01.
records.best_fit: Refugees and returnees recognised by UNHCR who hold a secondary-school qualification and have been admitted to an undergraduate, short-cycle tertiary or TVET place in their country of asylum or home country, and who are not already holding another higher-education scholarship.
records.eligibility_summary: Recognised refugees and, in selected countries, returnees seeking an undergraduate (ISCED 6) or short-cycle tertiary/TVET (ISCED 5, two years or more) place in their country of asylum or home country, who are not in receipt of another higher-education scholarship.

records.selection_notes: The published Rwanda call states that priority will be given to applicants who achieved excellent academic performance, that only one family member may hold a DAFI scholarship, and that female applicants and persons with special needs education are highly encouraged to apply. It also states that only qualified candidates duly registered with UNHCR are invited to interviews, that names of shortlisted candidates are posted at the respective offices, and that academic documents are verified with the relevant authorities (the last two statements are published in the Windle International Kenya DAFI scholarship instructions, not on the UNHCR Rwanda call). The UNHCR programme page states that UNHCR and its education partners closely monitor scholars' academic progress and well-being through regular engagement with students and their institutions.
records.notes: The scholarship does not cover master's degree programmes (published: 'DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies.' / 'Please note that the scholarship does not cover master's degree programs.'). Awards are not deferrable, renewable or multi-year by default: funding follows admission to an ISCED 5 or ISCED 6 programme in the cycle applied for. No return-home obligation is published, and because studies take place in the country of asylum or home country no relocation is required. No clinical or field-of-study restriction is published beyond the general rule that the programme targets undergraduate and short-cycle tertiary/TVET study. The 2024 cycle was the first since 2020 with a decrease in the number of scholars supported, reflecting reduced global funding. As this is a multi-country programme with no published global deadline, the applicable deadline is the one published by the applicant's own UNHCR country operation; the published 2026/2027 country windows had all closed by 31 August 2026 at the time of verification, and the platform itself remained live and accepting registrations on 2026-10-01.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold a recognised refugee status, or asylum-seeker status where your country operation accepts asylum seekers
Confirm you are not already receiving another higher-education scholarship - this is an explicit disqualifier
Confirm you are not confirmed for resettlement to a third country - this is an explicit disqualifier
Check that no other family member already holds a DAFI scholarship
Secure a formal admission letter from a university or approved tertiary institution in the country of asylum
Obtain the equivalence certificate from the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum
Have your high school diploma available as an official or certified copy
Have your UNHCR proof of registration ready
Locate your country operation's published call and deadline on the UNHCR country help page - there is no global deadline
Create your account on the DAFI Programme Management Platform well before the country deadline
important_advice_for_students: Do not rely on third-party scholarship listings for DAFI - every country operation sets its own window and criteria, and those aggregators routinely show deadlines that differ from your country's call
Do not apply for master's study: DAFI does not fund master's programmes at all
Do not pay anything: the official platform states 'DAFI Scholarship programme application is free of charge!' and no fee is published at any stage
Do not miss the country deadline: the published Rwanda call states 'late applications will not be considered'
Do not start a DAFI application before securing university admission - proof of admission is a required document
Do watch for the fact that the package varies by country operation, so what one country operation covers is not automatically what yours covers
Contact your country office using the published email for your country rather than guessing at the process
common_rejection_risks: Already holding another higher-education scholarship at the time of application
Confirmed for resettlement to a third country
A second family member applying for a DAFI scholarship in the same family
Missing or non-certified high school diploma
Missing or unavailable equivalence certificate from the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum
No proof of admission to a university in the country of asylum
Missing UNHCR proof of registration
Application submitted after the country operation's published deadline
Applying for a master's programme
estimated_uncovered_costs: Not established from official sources. The published package lists tuition, study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and states it 'varies from country to country', so what remains out of pocket cannot be stated without your country operation's own package description.
Master's degree study costs - explicitly not covered
Any costs for a second DAFI award within the same family - not available
document_audit: UNHCR proof of registration - must be attached
High school diploma - must be an official or certified copy
University admission letter or proof of acceptance for a university in the country of asylum - mandatory
Equivalence certificate from the Ministry of Education of the country of asylum - mandatory

No published file-size limit, accepted file type, translation rule or issue-date rule; upload in the format your country operation's call specifies and ask your country office if a translation is needed

alerts.trigger: Your country operation publishes its next DAFI call (typically published on the UNHCR country help page ahead of the academic year)
alerts.message: Read the full call before registering, then register on the DAFI Programme Management Platform and assemble admission and equivalence documents in parallel, since these are the long-lead items.

alerts.trigger: Your country deadline is within two weeks
alerts.message: Submit early. Late applications are not considered, and platform or upload issues are the most common reason for missing a DAFI deadline.

alerts.trigger: You are offered a resettlement departure
alerts.message: You become ineligible for DAFI once departure for resettlement to a third country is confirmed; raise this with your country office before accepting a scholarship offer.

alerts.trigger: You are already on another higher-education scholarship
alerts.message: You are not eligible to apply for DAFI at the same time. Do not submit a duplicate application.

submission_workflow: Read your country operation's DAFI call in full
Gather UNHCR proof of registration, certified high school diploma, university admission letter and Ministry of Education equivalence certificate
Register an account at https://unhcr-dafi-tertiary.scholarshipsplatform.com/
Start the application and save it in-progress
Attach all required documents
Submit before the country deadline
Monitor your email for the final status notification from the DAFI platform
post_award_requirements: UNHCR and its education partners monitor scholars' academic progress and well-being through regular engagement with students and their institutions
Scholars are encouraged to take part in community engagement and skills development activities (published Rwanda call wording)
questions_to_ask_host: Does my country operation's package cover everything I need for the specific programme I have been admitted to, given that it 'varies from country to country'?
Is my institution and programme eligible for DAFI funding in my country operation?
Do you require the equivalence certificate to be translated, and into which language?

records.description: The University of Westminster offers two Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarships to students who are seeking asylum in the United Kingdom. Each covers full tuition costs for a full-time master's course starting January 2027, plus a maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months, published on the University's central scholarship listing as 'Full tuition fee plus up to £12,000'. Applications are made by returning the completed application form with required evidence as PDF attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026.
records.best_fit: People who are seeking asylum in the UK, or who hold UK discretionary or limited leave to remain as a result of an asylum application, and who hold or can obtain an offer for a full-time master's course at the University of Westminster starting January 2027, and who cannot access taught postgraduate student loans from Student Finance.
records.eligibility_summary: UK residents seeking asylum, or holding discretionary or limited leave to remain following an asylum application, who hold a Westminster offer for a full-time master's course starting January 2027 and are not eligible for taught postgraduate student loans.

You must be resident in the UK

You must hold one of the following eligible immigration statuses before submitting your application: UK asylum seeker; UK discretionary leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application); UK limited leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application)

records.notes: The published exclusion list is explicit and disqualifying: students who already have a master's degree are not eligible to apply; students who are able to receive taught postgraduate student loans from Student Finance are not eligible; and the following categories of students are not eligible - Postgraduate Diploma, professional courses (eg RIBA pt III, ACCA, CIMA, CiLEX), conversion courses (eg Graduate Diploma in Law), and integrated masters/MPhil. Only two awards are available. The award is tied to a January 2027 course start, so it cannot be deferred to a later intake on the published terms. No renewal, return-home obligation, clinical restriction, tax treatment, document size limit, accepted file type beyond 'pdf attachments', translation rule or issue-date rule is published on the official pages read. The University also runs a separate one-place Westminster Sanctuary Scholarship for a student granted Indefinite Leave to Remain or Discretionary Leave to Remain, which is a different award and is not recorded here.

important_advice_for_students: Apply by email, not through a portal: the University publishes one route only, which is the completed form plus evidence as pdf attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk
Do not apply if you can get a taught postgraduate student loan. This is an absolute exclusion, not an assessment criterion, and it is checked against the Student Finance rules
Do not apply for a conversion course, an integrated masters/MPhil, a professional course or a Postgraduate Diploma; all four are named exclusions and a waste of a capped two-award round
Do not assume the maintenance grant stretches beyond 12 months. It is £1,000 per month for up to 12 months, which is a bounded figure, so build a plan around the end of the grant
Do not apply before you have the January 2027 course offer; the published eligibility requires the offer to exist first

Do not treat this as the University's undergraduate route or as the separate single-place Westminster Sanctuary Scholarship, which is a different award for a student granted Indefinite Leave to Remain or Discretionary Leave to Remain
Do not wait for a published interview or assessment stage: none is described, so the only hard timing constraint is the 2 November 2026 deadline

records.description: The University of Glasgow Sanctuary Scholarship supports applicants with refugee or asylum seeker status who are living in the UK and hold an offer to study at the University in the 2027/28 academic year, covering undergraduate and postgraduate taught entry in September 2027/28. It provides a full tuition fee waiver for applicants who cannot access mainstream funding through Student Awards Agency Scotland or Student Finance, together with a £5,000 per year stipend towards study costs. Six scholarships are available, and applying also puts a candidate forward for a small number of donor-funded awards that cover the £5,000 stipend only.

records.selection_notes: Six scholarships are available. Awards are made against the published eligibility conditions, which turn on three things: holding a firm offer for full-time study, UK location with Home or RUK fee status, and a qualifying asylum, refugee-protection, discretionary-leave or UK resettlement scheme status. The published page states that if you are unsure whether you are eligible to apply, you should contact the team using their enquiry form. No academic threshold, interview, assessment weighting or decision date is published.
records.notes: Accommodation is explicitly not included: the University states that University accommodation is not included in the Sanctuary Scholarship and that applicants will therefore need to cover their own accommodation costs or already live within a reasonable commuting distance of the University. The scholarship is not available to PGdip, PDGE or part time programmes. Award value varies by funding route: undergraduates with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding receive the £5,000 stipend towards study costs only; postgraduate taught masters students with refugee status (or equivalent) and access to funding receive the £5,000 stipend plus a partial tuition fee waiver to cover any shortfall not met by the Postgraduate Masters tuition fee loan. The University states that if your immigration status changes part way through your studies you should inform the Scholarships Team as soon as possible, as this may affect eligibility, that changes are reviewed on a case-by-case basis, and that the scholarship funding will not cease automatically but may be recalculated. The page contains an internal inconsistency: it states the offer requirement is for '2027/26' while the surrounding text describes the 2027/28 academic year, which appears to be a typographical error on the official page. The page also carries an eVisa notice referencing a BRP expiring on 31 December 2025, which is out of date relative to the current cycle.

records.description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. The selected candidate's home institution (CPS) is responsible for the administrative procedures to acquire the Visiting Student Researcher status and pays the University Services Fee, the DS-2019 visa processing fee and the Institute of European Studies administrative fees at UC Berkeley. The selected candidate must arrange and financially cover their own travel, accommodation and health insurance, and the call publishes no direct stipend or award figure.

records.selection_notes: Assessment is carried out by an academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD. Criterion A: candidate's curriculum, considering academic grades, track record and scientific achievements including peer-reviewed publications, scholarships, prizes, conferences and project participation (40%). Criterion B: scientific quality, innovative character of the work plan and feasibility of the research activities to be developed (30%). Criterion C: motivation letter explaining the relevance of the stay and the work to be developed for the scientific ambition of the doctoral work plan, and the expected impact of the stay on the candidate's career (30%). Selection is based on the analysis of these criteria, producing a positive or negative opinion, with final classification CF = 0.4 A + 0.3 B + 0.3 C.
records.notes: Applications are open on a rolling basis and are assessed in quarterly windows, so an application can be submitted at any time before closing; the call closes early if the annual quota is reached. Selected candidates must finance their own travel, accommodation and health insurance. Arrival at UC Berkeley cannot occur earlier than six months after selection for the programme. The call is governed by the published Expression of Interest Call (Chamada de Manifestação de Interesse) and the accompanying documents (Memorandum of Understanding Portugal_Berkeley_Program, FCT-CPS-Berkeley Protocol, model letter, Research Scholarships Regulation, Table of Scholarship-related Subsidies (2025), and the assessors' college).

important_advice_for_students: Do not expect a stipend, housing or travel money — the call publishes none, and travel, accommodation and health insurance are explicitly yours to fund

Do not plan to arrive sooner than six months after selection, whatever your personal timeline
Budget separately for Berkeley accommodation and US health insurance before applying, since the call gives you none
If you already hold an FCT doctoral research scholarship, remember the complementary supports are a separate request through myFCT, not automatic with this selection
There is no published benefit of applying at the very end of the year, because quota exhaustion can close the call before 30 December 2027

Weak academic record or little scientific output relative to criterion A weighting (40%)
