records.name: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
records.official_source: Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI) — Directorate General for Growth and Export Promotion, with ICE and Uni-Italia
records.region: Italy (host country). Applicants must be citizens permanently resident in one of 22 published partner countries: Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, People's Republic of China, Tunisia, Türkiye, Uruguay, Vietnam
records.duration: 9 months of study, starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year
records.deadline: The 11th edition (academic year 2026-2027) call was open from 20 April 2026 and closed at 6:00pm Italian time on 11 May 2026. The official programme site announces that the new call opens in 2027 (the 12th edition).
records.application_period: The 11th edition ran 20 April 2026 to 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time and is closed, with 1634 applications received, 982 eligible and 211 scholarships awarded. The official site carries the banner 'NEW APPLICATION OPENS 2027!' / 'IL NUOVO BANDO APRE NEL 2027!', so the next edition is announced but no opening date, closing date or application window has been published.
records.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is a MAECI scholarship programme run with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia that pays a nine-month scholarship to foreign students from 22 partner countries to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, combined with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. Courses are taught entirely in English, and the programme includes study of Italian language and culture plus a mandatory gender-equality and anti-gender-violence seminar or module. The winner receives an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800, paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the holder's name, and is exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions, but must still pay the regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident and civil liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship explicitly does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance.
records.best_fit: Students aged 25 or under (born on or after 1 January 2000) who hold a qualification valid for enrolment in a participating Italian Master's or Postgraduate course, permanently resident in one of the 22 listed partner countries, and not already studying at or graduated from an Italian university.
records.funding_period: per academic year (9 months of study), paid quarterly
records.eligibility_summary: Citizens permanently resident in one of 22 partner countries, born on or after 1 January 2000, holding a qualification valid for enrolment in an IYT Master's or Postgraduate course, and not already studying at or graduated from an Italian university.
eligibility: Citizens of Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, People's Republic of China, Tunisia, Türkiye, Uruguay or Vietnam, permanently resident in that country
Hold an academic qualification valid for enrolment in a Master's/Postgraduate degree programme at the chosen institution; students who are about to graduate are not eligible

Have submitted, following each university's own procedures, an application for pre-admission to a course included in the IYT programme; no exceptions are made for courses or universities not in the project
May apply for only one course (with a second, binding preference permitted for courses with limited enrolment)
Born on or after 1 January 2000, except applicants for scholarship renewal
English language proficiency certified from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference
Knowledge of Italian certified, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure
Not currently studying at an Italian university and not holding an Italian university degree
coverage: Annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly into an Italian bank account held in the scholar's name
Exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions at the participating institution
Study of Italian language and culture within the programme
Compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association representative of the region
Seminar or training module on gender equality and the fight against gender-based violence in the academic curriculum
benefits: Nine months of study starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year
Compulsory internship in an Italian company or professional association
Italian language and culture study integrated into the programme

Tax exemption under Article 3, paragraph 3, letter d-ter of the Consolidated Income Tax Law for IRPEF purposes, since sums paid as scholarships by the Italian Government to foreign citizens under international agreements are exempt

Additional university scholarships ('Borse Ateneo') offered by six participating universities: Università di Parma, Università degli Studi di Firenze, Università degli Studi di Bergamo, Università degli Studi della Tuscia, Università Ca' Foscari Venezia, Università degli Studi di Brescia
A reserved quota of IYT scholarships for Architecture and Design courses for applicants from India, Indonesia, Turkey, Brazil and Ethiopia
requirements: Applications must be submitted exclusively online through the programme's My-App registration page
Online applications submitted between 20 April 2026 and 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time for the 11th edition
Names and surnames must be entered exactly as they appear on the passport
Multiple applications using different email addresses are strictly prohibited and will be rejected
The scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy; participation in university international mobility programmes, company internships abroad and thesis research abroad are not possible
The scholarship is subject to prior review of legality by the Court of Auditors, so the actual award depends on the positive outcome of those checks
Course listings are published on the basis of a written undertaking by the relevant Rector, subject to withdrawal within 60 days if the university's governing bodies do not ratify participation
records.english_requirement: Courses are taught entirely in English. Applicants must attach certification of English language proficiency from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, ISE Digital – Trinity College, ISE Paper – Trinity College, PTE, Linguaskill, ESOL, TOEIC covering listening, reading, speaking, writing). Candidates who obtained a university degree at the end of a degree course taught in English may submit a university certificate attesting that English was the language of instruction, accepted as proof of level C1. A separate requirement exists for Italian: certification issued by the institution where the training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure; Italian certification is not mandatory but contributes to the evaluation score.
application_method: Apply for pre-admission to a chosen IYT course directly with that university, following the university's own procedures, within the deadlines set by the Technical Committee
Register on the IYT portal (My-App) using name and surname exactly as printed on the passport

Upload the required documents: final transcript with CGPA (or the dated and signed university statement if the certificate is pending), English proficiency certification from B2, Italian certification or commitment declaration, a video of no longer than 59 seconds, a one-page CV, and a valid passport
Submit the application online during the published call window
Await the Technical Committee's comparative evaluation; successful candidates are informed by email to the registration address
records.selection_notes: Examination and evaluation of applications is carried out by the Technical Committee of the IYT Program (MAECI, ICE and Uni-Italia), which may use an ad hoc commission. Scholarships are allocated in quotas defined for each country and awarded on the basis of a comparative evaluation of the applications against the requirements in Articles 3 and 5 of the call. The Design Scholarship quota is allocated using specially drawn-up rankings that take into account the order of preference for courses given by the student, as is the Borse Ateneo quota.
records.notes: Renewable: IYT scholarship holders may apply to continue the second year of the Master's by uploading a university certificate of exams taken (CFU), a certificate of attendance for an Italian language course (and, for the 11th edition holders, an internship project) by 20 July 2027; renewal and fee exemption for the second year are conditional on achieving 30 credits by 20 July 2027 and verified regular attendance of the university's Italian language course. All scholarship recipients must complete the paperwork for the start of their internship by 20 January 2027. Incompatible: the IYT scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarship or financial benefit from the Italian Government or any public institution (e.g. Erasmus+), including scholarships offered by Italian regions under regional education programmes. Must fund separately: the scholarship does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance covering illness and accidents in Italy. Not covered even after fee waiver: regional tax for the Right to Education, stamp duty, accident and/or civil liability insurance costs, and health insurance. Restrictions on mobility: the scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy. Award is conditional on the positive outcome of the Court of Auditors legality review.

official_details.description: Acknowledging the importance of attracting international students as a strategic leverage for the internationalization of the country's economy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation - Directorate General for Growth and Export Promotion, the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia, through the 'Invest Your Talent in Italy' Program, are offering scholarships to students interested in attending, for the 2026-2027 academic year, a higher education course in Italy (Master's Degrees and Postgraduate Degrees) at Italian state or legally recognized institutions associated with the Program, to be completed with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association.
purpose: Attract international talent as a strategic leverage for the internationalization of the country's economy
Promote the Italian academic system as a centre of excellence and strengthen collaboration between universities and businesses
Give Italian companies the opportunity to welcome young foreign talents trained in Italy
Spread Italian language and culture around the world
Enhance Italian higher education as a strategic asset for the country's internationalization
Promote gender equality and the fight against gender-based violence through a mandatory seminar or training module in the academic curriculum of all IYT scholarship recipients
sdg_requirement_details: The programme is dedicated to the memory of Giulia Cecchettin, a Padua biomedical engineering student murdered on 11 November 2023

records.official_source: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT), I.P.
records.region: Portugal (host country). Applicants may be national, foreign or stateless researchers, provided the host institution is in Portugal

records.description: RESTART is an FCT funding instrument that competitively finances individual R&D projects in all scientific domains for researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including adoption leave. The award is a project grant of up to EUR 50,000 per project for a maximum of 18 months, drawn from a total budget allocation of EUR 1.6 million, and it is held by the beneficiary R&D unit rather than paid as a personal living stipend. Candidates must hold a doctorate, be an integrated doctoral member of an R&D unit or hold a contract with a State laboratory, and have taken a parental leave of at least 120 days (or at least 72 days in a shared leave, whether exclusive or shared) between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive.
records.best_fit: Doctorate-holding researchers, including foreign and stateless researchers, based at a Portuguese FCT-funded R&D unit or State laboratory, who have taken a qualifying parental or adoption leave between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 and can obtain a commitment from their host institution.
records.funding_period: per project, up to 18 months of project development
records.eligibility_summary: Researchers (national, foreign or stateless) who hold a doctorate, belong to an R&D unit or hold a State laboratory contract, and have taken a parental leave of at least 120 days (or 72 days for shared leave) between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive, with a host institution commitment.

The minimum number of days required (120 or 72) must be reached between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive, regardless of the start or end date of the leave
Applications must be submitted with the commitment of the host institution

Researchers holding a scholarship contract may submit as proof of parental leave the statement of suspension of research activities funded by that scholarship, issued by the contracting institution, for an equivalent period; for FCT scholarships this may be replaced by simply indicating the relevant scholarship reference
Eligible applicants are national, foreign and stateless researchers

official_details.description: The Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT), alongside its commitment to promoting the advancement of scientific and technological knowledge, aims to promote gender equality in R&D activities and careers, inseparable from equality of opportunity for the whole national scientific community. With this objective FCT launches the 4th edition of the RESTART programme. RESTART is intended to promote gender equality and opportunity through the competitive funding of individual R&D projects in all scientific domains, when carried out by researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including for adoption. Aligned with public policies in this area, RESTART also covers, with specific eligibility conditions, cases of shared parental leaves. By empowering a competitive return to research activity in new circumstances, RESTART will support researchers in pursuing and developing an original and innovative research idea, with the possibility of associating other human and/or material resources, according to the funding made available and the planned execution time. This funding instrument is aligned with the concerns and recommendations of various international bodies, namely the Council of the European Union and the OECD.

records.official_source: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), A*STAR Graduate Academy

records.deadline: Application period: 1 November to 1 February & 1 June to 10 August. First application cycle opens on 1 November and closes on 1 February of the following year; second application cycle opens on 1 June and closes on 10 August of the following year.
records.application_period: Two cycles a year: 1 November to 1 February (outcomes from mid-April) and 1 June to 10 August (outcomes from mid-November). A*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis.
records.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.
records.best_fit: Final-semester undergraduates and Master's students at, or on track to graduate from, a Singapore autonomous university, and mid-PhD students already enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university, who want to do a research-intensive PhD at an A*STAR Research Institute. International students without Singapore Permanent Residence should be comfortable with a 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants of all nationalities may apply, but international students must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a Singapore autonomous university, hold at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent, be in the last semester of final studies (full-term) or minimally one semester into a Singapore AU programme (mid-term), and satisfy PhD admission criteria at an autonomous university.

records.selection_notes: Referees can be academic referees from universities or supervisors/PIs whom you have worked with. records.notes: Bond-free for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. Not deferrable within the 4-year funding period without approval: if you need more time to complete your PhD you will have to seek approval from A*STAR's management for your PhD extension. official_details.description: Whether you're looking to explore broad scientific fields or dive deep into a specialised area, AGS offers full funding, access to world-class research labs, and the chance to take on a 12-month overseas attachment during your PhD. purpose: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (STEM): enabling aspiring researchers to pursue PhD studies in biomedical sciences, chemistry, physics, engineering, and related fields. Scholars gain research experience at A*STAR and contribute to impactful work.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Semiconductor): supporting students in chip design, materials science, and semiconductor technologies. Scholars gain hands-on experience and help Singapore grow as a global hub for semiconductor talent and innovation.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Quantum): advancing talents in quantum computing, communications, and sensing. Scholars drive cutting-edge research and discoveries that strengthen Singapore's position in quantum technologies.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Computing): nurturing leaders in AI, cybersecurity, software engineering, and data science. Scholars tackle real-world digital challenges and build expertise to power Singapore's growth as a tech-driven nation.
AGS is a collaboration between A*STAR and local Autonomous Universities (AUs). Scholars will be jointly supervised by both the A*STAR and University supervisors.

As these are national scholarships, all applications will be treated equitably and reviewed holistically such as on academic track record, publications and research exposure/experience.
records.notes: Bond period: 4 years. Upon completion of the PhD programme, NSS (PhD) scholars will return to Singapore and contribute to A*STAR's research institutes and/or relevant organisations for 4 years. Scholars who complete their PhD in a non-anglophone country would serve a 3-year service commitment instead. Non-Singaporeans must take up Singapore citizenship no later than the third year of the PhD. A*STAR does not pay for consumables or research fees; fees involved in the lab should be borne by the university. If you need more time to complete your PhD beyond the funding period, you will have to seek approval from A*STAR's management for your PhD extension. All scholars need to seek A*STAR's written permission before changing your course of study/research project. Applicants with prior research experience at A*STAR (beyond their undergraduate Final Year Project) may request a waiver of the compulsory research attachment year, subject to approval; however, scholars are strongly encouraged to complete the attachment. Mid-term awardees receive the same terms of support as full-term NSS (PhD) awardees from the point of the award, with retrospective payment for all tuition fees and/or any compulsory fees from Year 1 of study onwards. All rates/allowances vary according to country and university, and are subject to adjustments made by A*STAR. If you are currently holding a scholarship for your undergraduate studies from another government ministry/agency, the page advises clarifying the policy and guidelines from your sponsoring organisation before applying to A*STAR.

records.description: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is a full-cost postgraduate scholarship at the University of Cambridge for applicants from outside the United Kingdom. It pays the University Composition Fee, a maintenance allowance, one economy return single airfare, inbound visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge, plus discretionary funds. It is open to any subject at Cambridge, which includes health-related postgraduate study such as the PhD in Public Health and Primary Care, although the clinical medical degrees are explicitly excluded. Approximately 70 full-cost scholarships are awarded each year, about two-thirds to PhD students.

records.selection_notes: Two-stage selection. Stage 1: academic departments at Cambridge nominate a small number of eligible applicants who meet all four criteria to a very high level; only departmentally nominated applicants are invited to interview. Stage 2: a 25-30 minute interview with one of four subject-based panels (Arts, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, Social Sciences) consisting of academics and practitioners, and possibly Gates Cambridge alumni and a Trust representative. The interview has four sections: welcome and introduction; Gates Cambridge (knowledge of the scheme, motivation, why you could be a Scholar, thoughts on the opportunities and responsibilities); academic and career plans; final thoughts and questions. Scholars are selected after interview. Gates Cambridge states it cannot provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants.

Deferred entry and part-time study: a pilot continues to allow applications to fund a part-time doctoral degree; part-time degrees other than the PhD are not considered. University rules bar a second degree of the same type from Cambridge.

official_details.description: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship covers the full cost of studying at Cambridge and provides additional discretionary funding. Core components are the University Composition Fee, a maintenance allowance for a single student, one economy return single airfare, and inbound visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge. Around 70 full-cost scholarships are awarded each year from an application pool of approximately 850 applications.
purpose: The Gates Cambridge mission is to build a global network of future leaders committed to improving the lives of others.

Each year Gates Cambridge offers around 70 full-cost scholarships to outstanding applicants from countries outside the UK to pursue a postgraduate degree in any subject available at the University of Cambridge.
Approximately two-thirds of the awards are offered to PhD students, with approximately a third of awards available in the US round and the rest in the International round.
The programme was established in October 2000 by an historic donation of US$210m from the Gates Foundation to the University of Cambridge; the first class came into residence in October 2001.

official_details.selection_notes: Gates Cambridge uses a two-stage selection process to ensure Scholars meet all criteria to the highest level. Stage 1, departmental nomination: academic departments nominate a small number of eligible applicants who meet all four criteria to a very high level; only those nominated are invited to interview. Stage 2, interview: a 25-30 minute interview, in person or virtually (in-person attendance encouraged where possible), with one of four subject-based panels - Arts, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences and Social Sciences - each made up of experienced academics and practitioners and possibly Gates Cambridge alumni and a Trust representative. Interview sections: (1) welcome and introduction; (2) Gates Cambridge - what you know about the Scholarships, your motivation, why you could be a Scholar, your thoughts on the opportunities and responsibilities; (3) academic and career plans - your academic work to date, your proposed degree, your career plans, and possibly probing intellectual or ethical questions with no 'right' answers; (4) final thoughts and questions, optional. Scholars are then selected after interview. Gates Cambridge states it is not able to provide feedback to unsuccessful applicants. The four selection questions and the Gates Cambridge reference are used to distinguish between candidates nominated by academic departments.

Do not write a research proposal if you are not applying to a PhD; the requirement is PhD-only.
Do not translate your own documents. Cambridge requires a full translation by a registered translator and explicitly says not to translate documents yourself.
Do not ask a friend, a relative, or a referee who cannot speak to your suitability for the scholarship to write the Gates Cambridge reference.

Do not accept a Gates Cambridge reference that is just a third academic reference; the referee must address the four Gates Cambridge criteria and can rank you as exceptional, strong, not strong or weak.
Do not email PDFs to the Admissions Office. Every supporting document is uploaded through the Applicant Portal; hard copies cannot be processed and will be disposed of.
Do not take the GRE test unless a course page tells you it is needed; there is a charge, and the GMAT is not accepted by any Cambridge course.

Do not assume you can get a partial award by combining Gates Cambridge with a UKRI fee award - if you hold a public fee award the Trust will not pay your fee or may share fee and maintenance costs, so tell the Trust before you accept.
Tell the Trust immediately if you are offered a job or another substantial scholarship, because the standard maintenance allowance can be reduced or withdrawn.
Expect no feedback if you are unsuccessful; Gates Cambridge states it cannot provide it.
If you are part way through a PhD at Cambridge, you cannot use Gates Cambridge to fund the remainder of it - apply only for a new degree.

Weak answers on commitment to improving the lives of others or leadership potential, which are two of the four weighted criteria and have the longest word allowances

Nominated by you in the Applicant Portal; submits through the Referee Portal by the application deadline. If you nominate the same referee for multiple course applications, they must submit a separate reference for each course.

Submit the application by 11:59pm UK time on your deadline; you may submit before references are uploaded, but all three references must arrive by the deadline.

records.description: The GHES Fellowship is a 12-month, full-time, NIH-supported mentored research training award in global health research, run by a consortium of Yale, Stanford, the University of Arizona and UC Berkeley under the Fogarty International Center's LAUNCH program. It pays a monthly stipend for 12 months on the NIH award stipend scale, plus research support funding (USD 15,000 for postdoctoral fellows, USD 10,000 for predoctoral fellows), visa and passport fees, and - for U.S. applicants - international health insurance, required vaccinations, a reimbursable roundtrip flight to the training site and travel and accommodation for the NIH orientation. Doctorate tuition and fees are expressly not an allowable expense, so this is not full funding for a degree.
records.best_fit: U.S. citizens or permanent residents, and citizens of the 15 named GHES collaborating LMICs, who hold or are completing a doctoral or health-professional doctorate (PhD, DrPH, MD, DO, DDS, DVM, MBBS, MBChB, MMed, PharmD) within the last five years, can commit 10-12 months in person at a GHES LMIC research site, and can secure a primary GHES U.S. mentor plus a primary GHES LMIC mentor.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to U.S. predoctoral trainees and to U.S. and LMIC postdoctoral and post-professional trainees whose terminal doctoral or health-professional degree was received within the last five years, who can spend 10-12 months at a GHES LMIC research site and who have both a primary GHES U.S. mentor and a primary GHES LMIC mentor.

records.selection_notes: A panel of external reviewers reads and scores each application in five areas: success as a GHES fellow; aptitude and interest in research; potential for a career in global health; research proposal; and plan for mentoring and training. The GHES Principal Investigators may conduct online interviews with applicants if deemed necessary. Final selection of fellows is made by the GHES executive committee based on the candidate's application, research proposal, supplemental materials, external reviews and scores. The first round of fellowship awards is likely to be offered in April and the second round likely between May and June. Accepted applicants are notified by email, followed by a formal letter of award; candidates who are not selected are informed by email.
records.notes: Not covered: doctorate tuition and fees are explicitly not an allowable GHES expense ('Would a GHES fellowship help pay for my doctorate degree tuition/fees? No, that is not an allowable expense.'). The GHES does not fund LMIC students (student scholars) at LMIC institutions. The GHES LMIC fellowship is not intended to support a stay as a visiting researcher in the US. Award conditions: this is a full-time 12-month fellowship (40 hours per week for all 12 months); trainees will not be permitted to hold another job, even temporary or part-time, during the fellowship. All stipends are potentially taxable under U.S. and international law; GHES cannot provide tax advice and fellows are encouraged to consult a qualified tax professional. Partial fellowships can be provided to applicants already supported - for example T32 fellows can be awarded research-related and travel funds while their stipend is provided by the T32 fellowship - but FIC concurrent support must be allowable from the other source's perspective. The Stanford page notes that one fellow received a seed grant to continue research with the mentor team after the fellowship; this is not a published entitlement of the award.

official_details.description: The Global Health Emerging Scholars (GHES) Fellowship is a 12-month, NIH-supported, mentored training in global health research designed to improve population health. Hosted by a consortium of Yale University, Stanford University, University of Arizona and UC Berkeley, the fellowship year typically runs July-June and offers training opportunities in 15 countries. GHES is part of the Global Health Program for Fellows and Scholars / Launching Future Leaders in Global Health Research Training Program (LAUNCH) sponsored by the Fogarty International Center (FIC) and several collaborating NIH institutes and centers.
purpose: The program's main objective is to train new generations of health researchers and professionals who will be prepared to address the emerging challenges in global health.

GHES encourages research on health challenges that result from rapid urbanization and social inequities, on challenges of delivering accessible and high-quality healthcare within resource-limited settings, and on interventions that address the efficient management of scarce resources and innovative solutions to improving health services.

Research areas include (but are not limited to) chronic and noncommunicable diseases, HIV/STIs and other infectious diseases, environmental health, maternal and child health, intentional and unintentional injuries, trauma, and mental health.

The program was established in 2012 and is comprised of four U.S. partner institutions - Yale University, the University of California at Berkeley, Stanford University and the University of Arizona - with collaborations in 15 LMICs representing Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean, South and Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Eastern Europe and Oceania.
study_type: Full-time, in-person research training at an LMIC research site
official_details.degree_award: Not a degree programme. It is a 12-month research training fellowship; no degree or certificate is awarded.
official_details.duration: 12 months, full time (40 hours per week for all 12 months, 100% of the trainee's time). The fellowship year typically runs July to June and training begins 1 July.

general_eligibility: GHES is designed for pre-doctoral trainees from the U.S. and post-doctoral and post-professional trainees from the U.S. and LMICs.
Pre-doctoral trainees must be enrolled in a program leading to a PhD or in an equivalent research doctoral degree program.
Postdoctoral trainees must have received, as of the beginning date of the training period, a Ph.D., M.D., D.D.S., or comparable doctoral degree from an accredited domestic or foreign institution.

Comparable doctoral degrees include, but are not limited to, D.M.D., DC, DO, DVM, OD, DPM, ScD, EngD, DrPH, DNSc, DPT, PharmD, ND, DSW, PsyD, MMed, MBBS, MBChB, as well as a doctoral degree in nursing research.
All applicants must have a primary GHES U.S. mentor and a primary LMIC mentor who are part of the GHES program; additional mentors may be proposed.

U.S. post-doctoral and pre-doctoral applicants can be from any college or institution in the country and do not have to be affiliated with Stanford, Arizona, Berkeley or Yale, but must have a professional relationship with a GHES U.S. mentor at one of those universities.
LMIC post-doctoral applicants must be part of or affiliated with an institution in one of the GHES collaborating LMICs.

Professional relationship means a relationship between individuals in a professional setting in which proposed mentors support the applicant's research focus areas and the applicant is willing to listen and work with them.
ineligibility_conditions: The terminal doctoral or health-professional degree must have been received within the last five years; 'If you received your doctoral/health professional degree more than five years ago then a master's degree within the last five years, you are not eligible to apply.'
LMIC applicants are not eligible to apply for predoctoral fellowships.
The programme is not accepting master's or undergraduate students at this time.
Non-US citizens are only allowed to apply for the U.S. predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships if they can provide proof of U.S. residency (green card).

An applicant with no institutional affiliation applying as a postdoctoral fellow is eligible only if the GHES mentor commits to appoint them in a postdoctoral position at the mentor's affiliated institution.
You are not eligible if you cannot commit to 10-11 months of living abroad at the LMIC research training site.
As a master's or undergraduate student at one of the four GHES institutions, you are not eligible to apply.

U.S. applicants who are not affiliated with UC Berkeley, the University of Arizona, Stanford or Yale must receive approval to apply from the GHES program manager and must provide an NIH biosketch and the names of potential GHES mentors already contacted (per the Stanford GHES page).
To apply as an LMIC fellow you must already have, or secure, an affiliation or appointment with one of the GHES research sites.
The GHES does not fund LMIC students at LMIC institutions, so an LMIC student-scholar cannot be funded under the LMIC route.
official_details.citizenship_residency: U.S. applicants must be a citizen of the United States or its territories or possessions, or a U.S. permanent resident; a permanent resident number must be included in the application of a U.S. permanent resident. LMIC applicants must be a citizen of one of the collaborating LMICs: Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Colombia, Ecuador, Ethiopia, India, Kenya, Lebanon, Malaysia, Nigeria, Peru, Samoa, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda.
official_details.international_eligibility: International eligibility is limited to postdoctoral applicants who are citizens of the 15 named collaborating LMICs and who are residents of, or affiliated with, a GHES research site in one of those countries. International students enrolled in a PhD programme at a U.S. consortium university who are not U.S. citizens are not eligible unless they hold a green card.

undergraduate: Not eligible: 'I am a master's (or undergraduate) student from one of the four GHES institutions, am I eligible to apply? No, the program is not accepting master's or undergraduate students at this time.'
masters: Not eligible as an applicant: a master's degree alone does not qualify.
A master's degree completed within the last five years does not restore eligibility if the doctoral or health-professional degree was completed more than five years ago.

If your degree will be completed by 1 July of your fellowship year you may apply for a postdoctoral fellowship; if accepted you must provide proof that you received the degree before officially starting.

Predoctoral candidates must submit an unofficial transcript.

U.S. predoctoral research support funding is USD 10,000; U.S. postdoctoral research support funding is USD 15,000; LMIC postdoctoral research support funding is USD 15,000 plus USD 15,000 for travel and the short-term U.S.-based training period; an additional USD 5,000 is available in all cases.

official_details.selection_notes: A panel of external reviewers reads and scores each application in the five published areas. The GHES Principal Investigators may conduct online interviews with applicants if deemed necessary. Final selection of fellows is made by the GHES executive committee and is based on the candidate's application, research proposal, supplemental materials, external reviews and scores. The first round of fellowship awards is likely to be offered in April and the second round likely between May and June. Accepted applicants are notified by email, followed by a formal letter of award; candidates who are not selected are informed by email. On the Stanford page, applicants not affiliated with one of the four consortium universities are directed to send their CV, a short description of their research interests, and the site and faculty member(s) most aligned with their interests to the GHES program manager to verify eligibility before applying.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a U.S. citizen, U.S. territory/possession citizen, or U.S. permanent resident - and if you are a permanent resident, have your green card number ready for Section 2.

Count back five years from the day you complete your degree: if your doctoral or health-professional terminal degree was completed more than five years ago, you are ineligible even if you hold a master's degree from the last five years.
Confirm you can physically spend 10-12 months at an LMIC research site - this is the main requirement and there is no exception for applicants who cannot live abroad.
Line up a primary U.S. GHES mentor at Stanford, the University of Arizona, UC Berkeley or Yale, and a primary LMIC GHES mentor, before you write anything. Both letters are mandatory.
Contact the GHES program manager at your U.S. mentor's institution - they can answer questions, review the requirements with you and help you and your mentors prepare materials before the deadline.
Ask your mentors to register for and certify NIH Biographical Sketch Common Forms in SciENcv early; this is a common bottleneck.
Register an ORCID and link it to your eRA Commons profile, which is now required for the applicant biosketch.

Ask both mentors for letters on their institutional letterhead, addressed to the Global Health Emerging Scholars Fellowship Selection Committee, signed, and containing name, position, institution, email, phone and work address.
Draft the research proposal against the published GHES guidelines and have a mentor check the formatting - proposals missing information or formatted incorrectly are not reviewed.

If you are predoctoral, prepare an unofficial transcript. If you are postdoctoral, make sure your degree will be complete by 1 July of the fellowship year, or be prepared to supply proof before you can start.
If you hold other funding (for example a T32), write explicitly how your GHES proposal differs from what is already funded.
Save your Qualtrics draft - the system stores your partially completed application by your computer's IP address - and submit exactly once by 1 October 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern Time.
important_advice_for_students: Act today. The published deadline is 5:00pm Eastern Time on 1 October 2026, so there is no slack in this cycle and no published re-opening.
Do not spend time polishing a proposal before you have a U.S. mentor and an LMIC mentor - without both, the application cannot be completed.
Do not translate or upgrade your transcript unnecessarily. Only predoctoral candidates need an unofficial transcript, and no certified-translation rule is published.
Do not use an old NIH fellowship biosketch format. Since 25 January 2026 everything uses the NIH Biographical Sketch Common Form in SciENcv.
Do not submit the Qualtrics form more than once; the page explicitly says to avoid multiple applications, and drafts are saved by IP address.
Do not count on this fellowship to pay your degree fees. Tuition and fees are explicitly not an allowable expense, so if you need to fund a doctorate you need a separate award.
Do not assume you can combine GHES with a US visiting-researcher stay as an LMIC fellow; that is explicitly not the intent of the fellowship.
Do not plan to hold a job, even part-time or temporary, during the fellowship year.
Do not skip the NIH orientation - it is mandatory for all trainees and its travel is funded.

If you are an LMIC applicant, get your formal affiliation or appointment at a GHES research site sorted early, because the programme does not fund LMIC students at LMIC institutions and only applicants already affiliated with a GHES site can be considered.

No professional relationship with a GHES U.S. faculty mentor at one of the four partner universities
No primary GHES LMIC mentor, or a mentor outside the 15 collaborating LMICs
Being unable to commit 10-12 months living at the LMIC site
Research proposal that is missing required information or formatted incorrectly - stated to mean it will not be reviewed

Biosketch on the superseded fellowship format, uncertified through SciENcv, or with no ORCID linked to eRA Commons
Research activities already funded from another source, with no explanation of what GHES adds
Applying without contacting the GHES program manager, which for non-consortium-affiliated U.S. applicants is the required route to eligibility verification
Submitting more than one Qualtrics application

records.description: The UJMT LAUNCH programme is a 12-month, full-time mentored global health research training fellowship funded by the NIH Fogarty International Center and delivered by a consortium of UNC Chapel Hill, Johns Hopkins, Morehouse School of Medicine and Tulane. It places trainees at core research sites in Africa, Asia and the Americas with at least one U.S. and one international mentor. Two award types exist: a Full award (monthly stipend, research funds, health insurance plus emergency medical and evacuation insurance, and travel funds) and a Travel and Research award (the same package without the monthly stipend). Research support is capped at up to USD 10,000 for postdoctoral and up to USD 7,000 for U.S. doctoral trainees. No stipend figure is published.
records.best_fit: U.S. citizens or permanent residents at any U.S. institution, and postdoctoral researchers who are citizens of the countries where UJMT has affiliated research institutions, who hold or will complete an MD, PhD, DrPH, DVM, PharmD or equivalent by July of the academic year and can commit 12 months full time to mentored research at an LMIC site. Targeted funding is expected for proposals on HIV, mental health and neurological disorders.
records.eligibility_summary: U.S.-based trainees must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents and may come from any U.S. institution; postdoctoral researchers who are citizens of one of the countries with UJMT-affiliated research institutions are also funded; postdoctoral applicants must have completed an MD, PhD, DrPH, DVM, PharmD or equivalent by July of the academic year, and U.S. doctoral applicants must be enrolled in a graduate degree programme and able to defer studies for the fellowship.

records.notes: Two award types are published, and not every trainee receives a stipend: the Travel and research award deliberately excludes the monthly stipend, so applicants should state or check which award they are applying for. official_details.description: Since 2012, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Johns Hopkins University, Morehouse School of Medicine and Tulane University have offered mentored research training through the UJMT Fogarty Global Health Fellowship programme, funded by the Fogarty International Center within the National Institutes of Health. The consortium brings together four universities and their respective international research training sites in Africa, Asia and the Americas. Each trainee works with a team of mentors, including at least one U.S. and one international member, to monitor progress and provide on-site supervision. The programme supports projects across a wide range of research topics but expects targeted funding for proposals on HIV, mental health and neurological disorders.

Trainee research projects are supported by mentors with expertise in clinical, public health, laboratory and implementation research.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your status: a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, or - if you are abroad - a citizen of a country with a UJMT-affiliated research institution.
Confirm you will hold an MD, PhD, DrPH, DVM, PharmD or equivalent by July of the academic year, or that you are a U.S. doctoral student who can defer studies for the full 12 months.
Check whether your doctoral programme lets you defer. This is a hard eligibility condition for doctoral applicants.
Decide early whether you are applying for the Full award (with monthly stipend) or the Travel and research award (without it), and plan your finances accordingly.
Line up at least two mentors: one U.S. mentor and one international mentor who is living and working full-time at the site where you will work.
Note that you can apply from any U.S. institution, but applicants from the four consortium universities (UNC, Johns Hopkins, Morehouse, Tulane) may be given priority.
If you are a doctoral candidate, remember that candidates in later stages of training - after comprehensive examinations or after clinical rotations - are given priority.
Work through the research design with both mentors before you draft anything; the page expects this and it is also what makes the proposal credible.
Draft to the exact format: everything single-spaced, 0.5" margins, Arial 11-point.
Watch the page limits: research proposal 2 pages (references excluded from the count), budget and justification 1 page, career goals 1 page, mentorship plan 1 page.
Build the research expenses budget inside the caps: up to USD 10,000 postdoctoral, up to USD 7,000 for U.S. doctoral trainees.
Complete NIH Biosketches for yourself and both mentors, and check the formatting - the page warns that a badly formatted biosketch reflects badly on the application.
Get your U.S. and international mentors to email their letters to FGHFP@med.unc.edu directly, well before the due date.
If you are jointly funded (for example by a T32), get a letter from that programme's PI or director stating the amount and duration of the support.
If you are an international postdoctoral applicant, plan the mandatory 1-3 month U.S. attachment now, with up to three key learning objectives and courses at your U.S. host's home institution.
Have a mentor review the whole application before you submit.
important_advice_for_students: Do not assume you will receive a stipend. There are two award types and the Travel and research award deliberately has no monthly stipend.
Do not budget beyond the research caps. The USD 10,000 and USD 7,000 limits are published caps on research expenses, not targets.
Do not apply as an international doctoral candidate. Only postdoctoral international researchers are funded; the doctoral criteria are marked U.S. only.
Do not submit an application with only one mentor, or with an international mentor who is not living and working full-time at the site - the letter requirements make both non-negotiable.
Do not upload recommendation letters. Mentors email them directly to FGHFP@med.unc.edu, so you have to chase them rather than attach them.
Do not let the NIH Biosketch formatting slip. It is called out explicitly as a reputational risk.

Do not write the research proposal without your international site mentor's input on human subjects - the Human Subjects section must describe the IRB process and approval timeline, which is a local-approval question.
Do not ignore the U.S. attachment requirement for international fellows. It is a LAUNCH programme requirement, not an optional enrichment, and it has to fit inside your 12-month plan.
Do not leave the IRB question vague. Approval timelines at the site can exceed a 12-month window if not planned at proposal stage.
If you are reading this after 1 October 2026, this cohort is closed; no re-opening or next-cycle date is published, so monitor the UJMT programme page for the next annual call.

An international doctoral applicant, which is outside the published criteria
A doctoral applicant who cannot defer studies for the fellowship
Fewer than two mentors, or an international mentor who is not living and working full-time at the site
Missing the required U.S. mentor letter or the required international mentor letter
More than four recommendation letters, or a co-funding letter that does not state the amount and duration of the other support
A research proposal that misses Specific Aims, the Significance/Innovation/Approach structure, the timeline, or the Human Subjects IRB description
Exceeding the page limits - 2 pages for the proposal (references excluded), 1 page each for budget, career goals and mentorship plan
Wrong formatting - not single-spaced, not 0.5" margins, or not Arial 11-point
An improperly formatted NIH Biosketch, for the applicant or either mentor
A research budget above the USD 10,000 postdoctoral or USD 7,000 U.S. doctoral cap
Missing the Short-Term U.S.-based Training Attachment for an international applicant, or one without up to three key learning objectives and stated relevance to the project
Submitting without mentor review of the materials

document_audit: Research proposal - exactly 2 pages, single-spaced, 0.5" margins, Arial 11-point. Must contain: (1) Specific Aims; (2) Research Plan overview with Significance, Innovation and Approach; (3) Timeline for the proposed scope of work; (4) Human Subjects describing the IRB process and timeline for approval. References may be supplied and do not count toward the two pages. Confirm the page count after adding the reference list.
Budget and budget justification - 1 page, same formatting; may include personnel and travel costs; keep research expenses within USD 10,000 if postdoctoral or USD 7,000 if a U.S. doctoral trainee.
Statement of career goals - 1 page.
Plan for mentorship - 1 page, and it must specify both the areas of mentorship and the frequency of meetings or calls with the mentorship committee.
Applicant NIH Biosketch - correct NIH formatting; verify page appearance before submission.
U.S. primary mentor NIH Biosketch.
International primary mentor NIH Biosketch.
U.S. mentor letter - required; emailed by the mentor directly to FGHFP@med.unc.edu.
International mentor letter - required; from a mentor living and working full-time at the site; emailed directly to FGHFP@med.unc.edu.
Optional additional letter - one only, from a co-mentor on the application, a prior mentor, or a prior or current supervisor.
Programme co-funding letter - only if jointly supported by another training programme or grant; must outline the amount and duration of that support.

Short-Term U.S.-based Training Attachment - international applicants only: up to three key learning objectives; proposed courses with dates if known, at the U.S. host's home institution; other learning activities including workshops and conferences; and the relevance of these activities to the research project.
No published file size limits or accepted file type list; confirm the portal's limits directly before uploading.

submission_workflow: Verify your eligibility stream: U.S. citizen or permanent resident, or citizen of a country with UJMT-affiliated research institutions, and check the degree completion date against July of the academic year.
Confirm you can defer your studies for 12 months if you are a doctoral applicant, and note that later-stage doctoral candidates are prioritised.
Choose your award type - Full award with stipend, or Travel and research award without.
Select a UJMT core research site and secure a U.S. mentor plus an international mentor who is living and working full-time there.
Review the research design extensively with both mentors before drafting.

Draft the 2-page research proposal with Specific Aims, Significance/Innovation/Approach, timeline and Human Subjects including the IRB process and approval timeline; put references outside the page count.
Draft the 1-page budget and justification inside the USD 10,000 postdoctoral or USD 7,000 U.S. doctoral cap, including personnel and travel costs if needed.
Draft the 1-page statement of career goals and the 1-page mentorship plan with areas of mentorship and meeting or call frequency.
Complete and correctly format the NIH Biosketches for yourself and both primary mentors.

If you are an international postdoctoral applicant, draft the Short-Term U.S.-based Training Attachment with up to three key learning objectives, dated course proposals at your U.S. host's home institution, other workshops and conferences, and stated relevance to the project.
If you are jointly funded, obtain the co-funding programme's PI or director letter stating the amount and duration of the support.
Have a mentor review all materials.
Reformat every component to single-spaced, 0.5" margins, Arial 11-point, and verify the page limits.
Submit the application online by the October 1 due date.
Confirm that both required mentor letters have been emailed directly to FGHFP@med.unc.edu by the due date.
post_award_requirements: Take up a 12-month full-time appointment at your assigned UJMT core research site.
Work under the supervision of a mentor team including at least one U.S. and one international member, who monitor your progress.
If you are a U.S. doctoral trainee, keep your studies deferred for the duration of the fellowship.
If you are an international postdoctoral fellow, complete the required 1-3 month U.S. attachment on activities not readily available in your home country, mixing didactic and practical activities.
Obtain and document human subjects approvals through the site's IRB process as set out in your proposal.
Spend research funds only within the approved budget and within the published caps, and keep documentation for reporting.
Ensure that any co-funder continues to be able to support you concurrently - the amount and duration of the co-funding is a matter of record.

records.description: The CLP Future Conservationist Awards give early-career conservation teams a project grant of up to US$15,000 for on-the-ground conservation work, together with membership of CLP's global Alumni Network, including further funding, training and mentorship. For the 2027 cycle the process has changed: Stage 1 is a concept note submitted by email, and only the highest-scoring concept notes are invited to submit a full application through CLP's online portal. Projects must deliver effective conservation interventions for globally important, at-risk habitats and species, combining ecological research with conservation action, and must go beyond academic research. CLP funding must cover at least 50% of the total project budget, so applicants must have or secure co-funding for the remainder.
records.best_fit: Early-career conservationists (no more than five years of professional conservation experience) who are nationals of the country where the project will run, working in a team of at least three people on applied conservation work on threatened species or habitats in one of CLP's eight themes.
records.funding_period: One-off project grant (maximum per project; no periodic or annual stipend published)
records.eligibility_summary: Early-career teams of at least three people, all nationals of the project country (one non-national member permitted if clearly justified), each with no more than five years of professional conservation experience, running a 6-12 month applied conservation project in an eligible country for no more than US$15,000.
eligibility: Proposed projects must deliver effective conservation interventions for globally important, at-risk habitats and species through both ecological research and conservation action

Projects must fall within one of these themes: a) climate impact and adaptation, b) biodiversity conservation, c) habitat restoration and/or management, d) social development and wellbeing, e) Indigenous community participation and/or community-led conservation, f) environmental policy, g) human-wildlife conflict, or h) environmental education and citizen science

'At-risk' species are those categorised by the IUCN Red List as globally threatened (Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable) or Data Deficient, or where there is information indicating the need for urgent local conservation action
All team members must be early in their careers (i.e. have no more than five years of professional conservation experience)
Project teams must include at least three people and explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
All team members must be nationals of the country in which the project will take place, although one team member can be a non-national if this is clearly justified

Project duration must be between six and 12 months

records.description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. Only fieldwork costs are considered, and award holders must provide project updates and a final report that are posted on their Rufford webpage. There are no deadlines, so the programme was open on the verification date.

records.duration: Each Whitley Award is worth GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year. Winners are announced at the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
records.deadline: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are now open and will close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026.
records.application_period: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are open and close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026. Registered applicants can log in to the WFN application portal and complete the form at any time before the deadline. records.description: The Whitley Awards recognise grassroots conservation leaders who are already delivering measurable, science-based conservation impact and give each awardee GBP 50,000 of project funding over one year to scale that work up. Applicants must be nationals of the country where they work, embedded in local communities, and backed by an experienced team or organisation, and the project must deliver practical, measurable conservation action for threatened ecosystems and biodiversity at the landscape or seascape level with tangible benefits for Indigenous peoples and local communities. Applications are made directly through WFN's online portal, with no invitation or nomination needed, and include a logical framework/timeline on the current-year Word template, a budget on the current-year Excel template, and three referees who must submit their references by the deadline. records.description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation funds the position; the Foundation's own programme page states a stipend of $100,000. This is a professional work placement, not a degree-granting scholarship, so no tuition is paid.

records.selection_notes: The host's Human Resources department vets applications to draw up a shortlist of ten files, which the Foundation then reviews; a shortlist of three candidates is put to the head of the host (for the AfDB route, the President of the Bank or a designate) for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the requirements and are considered for interview are contacted.
records.notes: This is a work placement, not a degree programme: the contract is for one (1) year and is not renewable, and the Fellow is not a regular employee of the host and gains no right to employment. For the AfDB route the Fellow is barred from applying for a staff position at the Bank for one year from the end of the Fellowship. The Fellow is not eligible for the Bank's child educational scheme, staff medical insurance or retirement plans; the Mo Ibrahim Foundation is responsible for ensuring the Fellow arranges their own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan. Applications are routed through three different host systems with potentially different closing dates, so check the host page you intend to use.

One-year contract; not renewable

official_details.citizenship_residency: Nationals of an African country. AfDB route additionally requires nationality of an AfDB member country and states the candidate may reside anywhere in the world.
purpose: Identify and mentor the future generation of outstanding African leaders. The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships were established in 2011 for this purpose (Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page).

Prepare the next generation of outstanding African leaders by providing unique work opportunities at the most senior level of prominent African institutions or multilateral organizations whose mandate is to improve the economic and social prospects of Africa, thereby creating a pipeline of future African leaders (AfDB vacancy notice).
Allow talented individuals to increase and enhance their professional capacity with the intention of contributing to the governance and development of their countries (AfDB vacancy notice).

Enable young African professionals to develop leadership capacity in a large institution, gain knowledge of the functioning of the United Nations, better understand Africa's socio-economic challenges and contribute to the analytical, advocacy and policy advisory work of the Commission (UNECA 2027 Mo Ibrahim Fellowship Programme notice).
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or development-alignment requirement is published for applicants. The UNECA notice states that ECA's mission is informed by the 2030 Agenda and Agenda 2063 and lists ECA's five strategic directions (including green growth, innovative financing for infrastructure, peace and security, and gender equality), but it does not require applicants to align their proposal with, or report against, any specific SDG.
The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's own fellowships page attaches no development or SDG designation to the Fellowship.
study_type: Professional work placement / leadership fellowship in the executive office of an international institution
Research and policy design assignment, not a taught course of study
official_details.degree_award: None. The Fellowship is a 12-month funded work placement. No degree, certificate or academic credit is awarded by the Foundation or by the host organisation on any official page read.
official_details.tuition_rule: Not applicable. No tuition is charged and none is waived, because no course of study is funded. The AfDB notice states that the Foundation 'will finance the costs associated with the position' and that 'this position is not a regular position of the African Development Bank'.
covered_expenses: Annual stipend of $100,000, paid monthly by the host organisation out of funds provided by the Foundation (AfDB: 'The fellow will receive an annual stipend monthly paid by the Bank out of the funds provided by Foundation')

All expenses related to the Fellow's official mission travel, including travel insurance, borne by the host organisation but excluding assumption-of-duty and repatriation travel (AfDB and UNECA notices)
Travel and shipping costs for the assumption of duty and repatriation at the end of the appointment, borne and paid out of funds provided by the Foundation (AfDB and UNECA notices)
Invitation to the Foundation's annual Forum (UNECA notice: 'The Foundation will invite the Fellow to participate in its annual Forum')
not_covered_or_excluded: The host's child educational scheme: 'The Fellow shall not participate in the Bank's child educational scheme' (AfDB notice)

The host's staff medical insurance and retirement plans: the Fellow 'shall not participate in the Bank's staff medical insurance and retirement plans' (AfDB notice; UNECA notice states the same exclusion)

The Fellow's own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements: 'The Fellow will cover his/her own medical insurance, child education and retirement plan arrangements for the period he/she will be working at ECA' (UNECA notice); the Foundation's role is only to ensure the Fellow has such arrangements (AfDB notice)
Any tuition, course or study cost of any kind
Any remuneration, pension or employee benefit beyond the published stipend: no such entitlement is published
Housing, meals and general living costs: no official page itemises these, so they are not established as covered
general_eligibility: National of an African country (Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page). AfDB route: must be a national of an AfDB member country, residing anywhere in the world. UNECA route: must be a national of an ECA member State, residing anywhere in the world.
At least 7 years of relevant work experience (Foundation page, AfDB notice and UNECA notice all state this).

Master's degree as a minimum: the Foundation page states 'Master's degree'; the AfDB notice requires 'outstanding academic credentials backed by a minimum of a Master's Degree from a recognized institution in banking, business, economics or other social sciences, finance, international development, or in any other discipline relevant to the Bank's business'; the UNECA notice requires 'at least a Master's degree or higher in Economics, Social Sciences, International Development, Business Administration, Law, Finance, Engineering, or any discipline relevant to the work of ECA'.

Under the age of 40; 45 for women with children (Foundation page and AfDB notice). For UNECA, under 40 on the date of the application deadline (20 November 2026), with consideration given to women under 45 with children on that date.
Relevant and demonstrable work experience, strong communication skills, demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to work with others (AfDB notice).
Competency in professionalism, teamwork, client orientation, planning and organising, and leadership potential (UNECA notice).
Sound knowledge of the internet and basic software for word processing, spreadsheets and presentations (UNECA notice).
UNECA route only: fluency in either English or French, with working knowledge of the other language desirable, and the application must be in either English or French.
ineligibility_conditions: Not an active, non-active, retired or separated staff member of the African Development Bank (AfDB route)
No close family relations with an active or non-active staff member of the Bank, such as mother, father, sister and brother (AfDB route)
Government officials, active military personnel and political party leaders are not eligible (AfDB route)
Not a national of an AfDB member country (AfDB route: 'To apply for this position, you need to be national of one of AfDB member countries')
Must not be an employee of the United Nations Secretariat or ECA (UNECA route)
Aged 40 or over on the application deadline date, unless the applicant is a woman under 45 with children (UNECA route)
Applications received after 20 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. (23:59) Addis Ababa time are not reviewed, and 'no exceptions will be made' (UNECA route)
Incomplete submissions are not considered 'under any circumstances'; where several submissions are received from the same applicant only the most recent is reviewed (UNECA route)

masters: A Master's degree is the minimum academic qualification on all three host routes. AfDB: 'outstanding academic credentials backed by a minimum of a Master's Degree'. UNECA: 'at least a Master's degree or higher'. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's own page states only 'Master's degree'.

The AfDB notice additionally requires the discipline to be relevant to the Bank's business; the UNECA notice lists Economics, Social Sciences, International Development, Business Administration, Law, Finance, Engineering or any discipline relevant to the work of ECA.
phd: No separate PhD-level rule is published for the 2027 cycle. The UNECA notice requires 'at least a Master's degree or higher', so a doctorate satisfies the education minimum, but no additional academic standard is set for PhD holders and no doctoral funding is described.

host_requirements: AfDB route: the Fellow performs the functions and duties of the position at the headquarters of the Bank in Abidjan, Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, 'or in any other location from which the Bank carries out its operations'.
AfDB route: the Fellow takes leadership guidance from the President, the Managing Directors, the Chief of Staff and Director of Cabinet and/or a designated Representative.

UNECA route: duty station Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; the Fellow is mentored by the Executive Secretary of ECA and/or a designated Representative in the Office of the Executive Secretary (OES) and supports the OES programmatic and administrative functions.
ITC route: the Foundation's page quotes the ITC Executive Director describing the programme as an opportunity to work alongside the Executive Director and her team in Geneva.
The Fellow signs a contract with the host before commencing of service (AfDB and UNECA notices).

For the duration of the contract the Fellow must comply with the Staff Regulations and Rules of the host for all operational purposes and purposes of conduct, and only the host, not the Foundation, may direct and instruct the Fellow.
The Fellow may be required to travel to different locations on the host's instructions (AfDB notice).

For the AfDB route, the host's own recruitment system applies the same standards as staff recruitment, including that the Bank does not accept dual nationality and requires supporting government-issued IDs such as a passport or national identity card.
document_format_rules: UNECA route: all documents must be submitted as PDF attachments. The notice states 'any other document/attachment types will not be accepted'.
UNECA route: large documents may be combined or compressed into a .zip file if necessary. The notice states 'Please do NOT use any other file compression formats (e.g. RAR)'.
UNECA route: the application must be in either English or French.
UNECA route: all required documents must be submitted at one time and in one email; the notice states that only the most recent submission from an applicant will be reviewed.

UNECA route: the UN Administrative Profile (AP) must be generated as a PDF from the Inspira system (https://inspira.un.org) and attached to the email. The notice states that ECA does not have the ability to retrieve draft or created APs from Inspira, so an email submission without a complete AP as a PDF attachment is considered incomplete and will not be reviewed.

UNECA route: the cover/motivation letter is created inside the online AP creation process in Inspira and appears on page 1 of the AP PDF under the heading 'Cover Letter/Motivation Statement for this Application'.
UNECA route: take a screenshot showing that the online survey responses have been sent, and include it in PDF format.

UNECA route: letters of recommendation must be addressed to the '2027 ECA Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellow Selection Committee'. Referees must send the letters directly to the applicant, who then includes them in the email submission; letters transmitted directly from referees to ECA will not be considered.

UNECA route: copies of academic degree certificates for master's degrees and doctorate/terminal degrees only. The notice states that copies of academic certificates that are not degrees, and copies of high school diplomas/transcripts, are not required, and that first-level (baccalaureate) documentation is not required because a master's is the minimum.

AfDB route: the online form on the Bank's website must be completed and submitted with a comprehensive CV indicating date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience, plus copies of academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation attached.
No file size limit, accepted file type, page limit, translation rule or signature rule is published on the AfDB notice, the UNECA notice or the Foundation page. These remain unconfirmed.
official_details.selection_notes: AfDB route: the Bank's Human Resources Department carries out an initial vetting of applications to develop a short list of ten (10) applicant files to be further reviewed by the Foundation; a short list of three (3) candidates is presented to the President of the Bank or his designate for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the Bank's requirements and are considered for interview will be contacted, and the President reserves the right to appoint a candidate at a lower level. UNECA route: due to an anticipated high volume of applications only finalists are contacted and no feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants; received applications are acknowledged within one week; an update is posted to the ECA fellowship page once selection concludes. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation page does not publish a selection method of its own beyond routing applicants to the hosts.
application_steps: Choose the host organisation route from the links published on the Mo Ibrahim Foundation fellowships page: African Development Bank (Abidjan), International Trade Centre (Geneva) or UNECA (Addis Ababa).

AfDB route: go to the vacancy page for the 2027 Mo Ibrahim Foundation Leadership Fellowship Program and complete the online application form on the Bank's recruitment system (external candidates apply at https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/).
AfDB route: prepare a comprehensive CV that states date of birth, nationality, education and relevant experience, and attach copies of academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation.

UNECA route: create an account on the UN Inspira system (https://inspira.un.org), then build a draft Administrative Profile with no linked Job Opening and generate it as a PDF; the cover/motivation letter is created as part of that process and appears on page 1.
UNECA route: complete the required online survey and take a screenshot showing the responses were sent, in PDF format.
UNECA route: obtain three letters of recommendation addressed to the '2027 ECA Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellow Selection Committee'; referees send them to the applicant, not to ECA.

UNECA route: email all documents in one message as PDF attachments to RecruitmentPPost@un.org with the subject line 'ECA 2027 Mo Ibrahim Leadership Fellowship (Applicant Last Name, First Name)'; the AP PDF, degree certificate copies, the three recommendation letters and the survey screenshot must all be in that single email.
ITC route: apply through the ITC vacancy published on the UN Careers system.
Submit before the closing date on the host's own timeline; AfDB closes 20 November 2026 and UNECA closes 20 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Addis Ababa time.
Save the submission confirmation. Received applications will be acknowledged within one week on the UNECA route.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits the application directly. There is no nomination by a university, ministry or employer on any of the three routes.
AfDB route: online application form on the Bank's website, submitted through the Bank's own recruitment portal (https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/ for external candidates).
UNECA route: email submission to RecruitmentPPost@un.org. The notice is explicit that the applicant, not the referee and not the institution, sends the complete package.
ITC route: application through the ITC vacancy published on the UN Careers system (https://careers.un.org/jobSearchDescription/285022?language=en).
official_details.application_portal: AfDB route: https://www.afdb.org/en/vacancy/2027-mo-ibrahim-foundation-leadership-fellowship-program-96407, with external candidates applying at https://afdb.jobs2web.com/job-invite/2343/. UNECA route: no portal — applications are emailed to RecruitmentPPost@un.org, with the Administrative Profile PDF generated from https://inspira.un.org. ITC route: https://careers.un.org/jobSearchDescription/285022?language=en.
arrival_rules: The travel and shipping costs for the assumption of duty are borne and paid out of funds provided by the Foundation (AfDB and UNECA notices).
AfDB duty station: headquarters of the Bank in Abidjan, Republic of Côte d'Ivoire, or any other location from which the Bank carries out its operations.
UNECA duty station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
ITC duty station: Geneva.
